the unsubscribe url is a state-mutating, token-less get with toggle semantics (watching/tracking to regular, regular/muted to muted): corporate mail scanners and link unfurlers (mimecast/proofpoint-style) prefetch the url and each fetch flips the level, so a scanner pass can downgrade watching to regular and a second fetch (or scanner plus user click) fully mutes the topic with zero user action; re-clicking an old link after re-watching downgrades again, and concurrent gets race so one toggle is lost. needs a confirmation step, post, or per-user token.

the end state contradicts what the email and confirmation page promise: the email footer says 'to stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here' and the page unconditionally renders 'you will stop receiving notifications for <title>', but for watching/tracking users (the majority of recipients) the code sets regular, which still sends notifications for replies, mentions and quotes; only users already at regular/muted end up muted. should either go straight to muted or render the message from the actual resulting level.

the unsubscribelink locale now hard-requires %{unsubscribeurl} for every opting-in mailer: email::messagebuilderhtmlpart renders i18n.t('unsubscribelink', templateargs) for any email built with addunsubscribelink: true, and i18n raises missinginterpolationargument when the key is absent, so any other caller (e.g. digest mailer or plugins) that doesn't supply unsubscribeurl now fails to build/send the email. all addunsubscribelink callers need auditing.

tu.save! bypasses topicuser.change, so no messagebus notificationlevelchange message is published to /topic/<id>: every other path that changes notificationlevel publishes it, meaning a tab that already has the topic open keeps showing the stale watching/tracking state (button and reason text) until a manual refresh, and the codebase now has two divergent write paths for the same state. using topicuser.change fixes this and the missing-row case together.

state-changing get on an email-embedded url: notificationlevel is mutated on a plain get (app/controllers/topicscontroller.rb:98-115) with no confirmation step or csrf token, making it csrf-able against logged-in users via to silently mute topics, and exposing it to email scanner/prefetcher probe traffic on the site's highest-volume mail class

the new unsubscribe route (topicsunsubscribe) permanently mutates topicuser.notificationlevel via a plain get request authenticated only by the session cookie — no per-user token, no confirmation step, exempt from rails csrf protection, and with checkxhr explicitly skipped — so any external site can embed and silently change the notification level of every logged-in visitor
email link scanners and av gateways that prefetch get urls will trigger the unsubscribe mutation for users who merely opened the email without clicking the link

the unsubscribe action is a toggle rather than an idempotent unsubscribe: a page refresh or second fetch escalates regular → muted, so the user's final state depends on how many times the link was fetched

topicuser.findby result is dereferenced without a nil check (tu.notificationlevel immediately after findby), raising nomethoderror and returning a 500 when the logged-in user has no topicuser row (e.g., forwarded email, shared browser, different account) — the controller also bypasses topicuser.change, which is the method that creates the row if missing and publishes the notificationlevelchange messagebus event that open tabs rely on

the shared unsubscribelink locale key / email::messagebuilder contract was changed to interpolate %{unsubscribeurl}, but templateargs only contains unsubscribeurl if the caller passes it — any mail built with addunsubscribelink: true + htmloverride without the new opt now raises i18n::missinginterpolationargument at build time and fails to send entirely; the pr updates only one caller with no guard or fallback for other core/plugin mailers using this public builder option

the unsubscribe copy overpromises: the action only drops watching/tracking users to regular, a level that still notifies and emails the user on replies and mentions, so users who click 'stop receiving notifications' keep receiving notifications for that topic — only a second fetch reaches muted
direct tu.save! bypasses topicuser.change, so there is no upsert and no notificationlevelchange messagebus publish, leaving other open tabs of the topic out of sync

the beforefilter configuration for :unsubscribe needs verification: if it is in an except: list rather than ensureloggedin ... only:, currentuser is nil for anonymous clicks and every logged-out click 500s at currentuser.id

the unsubscribe email link is a state-changing get with no token or confirmation that permanently mutates notificationlevel; mail-gateway link scanners/prefetchers and cross-site embedding (e.g., with no samesite cookies) can silently mute a user's topic, and revisiting the url keeps stepping the level down (watching → regular → muted)

the unsubscribe step-down logic maps watching/tracking to regular, which still emails the user when replied to/mentioned/quoted in that topic, contradicting the email and landing page text claiming they will stop receiving notifications; watching users must click twice to actually stop notifications

the client route topic-unsubscribe.js.es6 shows unconditional success text ('you will stop receiving notifications for title') even though no server mutation occurs when the url is reached via client-side navigation; the success text should be conditioned on the actual details.notificationlevel

the per-topic unsubscribe link interpolated into emails is site-relative: topicurl returns a relative path and nothing absolutizes the new unsubscribeurl key (unlike userpreferencesurl, which messagebuilder absolutizes), so the mailer likely interpolates '/t/slug/99/unsubscribe' into the email cta — an anchor that cannot resolve in a mail client, leaving the feature's primary cta dead.

the unsubscribe behavior contradicts the email/page copy: watching/tracking users are only stepped down to regular, which still sends notifications on replies/mentions, despite the copy saying 'you will stop receiving notifications' — and no test encodes the intended level-transition matrix that would have forced a decision on intended behavior.
the unsubscribe get endpoint is non-idempotent: each repeat get of the same url mutates state again, stepping watching → regular → muted across refreshes or repeat clicks.

the unsubscribe action hand-rolls mutation (findby + attribute assignment + save!) instead of using the canonical topicuser.change api, duplicating logic, skipping the messagebus publish so other open tabs never learn the level changed, embedding toggle business logic in the controller, and converting validation failures into 500s

eventmanager.ts:337 — createallcalendarevents now uses a sequential for...of with awaited createevent plus a per-destination prisma.credential.findunique, making booking latency scale linearly with host count instead of using promise.all

eventmanager.ts:596 — console.error(message) was removed from the updateallcalendarevents catch block, so failure reasons are no longer logged and callers only see synthesized success: false results with appname "none"

[medium/bug] src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:408 — assignmentsource is added to syncstatusoutbound, but status task/callers do not propagate it into shouldsync, so status syncs can echo back to their originating integration.

[bug] eventmanager's create path dereferences mainhostdestinationcalendar.integration with no null guard, so it throws a typeerror whenever evt.destinationcalendar is null or an empty array and the event location is google meet. booking creation and confirmation 500 with 'cannot read properties of undefined (reading integration)' for users with no destinationcalendar — handlenewbooking sets destinationcalendar to null when neither eventtype nor organizer has one, and confirm.handler passes [] — which is precisely the meet-selected-without-google-calendar case this fallback line exists to handle; the old optional-chained comparison fell back to cal video instead of crashing.

[bug] updateevent's fallback predicate event.destinationcalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalid === externalcalendarid)?.externalid only executes when externalcalendarid is falsy, so it compares every calendar's externalid against null/undefined and can never match, leaving selectedcalendar undefined where the old code returned destinationcalendar.externalid. rescheduling a booking whose calendar reference carries no externalcalendarid — which includes every booking created through eventmanager's no-credentialid path, since that path now stores result.externalid (undefined) on the reference — calls calendar.events.update with calendarid undefined, googleapis throws missing required parameter, and the google event is never updated.

[bug] deleteevent's fallback event.destinationcalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalid === externalcalendarid)?.externalid is evaluated only in the branch where externalcalendarid is falsy, so the predicate can never match a real calendar and calendarid is always undefined in that branch. cancelling a booking whose reference lacks externalcalendarid invokes calendar.events.delete with calendarid undefined, which googleapis rejects, so the google event is orphaned on the host's calendar after the cal.com booking is gone.

[bug] the db fallback assigns the raw prisma.credential.findunique result — fetched without the app relation, hence with no appname — into calendarcredential and hands it to getcalendar, which resolves the integration from credential.appname. getcalendar returns null for the appname-less credential, so calendar?.deleteevent(...) is a silent no-op: cancelling the collective bookings this pr targets, whose reference credentialid belongs to a teammate or team rather than bookingtodelete.user, leaves the event live on that calendar with no error surfaced.

[bug] createevent now selects the target calendar solely via destinationcalendar.find((cal) => cal.credentialid === credentialid), so a destination calendar without a credentialid — the case eventmanager's else-branch exists to serve — never matches and the event is written to 'primary' instead of the destination's configured externalid. bookings against a credentialid-less destination calendar now land in each connected google credential's primary calendar (duplicating the event once per credential) instead of the user's selected calendar, and the stored reference ends up with a wrong or missing externalcalendarid that later reschedule/cancel paths depend on.

[bug] office365calendarservice.createevent builds eventsurl from the first destination calendar's externalid no matter which host's credential is invoking it, so the per-destination creation loop this pr adds still targets the first host's calendar for every host. for a collective booking with multiple office365 hosts, the secondary host's creation posts to /me/calendars/{first host's calendar id}/events under the second host's token, microsoft graph returns 404, and the secondary host's calendar never receives the event — the multi-host fix only works for google.

[bug] larkcalendarservice.createevent resolves calendarid from the first destination calendar only, ignoring which destination and credential the eventmanager loop is currently processing. for collective bookings with multiple lark hosts, the secondary host's createevent calls the lark api with the first host's calendar id under the wrong credential, the call errors, and that host's calendar never gets the event — the pr's multi-host handling is unimplemented for lark.

[advisory] the recurring-series deletion sweep over all user calendar credentials and all updatedbookings now runs once per calendar reference, and inside the sweep each updated booking is still handled via references.find, i.e. only its first calendar reference. cancelling a multi-reference recurring collective booking issues references x credentials duplicate delete calls — every attempt after the first fails and is logged — while the remaining bookings' secondary calendar references are never deleted, orphaning events on teammates' calendars.

[advisory] the reschedule-merge path still deletes only booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes('calendar')) — a single reference — even though this same diff makes bookings carry multiple calendar references. rescheduling a collective booking that has calendar references on several hosts deletes only the first host's old event and leaves orphaned events on every other host's calendar.

[advisory] evt.destinationcalendar is set to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, and the subsequent evt.destinationcalendar?.push(...teamdestinationcalendars) then silently skips, dropping every teammate's calendar. a collective booking whose organizer has no destinationcalendar proceeds without any of the teammates' destination calendars and without any error, so no teammate calendar receives the event — the multi-host behavior this pr introduces no-ops for exactly that configuration.

[advisory] loadusers' new catch maps prisma.prismaclientknownrequesterror to httperror 400, rethrowing server-side database failures as client errors with the raw prisma message. a prisma known-request error during user loading (e.g. a p2024 connection-pool timeout) reaches booking clients as 400 bad request carrying the raw database error text, so clients treat a transient server fault as a permanent request error and internal db details leak into the response.

[advisory] createevent takes the organizer email from the first destination calendar while selecting the target calendar by credentialid, so the event written to a secondary host's calendar carries the first host's externalid as its organizer email. every multi-host collective booking produces events on secondary hosts' calendars whose organizer is misattributed to the first host's calendar id, misowning the very events this pr adds.

[bug] updateevent's fallback event.destinationcalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalid === externalcalendarid)?.externalid only executes when externalcalendarid is falsy, so the predicate compares externalid against a falsy value, never matches, and selectedcalendar is always undefined where the old code returned event.destinationcalendar.externalid. rescheduling any booking whose calendar reference lacks externalcalendarid (legacy bookings, plus new bookings created via the credentialid-less destination branch which this diff now stores as undefined) calls calendar.events.update with calendarid undefined — the google call fails and the event silently stays at the old time with only a log line.

[bug] deleteevent's fallback event.destinationcalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalid === externalcalendarid)?.externalid only executes when externalcalendarid is falsy, so the find never matches and calendarid resolves to undefined where the old code fell back to event.destinationcalendar.externalid. cancelling a booking whose reference lacks externalcalendarid calls calendar.events.delete with calendarid undefined — the google event is never removed and remains as an orphan on the host's calendar after the booking is cancelled in cal.com.

[bug] office365calendarservice.createevent builds the events url from destinationcalendar[0].externalid regardless of which host's credential is creating the event, ignoring the per-credential destination selection that the array migration requires. for a collective booking with multiple hosts, every non-first host's event is posted to /me/calendars/{first host's externalid}/events using the non-first host's token — graph returns 404, createevent fails, and that host's calendar never receives the booking while the booking itself succeeds, i.e. the pr's titular feature is dropped for office 365.

[bug] larkcalendarservice.createevent (and createattendees at ~line 164) resolve calendarid from destinationcalendar[0] only, so the event for any non-first host is created against the first host's calendar id using the wrong host's credential. for multi-host collective bookings on lark, the non-first hosts' createevent calls target a calendar id that does not exist under their credential — the lark api errors and those hosts never get the event, silently, since calendarmanager only logs the failure.

[bug] the booking row persists only evt.destinationcalendar[0] via connect: { id: evt.destinationcalendar[0].id }, so the multi-host destination set survives nowhere in the db and every flow that rebuilds a calendarevent from booking.destinationcalendar collapses a collective booking back to host 1. deferred-creation flows rebuild their evt from booking.destinationcalendar — confirm.handler (collective bookings with requiresconfirmation) and the stripe/paypal handlepaymentsuccess webhooks (paid collective bookings) then call eventmanager.create with only the first host's destination, so those collective bookings get a calendar event on host 1's calendar only and never on the other hosts' calendars.

[bug] evt.destinationcalendar is initialized to null (not []) when neither eventtype nor organizer has a destination calendar, making the subsequent evt.destinationcalendar?.push(...teamdestinationcalendars) a no-op that silently discards every teammate's collected destination calendar. a collective booking whose organizer has no destination calendar drops all teammates' destinationcalendars — their configured destination calendars are ignored and their events land on default calendars via the create-on-all-credentials branch instead of the calendars they configured.

[bug] basecalendarservice.createevent filters the credential's calendars down to those matching destinationcalendar[0].externalid, so when eventmanager creates the event on a non-first host's caldav credential the filter matches nothing. for multi-host collective bookings on caldav, the filter yields an empty calendar list for every non-first host, promise.all resolves with zero responses and no event is created on that host's calendar — the fan-out requirement is silently dropped for caldav.

[bug] the credentialid-less destination branch calls createevent(c, event) without destination.externalid (line ~377) while the reference writer now stores externalcalendarid: result.externalid, which is undefined on that branch — the old code stored evt.destinationcalendar.externalid. bookings created through the credentialid-less destination branch get calendar references with externalcalendarid undefined, so their later update/delete falls into the googlecalendarservice fallback that this same diff broke (undefined calendarid) — those google events can never be moved or cancelled.

[bug] the recurring-event delete sweep (bookingtodelete.user.credentials.filter(...endswith("calendar")).map(...) over updatedbookings) now sits inside the per-reference loop without being made reference-aware, so it executes once per calendar reference and still deletes only the first calendar reference of each remaining series booking. cancelling a recurring collective booking with n calendar references runs the sweep n times (duplicate deleteevent calls whose failures are swallowed by the surrounding catch) and never touches the non-first hosts' events for the remaining series bookings — those hosts' calendars keep orphaned events.

[advisory] update() was converted to process every calendar reference via filter, but the newbookingid merge path still uses booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("calendar")) to pick a single old reference to delete. when a booking with multiple calendar references (any post-pr collective booking) goes through the newbookingid merge path, only the first old calendar event is deleted and hosts 2..n's old events remain as orphans at the old time.

[bug] updateevent's fallback branch computes event.destinationcalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalid === externalcalendarid) at the exact point where externalcalendarid is falsy, so the find can never match and the fallback always yields undefined. rescheduling any booking whose calendar reference lacks externalcalendarid (legacy pre-refactor references, and the othercalendar path that passes bookingexternalcalendarid ?? null) now sends calendarid: undefined to the google api and the update fails, where the old event.destinationcalendar?.externalid fallback updated the correct destination calendar.

[bug] deleteevent's fallback searches for a calendar whose externalid equals the already-falsy externalcalendarid, making the event.destinationcalendar?.find(...) fallback provably dead code that always returns undefined. cancelling bookings whose reference carries no externalcalendarid now calls google's events.delete with an undefined calendarid, so the event is never removed from the destination calendar and remains orphaned, where the old event.destinationcalendar?.externalid fallback deleted it.

[bug] evt.destinationcalendar is initialized to null when both eventtype.destinationcalendar and organizeruser.destinationcalendar are absent, and the collective team calendars are then appended via evt.destinationcalendar?.push(...), which no-ops on null. for a collective event whose organizer never configured a destination calendar, every teammate's destinationcalendar collected in teamdestinationcalendars is silently discarded and the booking is written only to the organizer's default calendars — the exact multi-host case this pr claims to handle.

[bug] createevent now selects the target calendar solely via destinationcalendar.find((cal) => cal.credentialid === credentialid) with a || "primary" fallback, so a destination calendar whose credentialid is null never matches any credential. users whose destinationcalendar row has no credentialid — a state the old eventmanager explicitly branched for and the old code served via externalid — get every event created on their google primary calendar instead of the configured destination calendar.

[bug] larkcalendarservice.createevent resolves the target calendar from event.destinationcalendar[0] regardless of which destination/credential eventmanager.createallcalendarevents invoked it for, ignoring the credentialid parameter the new calendar interface added for exactly this purpose. for a collective multi-host booking with a lark destination that is not first in the array, the per-destination create call sends the first host's calendar externalid with the wrong host's token, the lark api call fails, and the teammate's calendar never receives the event — the multi-host fix only actually works on google.

[bug] office365calendarservice.createevent builds the events url from destinationcalendar[0].externalid only, ignoring which destination the eventmanager loop is currently processing. collective multi-host bookings route every per-destination create call to the first host's office365 calendar path (failing with the other hosts' tokens), so teammates' office365 calendars never receive the collective event.

[bug] basecalendarservice.createevent filters caldav calendars to mainhostdestinationcalendar.externalid (the first array element) only, so per-destination invocations from eventmanager.createallcalendarevents can never select any other host's calendar. collective multi-host bookings with apple/caldav destinations create the event only on the first host's calendar (or on none when the filter matches nothing for the invoked credential), silently skipping the remaining hosts' calendars.

[advisory] the new per-reference loop re-runs the recurring-cancellation block (all user credentials × all updatedbookings) once for every calendar reference, even though that block ignores the current reference entirely. cancelling a recurring collective booking with n calendar references issues n× duplicate deleteevent calls for the same events, pushing redundant failing (404) api responses into apideletes and logging spurious errors during cancellation.

[bug] updateevent's fallback branch searches event.destinationcalendar for an entry whose externalid equals externalcalendarid, but that branch only executes when externalcalendarid is falsy, so the find() can never match and selectedcalendar is always undefined. updating a booking whose calendar reference has no externalcalendarid (pre-refactor bookings, or references created through the no-credentialid destination path) sends calendarid: undefined to the google api and the update fails, where the old code fell back to event.destinationcalendar.externalid and succeeded.

[bug] deleteevent computes its fallback by finding a destination calendar whose externalid equals the already-falsy externalcalendarid, which never matches, so the fallback is always undefined and the delete falls through to defaultcalendarid 'primary'. cancelling a booking whose reference lacks externalcalendarid now targets the credential's primary calendar instead of the destination calendar where the event actually lives, so the real event is left orphaned while the delete 404s or removes the wrong event.

[bug] the slug spread condition was inverted from !isteambillingenabled to isteambillingenabled while the requestedslug metadata condition was left unchanged, flipping which deployments assign a slug at organization creation. with team billing enabled, organizations are created with slug set immediately, bypassing the requestedslug approval flow the metadata still records; with team billing disabled, organizations are created with no slug at all and are unreachable at their org url.

[bug] larkcalendarservice.createevent (and createattendees at line 163) ignores the credentialid argument and always uses destinationcalendar[0].externalid as the calendarid, so every host's credential targets the first host's lark calendar. for a collective booking with multiple lark hosts, each secondary host's createevent runs with their own token against the first host's calendarid and fails, so those hosts' calendars never receive the event — the multi-host fix only works on google.

[bug] office365calendarservice.createevent builds eventsurl from destinationcalendar[0].externalid regardless of which host's credential is performing the insert. for multi-host collective bookings, each secondary host's credential requests /me/calendars/{first-hosts-calendar}/events with its own token and gets a 404, so those hosts' calendars never receive the booking.

[bug] only evt.destinationcalendar[0] is connected to the booking's single destinationcalendar relation, so the additional collective hosts' destination calendars pushed into the array are never persisted anywhere. deferred-creation flows rebuild calendarevent from the persisted booking — confirm.handler.ts and the stripe/paypal payment-success webhooks wrap booking.destinationcalendar in a one-element array — so confirming or taking payment on a multi-host collective booking creates calendar events on only the first host's calendar and hosts 2..n never receive them.

[bug] createevent resolves the target calendar solely by matching destinationcalendar entries' credentialid against the passed credentialid and otherwise falls back to 'primary', so a destination calendar with a null credentialid — the case eventmanager.createallcalendarevents explicitly supports through its integration-filter branch — never matches. bookings whose destination calendar has no credentialid get their google event created on the credential's primary calendar instead of the selected destination calendar, while calendarmanager still echoes destination.externalid into the booking reference, so later updates and deletes target a calendar the event was never created in and 404.

[bug] the booking-reference mapping now takes externalcalendarid from result.externalid, but calendarmanager.createevent only sets that field when eventmanager passed destination.externalid as the third argument, and the no-credentialid branch calls createevent(c, event) without it. calendar references created through the destination-without-credentialid path persist externalcalendarid: undefined where the old code recorded evt.destinationcalendar.externalid, so later updates and deletes lose their calendar routing and fall into google's undefined/'primary' fallbacks.

[bug] for non-calendar (video) results the reference mapping now writes credentialid: undefined where the old code wrote result.credentialid, while the sibling mapping at line 209 keeps result.credentialid. video-call booking references are persisted without the credential that created the meeting, so any flow resolving the conferencing credential from the booking reference gets undefined; the inconsistency with the sibling mapping shows the drop is unintentional.

[bug] the recurring-series cancellation sweep takes only the first calendar reference of each remaining booking via references.find, although multi-host collective bookings now carry one calendar reference per host. cancelling a recurring collective booking deletes the series event from only the first host's calendar; the other hosts' series events survive as ghost events at the old times.

[bug] the recurring deletion sweep over all user calendar credentials x all remaining bookings now sits inside the loop over every calendar reference of the cancelled booking, so it executes once per reference. cancelling an r-host collective recurring booking issues roughly r x credentials x remaining-bookings delete calls: the first sweep does the work and every additional sweep re-deletes the same event uids, producing duplicate 404 failures logged as errors on each cancellation.

[bug] the merge path still deletes only the first calendar reference of the old booking via references.find, while the rest of update was rewritten to process every calendar reference. when a reschedule merges bookings (the newbookingid path) for a multi-host collective booking, the old event is deleted from only the first host's calendar and the other hosts' old events are orphaned at the previous time.

[advisory] when a destination's credentialid resolves to neither an in-memory credential nor a db credential with an app slug, the destination is skipped with no event created and nothing logged. a collective host whose credential was deleted or has no app row silently gets no calendar event for the booking; organizers discover the miss only when the host misses the meeting.

[advisory] createevent sets the google event's organizer email from destinationcalendar[0].externalid even when the credential-matched selectedcalendar is a different host's calendar. events inserted into secondary hosts' calendars carry the first host's calendar id as organizer email, misattributing the organizer on every non-first host's event and confusing organizer-based edit rights in google.

[advisory] updateevent sets organizer email from destinationcalendar[0].externalid regardless of which host's calendar the update targets via externalcalendarid. every reschedule of a multi-host collective booking rewrites the organizer on secondary hosts' events to the first host's calendar id.

[bug] the google meet fallback reads mainhostdestinationcalendar.integration off the destructured first element with no null guard, so it throws a typeerror whenever evt.destinationcalendar is null or an empty array. a booking or confirmation with location integrations:google:meet by a user with no destination calendar (handlenewbooking builds destinationcalendar: null at line 1067; confirm.handler builds []) crashes eventmanager.create with 'cannot read properties of undefined (reading integration)', returning a 500 and failing the booking, where the old optional-chained code fell back to cal video.

[bug] updateevent's fallback branch searches destinationcalendar for an entry whose externalid equals the already-falsy externalcalendarid, a predicate that can never match, so selectedcalendar is always undefined in that branch. rescheduling any booking whose calendar reference lacks externalcalendarid (legacy destination calendars without credentialid, pre-refactor references) now sends calendarid: undefined to the google api instead of the old destinationcalendar.externalid fallback, so the event is never updated and the old time slot stays booked on the host's calendar.

[bug] deleteevent's fallback branch uses the same self-referential predicate find((cal) => cal.externalid === externalcalendarid) inside the branch where externalcalendarid is falsy, which never matches and always yields undefined. cancelling any booking whose calendar reference has no externalcalendarid but whose destinationcalendar is populated now passes calendarid: undefined to calendar.events.delete, so the event is silently left on the host's google calendar after cancellation.

[bug] the rewrite of the organization slug spread inverts its condition: ...(!isteambillingenabled && { slug }) became ...(isteambillingenabled ? { slug } : {}), an unrelated silent objective change smuggled into a destinationcalendar pr. with team billing enabled, organizations now get slug set immediately, bypassing the requestedslug/isorganizationverified review flow (and writing both slug and requestedslug); with billing disabled (self-hosted), organizations are created with no slug at all, breaking org routing. neither behavior matches the accepted pre-pr semantics.

[bug] createevent selects the calendar via find((cal) => cal.credentialid === credentialid), which never matches destinations whose credentialid is null, so selectedcalendar falls back to 'primary'. bookings from users whose destinationcalendar rows have null credentialid (the legacy branch eventmanager still explicitly supports at line 347) now create the event on the account's primary calendar instead of the configured destination calendar, and because eventmanager's legacy branch calls createevent(c, event) without externalid, the stored reference also has no externalcalendarid, so later updates/deletes cannot locate the event at all.

[bug] larkcalendarservice.createevent ignores the new credentialid parameter and always uses the first destination calendar's externalid as calendarid (createattendees at line 164 repeats this). for a collective event with two lark hosts, the second host's createevent call sends the first host's calendarid with the second host's token, lark rejects it, calendarmanager's catch swallows the error, and the second host's calendar never receives the event while the booking still succeeds.

[bug] office365calendarservice.createevent builds eventsurl from the first destination calendar's externalid, ignoring which host's credential is performing the insert. for a collective event with multiple office 365 hosts, the second host's call hits /me/calendars/{firsthostexternalid}/events with the second host's token, microsoft returns 404, and that host's calendar never gets the event even though the pr's purpose is to add it.

[bug] basecalendarservice.createevent filters the credential's calendar list by the first destination calendar's externalid, so for any host other than the first the filter matches nothing. for a collective event with multiple caldav/apple hosts, the second host's createevent call filters that host's own calendars by the first host's externalid, matches zero calendars, and creates the event nowhere, so the host silently has no calendar event for a confirmed booking.

[bug] eventmanager.create now writes credentialid: undefined for video-type booking references, where it previously stored result.credentialid. bookings that use a dedicated video integration no longer record which credential created the meeting, so flows that resolve the video credential from the booking reference (e.g., reusing the same zoom credential when rescheduling) find none and fall back to a default credential, creating the rescheduled meeting under the wrong integration account.

[advisory] createevent sets organizer.email from the first destination calendar's externalid for every host's insert, not from the destination matching the credentialid actually being used. on the second and later hosts' google calendars, the inserted payload names the first host's calendar id as organizer; attendees viewing the event on those calendars see a wrong (and often non-email) organizer value, and the payload is factually incorrect for every host except the first.

[bug] handlenewbooking builds evt.destinationcalendar as null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, then gates the member-calendar merge on evt.destinationcalendar?.push, which no-ops on null. a collective booking whose organizer has no destination calendar silently drops every team member's destination calendar collected in teamdestinationcalendars, so members' calendars never receive the event — defeating the pr's own objective for exactly this organizer shape.

[advisory] the only enforcement of the maxsegmentspans limit was deleted, leaving the constructor/config option dead while the effective cap is a hardcoded 1000 inside the lua script. operators tuning maxsegmentspans get no effect — raising it to allow larger segments still loses spans at the hardcoded 1000, and lowering it to protect flusher memory no longer skips anything — and the two limits silently diverge because the lua cap is not derived from the config.

[bug] the enableadvancedfeatures branch slices the queryset with a negative start offset, which django's queryset.getitem rejects with assertionerror("negative indexing is not supported"), so the comment's claim that the orm handles negative slicing automatically is false and the branch can never return results. a crafted cursor with a negative offset (client-supplied and parsed by cursor.init via int(offset) with no clamp) plus optimizedpagination=true from a superuser produces an assertionerror and a 500 instead of a page — the advertised negative-offset feature is dead code that only ever crashes.

[bug] optimizedcursorpaginator subclasses basepaginator while copying cursorpaginator's numeric getitemkey, but the endpoint's paginate call passes no key= so the cursorpaginator constructor state (self.key/self.desc) is never set — and even if key were derived from orderby="-datetime", math.floor/math.ceil on an auditlogentry.datetime (a datetime, not a number) raises typeerror. get /api/0/organizations/<slug>/auditlogs/?optimizedpagination=true returns an unhandled attributeerror/typeerror 500 for every request that has any rows, so the new paginator can never serve the endpoint it was added for.

[bug] the enableadvancedfeatures negative-offset branch evaluates queryset[startoffset:stop] with startoffset = cursor.offset < 0, which django's queryset.getitem rejects with assertionerror ('negative indexes are not allowed') — the comment claiming the orm 'properly handles negative slicing automatically' is false. every request that actually exercises the advertised negative-offset feature (admin with optimizedpagination=true plus a cursor carrying a negative offset) gets an unhandled 500; the branch can never return results.

[bug] zunionstore is invoked without an aggregate option, so its default sum doubles the endtimestampprecise score of any payload present in both source sets — which occurs whenever kafka redelivers a span whose parent set was already merged into the target set. redelivered spans get scores of 2x their timestamp, so zpopmin evicts in the wrong order — stale duplicate-delivered spans survive while genuinely newer spans are dropped — silently corrupting which spans a segment keeps.

[bug] the migration from redis sets (sadd/scard/sunionstore/sscan) to sorted sets (zadd/zcard/zunionstore/zscan) is applied in-place with no expand/dual-write phase, so old-code and new-code processes cannot coexist against the same keys during a rolling deploy. during the deploy window, segments written by old pods via sadd exist as plain sets; any new pod executing this lua script calls redis.call("zcard", spankey) on a set key, which raises redis wrongtype, aborting the script and leaving redirect state half-written. likewise new pods' zunionstore into a destination that old pods subsequently sunionstore, and flusher pods calling zscan on a set, all fail: buffered segments become unflushable and their spans expire via settimeout ttl, silently losing data. the only safe path is a versioned key scheme or a dual-compatible read (type check), neither of which exists.

[bug] loadsegmentdata switches sscan to zscan with no compatibility handling, so it hard-fails on any segment key still holding set-typed data written by old-version producers. during rolling deploy (or on any leftover key from before the deploy), zscan on a set key returns a redis wrongtype error, which crashes the flusher's pipeline execute and prevents all segments from being flushed in that batch, not just the stale-typed one; affected spans hit the key ttl and are dropped. there is no migration/backfill step converting existing sadd-populated keys to sorted sets.

[bug] the zpopmin-based eviction silently deletes buffered span payloads whenever a segment exceeds 1000 spans, with no logging, no dead-letter, and no protection for the root/segment span. a trace with >1000 buffered spans has its oldest payloads irrecoverably destroyed in redis (no backup/export step), producing partial or broken segment trees on flush — the dropped members can include the root span payload whose parent linkage other spans depend on, so the entire segment is discarded downstream. silent, irreversible data loss with no operator-visible signal.

[bug] processbatch reads val["endtimestampprecise"] as a required key, so any message lacking the field (review-base schema versions of ingestspansv1, or messages produced by pre-deploy producers) raises keyerror and crashes the consumer. during the rolling deploy, kafka partitions still contain messages serialized under the old schema without endtimestampprecise; the process consumer hits keyerror, enters a retry/backoff loop and stalls span ingestion across the partition until every old message passes or is skipped. using val.get("endtimestampprecise", fallback to val["endtimestamp"]) would keep old and new messages compatible.

[bug] the optimizedcursorpaginator's negative-offset branch slices a django queryset with a negative start index (results = list(queryset[startoffset:stop]) with startoffset < 0), which django raises assertionerror('negative indices are not allowed on querysets') for, crashing the request. any admin request with optimizedpagination=true and a cursor carrying a negative offset returns a 500 from the organization audit logs endpoint instead of a page of results; the comment claiming 'the underlying django orm properly handles negative slicing automatically' is false for orm querysets.

[bug] the script switches scard/sadd/sunionstore (set type) to zcard/zunionstore (zset type) on the same span-buf:s:... keys, but existing keys written as plain sets by the pre-deploy code (or by the still-deployed old writer during a rolling deploy) cause every z command to fail with wrongtype. during the deploy window (keys live for settimeout), any buffered segment whose set key was created by the old sadd path makes the lua script error out, so processspans' pipeline fails and the span batch is not buffered — spans silently fail to enter the segment buffer with only a redis error to show for it.

[bug] processspans now issues zadd on setkey, which raises wrongtype for any pre-existing key created by the old code path (or by an un-upgraded instance in the rolling deploy) as a set. any segment key that currently holds a set (written via the previous p.sadd) makes the pipeline execute fail on the first zadd, so the whole batch of spans for that trace fails to buffer and the consumer errors instead of migrating or branching on key type.

[bug] processbatch reads val["endtimestampprecise"] as a required key with no .get() fallback, so messages produced before the field existed (or by lagging producers during the rolling deploy) raise keyerror. the kafka consumer crashes on the first old-format message in the partition; because the message is committed/handled per-batch this poisons the partition, repeatedly failing the same offset — a rolling-deploy skew where new consumers and old producers cannot coexist.

[advisory] the zpopmin eviction silently drops up to spancount-1000 spans from a segment with no metric increment and no log line, unlike the flush path which emits metrics for oversized segments. operators lose observability into segment truncation: flushes will emit segments missing their oldest spans with zero signal, and the hardcoded 1000 cap ignores the configurable maxsegmentspans the python side used to enforce.

[advisory] the maxsegmentspans guard (metric spans.buffer.flushsegments.segmentspancountexceeded plus skip-and-drop) is deleted, leaving only the byte-size limit, while the lua-side 1000-cap is enforced only at insert time and only via zpopmin. segments flushed from keys that grew past 1000 before this code deployed (or via the fallback zcard path when eviction was bypassed) now produce arbitrarily large segments with only a byte cap, and dashboards alerting on the removed span-count metric go permanently silent.

[advisory] reducing the redirect-chain cap from 10000 to 1000 changes the documented contract ('segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined correctly') with no comment update, and the mismatch with the hasrootspan/flush logic is unobserved. traces with redirect chains deeper than 1000 now silently produce unjoined/duplicated segments during buffering, with no metric or log distinguishing the truncation; debugging production segment-assembly failures will misattribute the cause.

[bug] addguests.handler loads the booking with no status filter and bookinglistitem adds the 'additional guests' action to the base menu unconditionally, so guests can be added to cancelled or still-pending bookings. new guests of a cancelled booking receive an ics request with status:confirmed plus a 'guests added' email for a meeting that does not exist, updatecalendarattendees mutates the calendar entry of a cancelled event, and for pending bookings guests are told the event is confirmed before the organizer has accepted it.

[bug] for event types with seatspertimeslot the handler creates attendee rows directly with no capacity check and no attendeeseatreference, so guests added through this endpoint exceed the booked seat count and exist outside the seat-reference model the seats feature is built on. a seated booking already at capacity gains additional attendees (overbooking the time slot, since seat availability is derived from booking attendees), and seats-driven logic that reads each attendee's seat reference encounters attendees without one.

[bug] the mutation's onsuccess closes the dialog and resets the email list but never calls setisinvalidemail(false), so after a failed validation followed by a successful add, the red 'emails must be unique and valid' banner is still rendered the next time the dialog is opened. the user reopening the add guests dialog sees a validation error above an empty, valid form until they cancel or submit again; the banner is also never cleared while the user corrects the emails after a failed attempt.

[advisory] sendaddguestsemails failures are caught and reduced to console.log('error sending addguestsemails') with the error object discarded, and the handler still returns success. the organizer sees the 'guests added' success toast while some or all attendees received nothing, and the log line carries no error detail or structured-logger context, making the failure undiagnosable in production.

[advisory] when every submitted guest is filtered out because they are already an attendee or blacklisted, the handler throws badrequest with message 'emailsmustbeuniquevalid', which is false in both cases. a user adding an already-invited colleague (the dialog only checks uniqueness within the current input, not against existing attendees) is told their emails are invalid instead of 'already invited', prompting confused retries with the same result.

[bug] the permission check joins isteamadmin and isteamowner with && while naming the result isteamadminorowner, so team admins who are not owners are denied instead of allowed. a team admin (role admin) who is not the booking's organizer or an attendee gets forbidden when adding guests to their team's bookings — the admin portion of the intended permission matrix (organizer/admin/owner/attendee) is silently dropped; under exclusive membership roles the && can only ever pass for owners.

[bug] addguestshandler never checks booking.status, and the new 'addmembers' action is added to bookinglistitem's actions array unconditionally (unlike the roundrobin conditional directly below it), so guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, or pending bookings. new guests receive attendeescheduledemail invites with a hardcoded status:'confirmed' ics request (organizer-add-guests-email.ts / attendee-add-guests-email.ts) for an event that was cancelled or never confirmed, re-adding a dead event to their calendars, and existing attendees get 'guests added' notices for it.

[bug] zaddguestsinputschema enforces only per-string email format with no uniqueness, and the handler's filter (addguests.handler.ts:74-78) only exact-matches existing attendees, so duplicate or case-variant emails create duplicate attendee rows. adding 'john@x.com' when attendee 'john@x.com' already exists — reachable through the dialog, whose uniqueness check only covers the input array — persists a second attendee row for the same person who then receives two different guest emails; a direct api caller can pass the same email twice for the same result.

[bug] eventmanager is constructed from the acting user's credentials (getuserscredentials(ctx.user)) even though the permission check deliberately admits non-organizer actors, so for attendee or team-admin actors the calendar update runs without the organizer's calendar credentials. when anyone other than the organizer adds guests, updatecalendarattendees cannot authenticate against the organizer's destination calendar, so the calendar event's attendee list is never updated (or the mutation errors after attendees were already persisted at line 92), leaving the organizer's calendar and the booking permanently out of sync — the organizer's credentials are already loaded in booking.user.credentials but are not used.

[bug] for seated event types the handler creates bare attendee rows via createmany with no seatspertimeslot capacity check and no bookingseat records, even though it passes seatspertimeslot/seatsshowattendees into the calendarevent (lines 145-146). guests added to a seated booking exceed the seat limit with no guard, and per-seat flows (seat-only cancellation, sendscheduledseatsemails, seat counts on the booking page) never see these attendees because they have no bookingseat records — the seat-gated sibling path of the attendee model this diff touches was left unchecked.

[bug] onsuccess resets multiemailvalue but never resets isinvalidemail, so the 'emails must be unique and valid' error banner persists into the next dialog session. after one failed validation followed by a successful add, reopening the dialog shows the red error banner over a fresh empty form (until cancel is clicked); the banner also never clears while the user corrects the emails, since nothing resets it on change.

[bug] the remove-button tooltip uses the hardcoded literal 'remove email' instead of a t() key, unlike every other user-facing string in the component. non-english users see an untranslated english tooltip in a shared @calcom/ui component that is exported for reuse beyond this dialog.

[advisory] any authenticated attendee may add an unbounded number of guests in a single call (no max on the guests array, no rate limit), and each address receives a calendar invite email replyto'd to the organizer. an attendee can use an organizer's booking as an invite/email cannon to arbitrary third parties with messages that look like they come from the organizer (phishing surface); the only guard is the global blacklistedguestemails env var, which is not per-event-type and is case-broken per the separate bug.

[bug] the server schema accepts duplicate emails within guests (no uniqueness refine), while the client hand-copies the schema inline in addguestsdialog.tsx:26-29 with a uniqueness refine, so the accepted 'emails must be unique' constraint is enforced only in the ui and the two hand-maintained copies have already drifted. a direct addguests mutation with guests ["a@b.com","a@b.com"] passes server validation; the handler's filter (addguests.handler.ts:74-78) only dedupes against existing attendees, so both copies reach createmany and the guest ends up duplicated in the attendee list receiving duplicate invitation emails and a duplicated ics attendee entry, or the insert dies with a raw prisma unique-constraint 500.

[bug] the mutation's onsuccess resets multiemailvalue but never resets isinvalidemail, so the validation-error banner survives a successful submission. a user who triggers the 'emails must be unique and valid' banner, corrects the address, and adds guests successfully sees the same red error banner immediately upon reopening the dialog for the next booking, over a fresh empty form.

[bug] sendaddguestsemails is called with the raw guests input instead of the filtered uniqueguests array, so the email layer's newguests classification includes emails the handler explicitly refused to add. when a user submits an existing attendee's email alongside new guests, that existing attendee matches newguests.includes() in email-manager.ts:541 and receives a duplicate attendeescheduledemail booking confirmation instead of the attendeeaddguestsemail 'guests added' notice.

[bug] the organizer lookup runs findfirstorthrow on booking.userid || 0, so a booking with a null userid (a case the code itself anticipates) queries user id 0 and throws an unhandled prisma p2025. an attendee of an unassigned team booking who adds guests passes the permission gate and then receives a 500 internalservererror from the crashed findfirstorthrow instead of a 4xx response.

[bug] the booking query filters only on id with no status constraint, so the addguests mutation accepts cancelled and rejected bookings. adding guests to a cancelled booking creates attendee rows, calls updatecalendarattendees on the organizer's calendar event for a meeting that will never happen, and emails the new guest a confirmed ics invitation to a dead event.

[bug] the duplicate check compares guest === attendee.email case-sensitively while the blacklist check on the very next line lowercases both sides, so the same address in different casing bypasses dedup. re-adding an attendee as john@example.com when the stored row is john@example.com creates a second bookingattendee row for the same person, who then receives both the scheduled confirmation and the guests-added email.

[advisory] the team-member notification loop in sendaddguestsemails is dead code for this feature because the only caller (addguests.handler.ts:124-147) builds evt without a team field, so calendarevent.team is always undefined. non-organizer team members of collective/round-robin bookings never receive the 'guests added' notification this loop was written to send, and the next maintainer assumes team notification works because the branch exists; either populate evt.team in the handler or delete the loop.

[advisory] the handler persists the new attendees (lines 92-105) before updatecalendarattendees with no compensation, so a calendar-api failure leaves the database mutated while the mutation returns an error. when the calendar provider rejects the update, the guests are already stored; the organizer retries and now gets badrequest 'emailsmustbeuniquevalid' because the guests are existing attendees, leaving a half-applied state with a misleading error and no calendar update.

[advisory] the eventmanager is constructed from the caller's credentials (getuserscredentials(ctx.user)) even though the booking query includes booking.user.credentials, which then goes unused, so the calendar update runs as whoever called the mutation rather than the booking's organizer. when a non-organizer (an attendee or team admin, both explicitly allowed by the permission gate) adds guests, updatecalendarattendees runs with no credential for the organizer's destination calendar, so the organizer's external calendar event is left without the new guests while the confirmation emails claim they were added; the included-but-unused credentials in the query show the original intent was to use the organizer's.

[bug] the permission check named isteamadminorowner joins isteamadmin and isteamowner with && instead of ||, requiring the caller to be both admin and owner of the booking's team. team admins who are not owners (and owners who are not admins) are wrongly rejected with forbidden when adding guests to team bookings, so the authorization control does not implement its own stated admin-or-owner semantics and the feature silently fails for the entire admin role.

[bug] the uniqueguests filter only removes emails that match pre-existing attendees, and the server-side zaddguestsinputschema (addguests.schema.ts:5) omits the uniqueness refine the client applies in addguestsdialog.tsx, so duplicate emails within a single request each create an attendee row. a direct trpc call with guests:["victim@x.com","victim@x.com",...] bypasses the dialog's client-only refine, creates n duplicate attendee rows for the same mailbox, and sendaddguestsemails then sends one full-details email per duplicate row — a single mutation becomes an n-email bomb to a chosen address and permanently corrupts the booking's attendee list.

[bug] zaddguestsinputschema places no maximum length on the guests array, so the mutation accepts an arbitrarily large list of emails in one call. any attendee of any booking — the weakest authorization tier this endpoint grants — submits a 10,000-entry guests array, creating 10,000 attendee rows and triggering 10,000+ full-detail emails (one per new guest plus one per existing attendee) with no server-side cap, an email-bombing and resource-exhaustion vector through the platform's mail infrastructure.

[bug] the handler builds eventmanager from the calling user's credentials (getuserscredentials(ctx.user)) instead of the booking organizer's, while the booking.user.credentials rows fetched at line 38 are never used. when an attendee — a caller this endpoint explicitly authorizes — adds guests, updatecalendarattendees runs with credentials that have no access to the organizer's calendar event, so the calendar attendee list is never updated (or the mutation throws after the db write already persisted), and every request needlessly materializes the organizer's oauth tokens in memory.

[advisory] sendaddguestsemails sends an email to every attendee on the booking on every invocation rather than only the newly added guests. an attendee (the lowest-privilege caller this endpoint authorizes) loops the addguests mutation with one fresh guest per call and forces one 'guests added' email per call to the organizer and every other attendee — an unthrottled harassment/spam channel through the platform's mail sender that also degrades sending reputation.

[bug] the existing-attendee dedup compares emails case-sensitively (guest === attendee.email) while guest emails are stored verbatim (line 86), so a case variant of an existing attendee is not filtered out. a caller re-adds alice@x.com as alice@x.com, creating a second attendee row for the same real mailbox — the person is double-counted on the booking, receives duplicate emails, and appears twice on the calendar event.

[advisory] addguests createmany's new attendees without ever checking booking.eventtype.seatspertimeslot, even though the handler is seats-aware (it copies seatspertimeslot into evt at line 145). organizers of seat-limited event types get bookings overbooked past the configured seat cap — the capacity limit enforced at booking time is bypassed through the guest-add path, so seats-based attendee counts and per-seat emails no longer match configured capacity.

[bug] isteamadminorowner joins the two role checks with && instead of ||, so the caller must satisfy both isteamadmin and isteamowner for the team-permission branch to pass. a team admin who is not the team owner is thrown forbidden ('youdonothavepermission') when adding guests to their team's booking — the exact role this check was written to allow is locked out, and the branch is effectively owner-only (or always false where roles are mutually exclusive).

[bug] the catch around sendaddguestsemails discards the caught err and logs only the static string 'error sending addguestsemails', after which the handler returns { message: 'guests added' }. when guest-notification email delivery fails, the user still sees the 'guestsadded' success toast and the operator gets a log line with no error message or stack — the failure is undiagnosable and indistinguishable from success.

[bug] uniqueguests filters guests only against existing attendees and the blacklist, never against duplicates within the guests array, and the server-side zaddguestsinputschema omits the uniqueness refine that the dialog's hand-copied client schema enforces. a direct addguests mutation submitting the same email twice (['a@x.com','a@x.com']) passes server validation and reaches the attendees createmany, which throws an unhandled prisma p2002 unique-constraint error — the caller gets http 500 instead of the badrequest the handler promises for invalid emails.

[bug] the eventmanager is constructed from the caller's credentials (getuserscredentials(ctx.user), {...user}) even though the permission check explicitly authorizes attendees and team admins, while the organizer's credentials fetched via the booking query's user include (lines 35-39) are never used. when anyone other than the booking organizer invokes addguests (e.g., a team admin on a round-robin booking), updatecalendarattendees has no credential matching the organizer's destination calendar and silently skips the update — guests are persisted and emailed but never appear on the organizer's calendar event.

[bug] onsuccess resets multiemailvalue but never clears isinvalidemail, and the addguestsdialog component stays mounted in bookinglistitem between dialog opens. after a failed validation followed by a successful add (or after closing the dialog while the error banner is showing), reopening the dialog immediately displays the stale 'emailsmustbeuniquevalid' error banner over a fresh empty form.

[bug] sendaddguestsemails is passed the raw guests input instead of the uniqueguests list that was actually persisted, so emails filtered out as already-on-the-booking still classify their owner as a new guest. a user who re-submits an existing attendee's email (the dialog cannot block this, it only checks format and intra-form uniqueness) causes that attendee to receive the full attendeescheduledemail booking confirmation instead of the attendeeaddguestsemail guests-added notification.

[bug] guest deduplication compares emails case-sensitively (guest === attendee.email) even though email addresses are case-insensitive and no lowercasing is applied to the submitted guest. submitting 'john@x.com' when 'john@x.com' is already an attendee passes the filter and creates a second attendee row differing only in case — the guest receives duplicate emails and appears twice on the calendar and in the ics invite.

[advisory] addguests performs three non-transactional side effects in sequence — attendee createmany (92-106), calendar update (165), emails (168) — with no compensation or rollback on failure. a failure in updatecalendarattendees 500s the request after attendees are already persisted; the user's retry with the same valid emails then hits the uniqueguests.length === 0 badrequest 'emailsmustbeuniquevalid' (lines 80-81), reporting their valid input as invalid, and nobody can tell the calendar was never updated.

[bug] the organizer lookup uses findfirstorthrow({ where: { id: booking.userid || 0 } }), so a booking whose nullable userid is null resolves the query to id 0 and takes the throw path. an attendee of a null-userid booking who passes the permission check receives an unhandled prisma p2025 error — http 500 with no trpcerror shape — instead of any meaningful response.

[bug] isteamadminorowner joins the two role checks with &&, requiring the caller to be simultaneously team admin and team owner, contradicting the variable's name and the or-shaped permission line that consumes it. a team admin who is not the owner fails isteamowner, so the conjunction is false and they receive forbidden when adding guests to a team booking they don't organize — the branch grants nothing beyond the organizer/attendee paths, so the admin-or-owner permission it advertises is dead code.

[bug] the server-side zaddguestsinputschema omits the uniqueness refine its client-side twin enforces, and the handler's uniqueguests filter (addguests.handler.ts:74-78) only removes emails already on the booking, never duplicates within the request, so createmany inserts one row per array entry. a direct addguests mutation with ['a@x.com','a@x.com'] — the dialog's refine being client-only — writes two attendee rows for the same person on one booking, producing duplicate confirmation emails and duplicate ics attendee entries, and two concurrent requests adding the same email race past the read-filter-write sequence identically.

[bug] the handler commits the new attendee rows via prisma.booking.update with attendees.createmany (lines 92-106) before the external calendar update (line 165) and email send (line 168) run, with no transaction, compensation, or attendee-removal path. when eventmanager.updatecalendarattendees fails (expired oauth credential, provider error, already-deleted external event), the guests are already persisted, the client sees an error, and resubmitting the same emails is rejected by the uniqueguests filter with emailsmustbeuniquevalid — the booking is left with guests who never reached the external calendar or their inbox, and the organizer has no indication that resubmitting with one extra email is the only recovery.

[bug] the eventmanager charged with updating the booking organizer's external calendar is constructed from the caller's credentials (getuserscredentials(ctx.user)) instead of the organizer's (booking.user). when the caller is an attendee or team admin — precisely the non-organizer paths the permission check enables — the manager holds no credential matching the booking's calendar references, so updatecalendarattendees cannot update the event and the guests silently never appear on the external calendar while the db rows and the success response say they were added.

[bug] sendaddguestsemails is called with the raw request array guests rather than the filtered uniqueguests that were actually inserted, so email-manager's newguests.includes(attendee.email) classification treats excluded emails as newly added guests. an organizer who includes an already-attending email alongside new ones causes that existing attendee to receive a full attendeescheduledemail ('your event has been scheduled' with a request ics) instead of the guests-added notification, because their email was filtered out of the db write yet still matches the raw list.

[bug] the duplicate check compares emails case-sensitively (guest === attendee.email) while the blacklist is lowercased only on the environment-variable side, so case variation defeats both guards. submitting 'guest@example.com' when 'guest@example.com' already attends inserts a second attendee row for the same person — duplicate emails and duplicate ics attendee entries — and 'banned@example.com' bypasses blacklistedguestemails because the submitted guest is never lowercased before the includes check.

[bug] the organizer lookup passes booking.userid || 0 to prisma.user.findfirstorthrow, so for a booking whose userid is null — the nullability the || 0 fallback itself concedes — the query searches for user id 0 and throws prisma p2025. a permitted caller (an attendee of such a booking) gets an unhandled prisma error surfaced as a 500 internalservererror instead of a trpcerror, with no guests added.

[bug] handleadd sets isinvalidemail to true on validation failure but never clears it when validation succeeds, and the mutation's onsuccess resets the email list without resetting the flag. a user who trips the validation once, corrects the email, and successfully adds guests reopens the dialog to a stale 'emails must be unique and valid' banner over an empty input, and the banner also stays visible while a corrected submission is pending.

[advisory] the catch block around sendaddguestsemails logs a fixed string that discards the caught error object, and the handler unconditionally returns 'guests added'. when email delivery fails wholesale, guests are persisted but never receive the invite or ics, the organizer sees a success toast, and the operator troubleshooting it has only a bare 'error sending addguestsemails' console line with no error details.

[advisory] guest attendees are persisted with name '' and the organizer's timezone and locale as placeholder values, bypassing the attendee-creation path that normally captures the booker's own name and timezone. every downstream artifact for a guest renders placeholder data: emails greet an empty name, the ics attendee cn is blank, attendee lists show nameless rows, and date lines are formatted in the organizer's timezone, so guests in other zones see wrong local times in the email body.

[advisory] the dialog hand-rolls a local zaddguestsinputschema with the same name as the server's schema instead of importing the single definition, and the two copies have already drifted — the client refines for uniqueness, the server does not. the api contract is enforced differently in two places that must be edited in tandem: the existing drift is exactly what lets a direct mutation insert duplicate attendees, and the next constraint (guest-count cap, email normalization) will silently apply to only one side; importing the shared schema deletes the local copy and the whole drift class.

[advisory] the booking is fetched with no status or endtime condition and the handler never checks booking.status before adding guests, while both new email templates hardcode ics status confirmed with method request. guests can be added to cancelled or past bookings and each one receives a fresh confirmed request invite to an event the organizer cancelled — guests show up for nothing and the cancellation is undermined by a re-issued confirmed event.

[bug] the addguests mutation swallows every email-delivery failure in a catch that only console.logs a fixed string (discarding the err object) and then returns { message: 'guests added' } as success. when the mailer rejects, guests are persisted and the ui shows the 'guestsadded' success toast while no organizer, attendee, or new guest receives any notification; because err is discarded, the failure is also undiagnosable from server logs.

[bug] attendee rows are committed via prisma.booking.update/createmany before the external eventmanager.updatecalendarattendees call, with no transaction or rollback joining the two. if updatecalendarattendees throws (calendar api auth/network failure), the mutation rejects with an error toast while the guests are already persisted; every retry then hits the uniqueguests.length === 0 branch and fails with badrequest 'emailsmustbeuniquevalid', leaving the organizer unable to complete an operation that half-succeeded, with no notification emails ever sent.

[bug] the eventmanager is built from the caller's credentials (getuserscredentials(ctx.user)) instead of the booking organizer's, even though the findfirst at lines 35-40 explicitly fetches booking.user.credentials that are then never used. when an attendee or team admin — authorized by the isattendee/isteamadminorowner checks — adds guests, updatecalendarattendees runs with no credential for the organizer's connected calendar and silently skips the update: the organizer's google/outlook event never gains the guests while the api reports 'guests added' success.

[bug] isteamadminorowner is computed with && ((await isteamadmin(...)) && (await isteamowner(...))), requiring the user to be both admin and owner, contradicting the variable's own name. a team admin who is not the team owner receives forbidden 'youdonothavepermission' when adding guests to their team's booking — the permission path named 'adminorowner' is broken for the entire admin role.

[bug] blacklist entries are lowercased but the guest email is compared raw (blacklistedguestemails.includes(guest)), and the existing-attendee dedup check (guest === attendee.email) is case-sensitive. 'spam@x.com' bypasses a blacklistedguestemails entry 'spam@x.com' and is created as an attendee, and a case-variant of an existing attendee's email passes the filter so createmany inserts a duplicate attendee row that then receives duplicate emails and ics entries.

[bug] the server schema accepts duplicate emails (z.array(z.string().email()) with no uniqueness refinement) while the only dedup guard, zaddguestsinputschema's refine, lives client-side in addguestsdialog.tsx:26-29. a direct trpc mutation with guests: ['a@b.com', 'a@b.com'] passes server validation and createmany inserts two identical attendee rows, producing duplicate emails and duplicated ics attendees — exactly what the client-side refine exists to prevent.

[bug] the organizer is fetched with prisma.user.findfirstorthrow({ where: { id: booking.userid || 0 } }) with no not-found handling, despite the author's own '|| 0' acknowledging userid can be null. for a booking whose userid is null or whose organizer user was deleted — reachable because the isattendee check at line 52 authorizes attendees of such bookings — the handler throws a raw prisma p2025 that surfaces as an unhandled internalservererror 500 instead of the 4xx trpcerror shape every other failure path in the handler returns.

[bug] sendaddguestsemails is called with the raw input guests instead of uniqueguests, so the branch test newguests.includes(attendee.email) in email-manager.ts:541 also matches existing attendees whose address was re-submitted. an already-attending user who was accidentally re-included in the guest list receives the attendeescheduledemail 'you're scheduled' email for a long-past event instead of the 'guests added' notification — wrong content that misleads the recipient about why they were emailed.

[advisory] the team-member notification loop in sendaddguestsemails is dead code: addguests.handler.ts builds evt (lines 124-147) without ever setting team, so calendarevent.team?.members is always undefined. for team and round-robin event types, team members silently receive no guests-added notification even though this branch exists solely to send it — a dropped-notification path whose failure is invisible to users and operators.

[bug] the error-toast fallback is unreachable because the template literal ${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)} is always truthy, so message || t('unabletoaddguests') can never take the fallback. when a transport/network error leaves err.data and err.message undefined, the user sees the literal toast 'undefined: undefined' instead of the intended 'unable to add guests' message.

[bug] onsuccess resets the email list and closes the dialog but never resets isinvalidemail (unlike the cancel button, which does). after one failed validation followed by a successful add, reopening the dialog shows the stale 'emails must be unique and valid' error banner over an empty form, telling the user their untouched input is invalid.

[advisory] replyto is built as the organizer plus every attendee email with no bound, and the attendee list grows with every add-guests call. on seats bookings or after repeated guest additions the header accumulates dozens of addresses until strict smtp receivers reject the organizer's notification outright; it also discloses every attendee address to each recipient, defeating seatsshowattendees=false.

[advisory] the guests array has no .max() cap, so a single authorized request creates an unbounded number of attendee rows and triggers an unbounded number of outbound emails (organizer, every existing attendee, and every new guest is emailed per call). a permitted caller iterating the mutation with large guest lists mail-bombs every attendee from the instance's mail server on each call, risking provider throttling/blacklisting and unbounded bookingattendee growth with no server-side limit to stop it.

[bug] the badrequest thrown when uniqueguests is empty reuses 'emailsmustbeuniquevalid', but the actual condition is that every submitted guest was already an attendee or blacklisted — not that the emails are malformed or duplicated. a user who re-submits valid, unique addresses — for example retrying after the calendar-update failure in the non-atomic flow — is told their correctly-formatted emails are invalid, misdirecting debugging and hiding that the first attempt already added the guests.

[advisory] the handler authorizes and executes addguests without ever checking booking.status, so the flow runs on cancelled and rejected bookings. guests added to a cancelled booking receive attendeescheduledemail/ics attachments with status confirmed for an event that no longer exists, the cancelled booking's attendee list is mutated, and the api reports 'guests added' for a dead event.
