[bug] in updateevent the fallback branch event.destinationcalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalid === externalcalendarid)?.externalid is only evaluated when externalcalendarid is falsy, so it compares each calendar's externalid against undefined and always returns undefined — the condition is tautological and the previous fallback to destinationcalendar.externalid is destroyed. reschedules/updates of a google calendar event that rely on the booking's stored destinationcalendar (no externalcalendarid argument) now pass calendarid: undefined to calendar.events.update, which makes the google api reject the call and the calendar update silently fails; the same tautological find at lines 312-315 breaks deleteevent the same way.

[bug] evt.destinationcalendar?.push(...teamdestinationcalendars) silently no-ops when destinationcalendar is null (the case when neither eventtype nor organizeruser has one), and the preceding teammemberpromises loop reads user.destinationcalendar from user objects whose select (dynamic-user prisma select / eventtype.users) is not shown to include the destinationcalendar relation. for collective events where the organizer has no destination calendar, all team members' destination calendars are silently dropped instead of being used, so no per-host calendar events are created; if the user query select lacks destinationcalendar the push list is empty for every collective booking regardless.

[advisory] the db-fallback credential fetch requires credentialfromdb.app?.slug to be truthy, but core calendar credentials (e.g. googlecalendar credentials created before the app store migration, or credentials whose app row is absent) have no related app record, so the constructed credential stays undefined and the destination is silently skipped. legacy/pre-app-store credentials referenced by a destinationcalendar.credentialid cause that host's calendar event to be silently not created (no error surfaced), reproducing exactly the class of silent-skip bug this refactor was meant to fix; the same copy-pasted fallback in updateallcalendarevents (lines ~505-520) and the one in handlecancelbooking has the same dependency.

[bug] the meet-location fallback dereferences mainhostdestinationcalendar without a null guard, crashing when destinationcalendar is null/empty (the old code used optional chaining). when evt.destinationcalendar is null (no calendar connected, the common single-user case) and location is google meet, mainhostdestinationcalendar.integration throws typeerror, failing the booking with a 500 instead of falling back to cal video as the contract promises.

[bug] backup codes are generated and persisted during the setup step, before 2fa is ever confirmed, and the only place they are shown to the user is after successful enable — a user who runs setup and abandons the flow (or closes the modal at the qr/totp step) has 10 valid, never-revealed backup codes silently stored against their account. users who enabled 2fa via any earlier path or who abandoned setup have stored backup codes they never saw and cannot view again; the single-use consumption in login then deletes codes the user never knew existed, and the codes were accepted as valid second factors without ever being delivered.

[advisory] setup.ts calls symmetricencrypt with process.env.calendsoencryptionkey without the presence guard that the login and disable handlers added in this same diff, so the new backupcodes write path throws an unhandled typeerror when the key is unset rather than returning a structured error. operators running without calendsoencryptionkey get a raw 500 from /setup with no console.error breadcrumb, inconsistent with the sibling handlers that handle the same condition explicitly in this pr.

[bug] the 'no codes' sentinel is unrepresentable: missingbackupcodes is only raised when the backupcodes column is null, but consumption writes json arrays of null entries, so a user who has burned all 10 codes has a non-null column of nulls. a user with zero remaining codes gets 'backup code is incorrect' on every attempt instead of the 'missingbackupcodes' guidance ('generate them in your settings'), permanently and misleadingly — the same check exists in disable.ts and fails identically there.

[bug] backup code consumption uses a read-decrypt-modify-encrypt-write sequence with no transaction or conditional update, so the same backup code can be replayed in concurrent requests. two simultaneous logins submitting the same backup code both pass the indexof check before either write lands (next-auth credentials callbacks run concurrently), so a single one-time code grants two sessions — defeating the single-use guarantee the copy promises ('each backup code can be used exactly once') and letting an attacker who sniffed/copied a code use it even after the legitimate user already consumed it, if requests race.

[advisory] backup codes are generated with crypto.randombytes(5).tostring('hex'), yielding only 40 bits of entropy per code, well below the conventional 80+ bits for backup/recovery codes. an attacker who can submit many login attempts (e.g. via the credentials endpoint where rate limiting is per-ip and trivially distributed) has a materially better chance of guessing a valid code than against an 80-bit code; users with weak/leaked passwords get a second factor that is meaningfully brute-forceable.

[advisory] backup code verification uses backupcodes.indexof(credentials.backupcode...) — a plain, early-exiting string comparison rather than a constant-time comparison (timingequal/crypto.timingsafeequal), and the same non-constant-time indexof appears in disable.ts. each failed attempt leaks how many leading characters of a candidate code match positions in the stored list (indexof short-circuits per element, === per character); combined with the 40-bit code size this measurably aids online guessing by an automated attacker. rebuttal: per-request timing jitter makes the leak impractical — but with 10 ordered codes and 40-bit values the leak compounds across attempts rather than being neutralized.

[bug] ensureloaded! is only called from applicationcontrollersetlocale, so the fallback locales are never pre-loaded on any non-request rendering path (mailers, sidekiq jobs, rake tasks, system messages). a background-rendered mailer or job that calls i18n.t with a user locale whose translations aren't yet loaded falls back through fallbacklocalelist to sitesetting.defaultlocale/:en, and the simple backend returns 'translation missing' strings to end users in emails and system messages, because nothing on those paths ever ran i18n.fallbacks.ensureloaded!.

[bug] fallbacklocalelist[] unconditionally computes its own list and ignores the hash's stored contents, so the documented i18n fallbacks configuration api (i18n.fallbacks = {:de => [...]} or per-locale assignment i18n.fallbacks[locale] = [...]) is silently discarded — writes go into the hash but every read bypasses them. any plugin, engine, or ops code that sets explicit per-locale fallbacks (the standard way to express e.g. zhtw -> zhcn, which the todo itself anticipates) stores a value that is never read; the custom fallback chain runs instead, and the misconfiguration produces wrong-language output with no error.

[bug] fallback resolution invokes sitesetting.defaultlocale — a database-backed read — on every missing-translation lookup, including on threads where no db connection is expected (boot-time initializers, migrations, background jobs before connection establishment, rescue paths after connection loss). i18n.t, which previously touched no storage, now hits sitesetting (db) whenever a key is missing in the current locale; during boot or in a job with no connection this raises (e.g. pg::connectionbad) inside translation lookup, converting a benign missing translation into a crash of that job/initializer, and it adds a synchronous db read inside every translation miss on hot paths.

[bug] i18n.fallbacks.ensureloaded! is invoked only from applicationcontrollersetlocale, so fallback locales are loaded exclusively on web-request paths. background jobs, actionmailer deliveries, rake tasks, and sidekiq/scheduled jobs that set i18n.locale directly never trigger ensureloaded!, so a translation missing in the job's locale falls back to an unloaded defaultlocale and emits the raw key / missing-translation exception into emails and queued work — exactly the artifacts the 'server-side localization fallbacks' intent promised to protect, silently uncovered outside the controller happy path.

[bug] the code depends on queue.queue.shutdown() and queue.shutdown, which only exist in python 3.13+. on any python version below 3.13, fixedqueuepool.shutdown() crashes with attributeerror: 'queue' object has no attribute 'shutdown', and every except queue.shutdown clause raises attributeerror when evaluated, so the graceful-shutdown path the pr advertises never works — workers hang in workqueue.get() and daemon threads are killed mid-processing on interpreter exit.

[bug] simplequeueprocessingstrategy.close()/terminate() shut down the factory-shared fixedqueuepool, but resultsstrategyfactory reuses the same queuepool instance for every createwithpartitions call, so after any close arroyo creates a new strategy whose workers are all dead. on a partition rebalance (arroyo closes the old strategy then asks the factory for a new one), the new simplequeueprocessingstrategy submits workitems to queues whose orderedqueueworker threads have exited; messages accumulate forever, result processing silently stops, and offsets are never committed for those partitions.

[bug] getqueueforgroup uses python's hash(groupkey), which is salted per-process via pythonhashseed, so group→queue assignment is not stable across restarts or sibling consumer processes. two processes consuming the same topic (the cli supports --processes > 1 with numprocesses, which forks children) hash the same subscription key to different queue indices, so ordering guarantees for a subscription are broken by process boundaries; tests like testdifferentgroupsdistributed (asserting len(queueindices) == 3 over 20 keys) also become seed-dependent and can fail intermittently in ci.

[advisory] the strategy feeds message.payload directly to decoder (resultsstrategyfactory.decodepayload), which begins with assert not isinstance(payload, filteredpayload), so a filteredpayload reaches the generic except branch and is logged as an unexpected error rather than being filtered cleanly. any arroyo filter step upstream of this strategy turns filtered messages into a logged exception storm with full stack traces per message, and the offset is silently marked complete — operators see 'error submitting message to queue' errors in logs while processing is actually fine, masking real errors.

[bug] genrequestdata compares nodestore error-event timestamps (epoch seconds, or iso-8601 strings for js-sdk events) directly against rrweb breadcrumb timestamps (epoch milliseconds) with no unit or type normalization, so the ordering predicate compares incompatible values. for js-sdk error events the str-vs-number comparison raises typeerror and the summarize-breadcrumbs endpoint returns 500 for any replay that has errors; even when timestamps are floats, every error is ~1000x 'older' than every breadcrumb, so all error lines are emitted before the first breadcrumb and the docstring's promised chronological interleaving never happens.

[bug] fetcherrordetails pairs error ids with node data positionally via zip(errorids, events.values()) instead of looking up events by nodeid, so the pairing holds only if getmulti returns values in input order and includes none entries for missing nodes. when any referenced error event has been cleaned from nodestore (retention expiry), getmulti's returned mapping omits it, every later error shifts one position, and each error id is paired with another error's title/message in the payload sent to seer, corrupting the error context in the ai summary.

[bug] browserreportserializer declares both age and timestamp as required=false and enforces only mutual exclusion, so a report containing neither field passes validation even though the validators' own docstrings (and both cited specs) require exactly one of them to be present. spec-violating reports with neither age nor timestamp are accepted with http 200 and counted in the browserreporting.rawreportreceived metric, so the metric overcounts valid reports and the one-of contract the new validation claims to implement is not enforced.

[bug] fetcherrordetails pairs errorids with nodestore results positionally via zip(errorids, events.values()), but getmulti returns a dict keyed by nodeid that omits missing keys and need not preserve input order (the django backend returns only found rows in query order), so whenever a node is missing or reordered the errorevent is built with a different error's id and data. errorevent.id is misattributed to the wrong error whenever any node is absent or the backend reorders results — latent today because only title/message/timestamp reach the log message, but any consumer of the id (e.g., deep-linking an error out of a summary) points at the wrong event; on the django nodestore backend this triggers whenever any error node has been cleaned up while others remain.

in haspermission(clientmodel, string), the 'all-clients' type-level fallback only fires when no per-client resource exists; once a per-client resource exists, evaluation runs only against that resource and the type-level resource is never consulted. since deleting a scope permission (the standard authz admin api, used in the tests' @aftereach) removes the policy but not the resource, an orphaned policy-less per-client resource permanently shadows type-level grants: after deleting a client-specific permission and later granting an 'all clients' manage permission, that one client returns 403 forever. the same shadowing occurs with a live per-client resource holding a grant for a different scope (e.g., per-client view + all-clients manage still denies manage for that client), contradicting the 'all-clients' semantics the fallback comment describes. the pr's tests never delete a per-client permission and then rely on a type-level grant, so this isn't covered.

clientpermissionsv2 throws raw unsupportedoperationexception from methods still declared on the shared clientpermissionevaluator/clientpermissionmanagement interfaces (setpermissionsenabled, ispermissionsenabled, resource, getpermissions, canexchangeto, exchangetopermission, managepermission, etc.), while the clientremovedevent listener (touched by this pr) still calls management(...).clients().setpermissionsenabled(client, false) on every client removal, and token-exchange and the v1 permission rest endpoints also call into this surface — so any v2-mode caller reaching these methods gets an unhandled 500 instead of graceful behavior; in particular, if management() dispatches to the v2 evaluator, deleting a client throws (or cleanup is silently skipped if the provider-event manager swallows listener exceptions).

clientremovedevent cleanup listener in adminpermissions calls clients().setpermissionsenabled(client, false), but clientpermissionsv2.setpermissionsenabled unconditionally throws unsupportedoperationexception; since the listener now runs only when adminfinegrainedauthz is enabled (exactly when the v2 evaluator is active), every client deletion under the feature either fails/rolls back or silently skips cleanup, leaving orphaned per-client permission resources

all-clients manage does not imply view/list of client scopes: canviewclientscopes/requireviewclientscopes delegate to canview() which checks only all-clients view, so a manage-only grantee can create/update/delete client scopes but gets 403 when listing or viewing them — inconsistent permission lattice producing mutate-but-cannot-read behavior

[bug] on restart, createprocessforshards replaces self.processes[processindex] with a new process/thread without stopping the old one when it is a threading.thread (the isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process) guard skips the kill entirely for threads), so the old thread keeps flushing the same shards concurrently with the new one. in any producetopipe (threaded) deployment where a flusher is restarted via ensureprocessesalive, two threads flush the same shard simultaneously and produce duplicate span segments to kafka; restarts accumulate leaked threads.

[bug] flusherprocesses from the click option is an unvalidated int (default 1, no min= bound in click.option), and a non-positive value like -1 produces numprocesses = min(-1, len(shards)) = -1, so range(-1) yields an empty processtoshardsmap and zero flusher processes are ever created. an operator passing --flusher-processes -1 (or any negative value) silently gets a consumer with no flusher at all: spans accumulate in redis unbounded while the consumer reports healthy.

[bug] when a flusher running as a threading.thread (producetopipe path, used by tests and the pipe consumer) is declared hung, ensureprocessesalive skips killing it but calls createprocessforshards for the same shard list, leaving the old hung thread alive alongside a new thread both polling the same redis shards. two flusher threads race to fetch-and-delete segments from the same shards, producing duplicate kafka span payloads or interleaved partial flushes; the hung thread is never reaped, so each hang+restart leaks a live thread and multiplies redis load.

[advisory] join() breaks out of the process loop when the deadline expires, so every spawnprocess later in the dict iteration order is never sent terminate(), and is only reaped because it is daemon=true. during a timeout-limited shutdown, some flusher processes keep running and keep producing to kafka after join() returns, letting in-flight segments race against the next consumer instance's rebalance; the old single-process code had the same window but the multi-process version widens it to n processes non-deterministically.

[advisory] maxprocesses = maxprocesses or len(buffer.assignedshards) treats an explicit 0 (or the cli passing 0) as "use one process per shard", inverting the operator's intent to disable parallel flushers. an operator setting --flusher-processes=0 to force the single-process behavior instead gets the maximum fan-out (one process per shard), the exact opposite of the requested configuration.

[advisory] in join, when the shared deadline expires mid-loop, break skips both waiting on and terminate()-ing all remaining flusher processes, so only the first process is reliably terminated on timeout. a consumer shutdown that hits its join timeout leaves n-1 spawned flusher processes alive holding redis segment leases; they keep flushing and producing after the consumer is considered down, so operations teams see ghost producers during any timed-out deploy or crash-loop restart.

[bug] when the flusher runs in threading mode (producetopipe is set, i.e. the test/pipeline path) and a process is judged unhealthy by the hang check, ensureprocessesalive never terminates the old thread (the kill is guarded by isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process)) yet immediately calls createprocessforshards to start a new thread over the same shards. two concurrent flushers poll the same redis shards and produce the same segments to kafka twice, duplicating span data downstream; the zombie thread also keeps updating the shared healthysince value, masking future hangs of the replacement thread.

[bug] spanflusher.join() uses break inside the per-process loop to exit the entire outer for-loop when the deadline is exhausted, so all remaining processes are never terminated or waited on. on a timeout during consumer shutdown, flusher processes for later process indices keep running and keep producing spans to kafka after join() returns, so messages are emitted for offsets already committed (or not committed) by the dying consumer, producing out-of-order/duplicate data with no bounded shutdown.

[advisory] the new --flusher-processes option defaults to 1, and flusher.py computes maxprocesses = maxprocesses or len(buffer.assignedshards), so passing 0 (or any falsy value) silently means one-per-shard rather than unlimited-parallel or an error. an operator setting --flusher-processes=0 expecting to disable the extra processes instead gets maximum process count spawned (one per shard), multiplying redis connections and memory usage per consumer; the falsy-or idiom makes the cli value ambiguous.

[bug] on an unhealthy process, ensureprocessesalive calls process.kill() and immediately starts a replacement via createprocessforshards, without joining or reaping the killed process. for a cause="hang" restart the old process is still running during the new one's startup; both processes poll the same shards concurrently, and if a segment fetch is not strictly atomic per shard, segments get produced to kafka twice (duplicate spans downstream), while the unreaped zombie accumulates one dead process object per restart.

[advisory] join() consumes the shared deadline sequentially per process and breaks out without terminating the remaining processes when time runs out. with n flusher processes and a bounded timeout, the first hung process eats the entire deadline; every later process is skipped without terminate() and its redis-backed segments are never flushed before the consumer exits — operators doing bounded shutdowns see silently unflushed spans for all shards after the first stuck one.

[advisory] self.maxprocesses = maxprocesses or len(buffer.assignedshards) uses truthiness on an int option, so flusherprocesses=0 falls back to one-process-per-shard instead of being honored or rejected. an operator who sets --flusher-processes 0 intending to minimize processes (or a misconfigured deploy) silently gets the maximum process fan-out, the opposite of the intent, with no warning.

[bug] the validation regex explicitly permits a port suffix ((:[0-9]{1,5})?) but recordforhost matches on uri.host, which excludes the port, so a host saved with a port can never be matched. an admin who enters eviltrout.com:3000 passes validation and appears saved, but embed requests from that origin (referer http://eviltrout.com:3000/..., uri.host eviltrout.com) are rejected with invalid referer host — the exact scenario the 'multiple hosts' spec in embedcontrollerspec claims to cover but doesn't, since no spec creates a host with a port.

[advisory] in the new ids hydration branch, hydrated || [] is dead code (a .map result is never nil) and individual lookupsubtype misses are still pushed into the array, so a payload whose root omits one referenced id yields an array containing an undefined element instead of an empty/skipped value. the next developer consuming a ids hydration where the side-loaded root is incomplete (e.g. a serializer that forgets to include one record) gets undefined array elements that crash on .get('id') at render time instead of a detectable empty result.

[bug] the migration builds its insert with ruby string interpolation of the raw setting value ('{h}') instead of a quoted/parameterized sql value. a crafted embeddablehosts setting value containing a single quote (the old setting accepted free text lines) produces a malformed sql statement and aborts the migration, breaking the deploy; it also permits sql injection through the setting value.

[advisory] the model enforces a format check but no uniqueness invariant on host, even though the old newline-separated site setting was implicitly a set and the ui presents the table as a list of distinct allowed hosts. an admin can save the same host twice with different categories; recordforhost then returns an arbitrary first match, so the category chosen for the duplicate row silently never applies to new embedded topics, and the next admin editing the 'wrong' row sees no effect.

[bug] the migration does execute("select c.id ... where s.name = 'embedcategory'")[0]['id'] with no nil guard, so it crashes with nomethoderror on any install that never set the embedcategory site setting. every fresh install (and every existing install without embedcategory configured) fails to run the migration, halting the deploy with undefined method '[]' for nil:nilclass — the schema for the new table never exists and all embed endpoints break.

[bug] the backfill interpolates each migrated host value directly into an insert statement (values ('{h}', ...)), so any host string containing a single quote breaks or injects. a legacy embeddablehosts value like o'brien.example.com (accepted by the old free-text setting) makes the migration raise a sql syntax error on deploy; crafted values execute arbitrary sql.

[bug] categoryid is assigned from params with no existence check and the table has no fk or check tying it to categories, so a host row can persist with a categoryid pointing at a deleted or nonexistent category. an admin picks a category, that category is later deleted (or the id is stale in an open tab on save); the saved host keeps the dangling id and the embed ui renders a blank/broken category badge with no way to detect the orphan at write time.

[advisory] save() sends only host and categoryid derived from this.categoryid, which is set only in the edit() action — an unsaved-new-row path or a save without prior edit leaves categoryid null and the buffered host name is read via getproperties('host') while the input binds to buffered.host, duplicating the host value in two places. if save fires before edit() ever set categoryid (e.g. an enter-keypress race on a newly added row), the row is persisted with categoryid null, which the backend silently rewrites to uncategorized — the admin sees their newly added host land in the wrong category with no error surfaced.

[bug] the migration interpolates the raw embeddablehosts setting value into an unquoted-parameter sql string ("insert into embeddablehosts ... values ('{h}', ...)"), so any stored host entry containing a single quote (the old setting accepted free-form lines) breaks the insert with a sql syntax error and aborts the migration mid-way. the migration crashes during deploy after already deleting nothing (delete runs later) but leaves the site un-migrated on older hosts; on retry the embedcategory join query can also return an empty set and nil['id'] raises nomethoderror on installs where embedcategory's row holds '' (inner join on s.value = c.name matches nothing), making the migration non-restartable and blocking deploys.

[advisory] expandablefirstpost? silently drops the "an embeddable host is configured" gate that the original intent of the check encoded — it now returns true whenever embedtruncate is on and the topic has an embed, even if the embeddablehosts table is empty or the host was deleted after the topic was embedded. a site that removes all embeddable hosts keeps serving truncated/expandable first posts for previously-embedded topics (the check no longer consults current host configuration), a behavior change from the prior contract that the renamed spec case ('is false if embeddablehost is blank' now passes vacuously with no host fabrication) papers over rather than explicitly accepts.

[advisory] the migration string-interpolates the stored site-setting value h directly into a raw sql insert: execute "insert into embeddablehosts (host, categoryid, ...) values ('{h}', ...)". any admin-configured embeddablehosts line containing a single quote (or anything that alters sql syntax) breaks the migration mid-run or executes unintended sql against the sitesettings value; the migration's select path treats this data as trusted and unescaped even though it is user-entered admin config, and this data-migration pattern invites copy-paste into future code that interpolates request-derived values.

[advisory] the host validation regex permits an optional port (\(:[0-9]{1,5}\)?) but beforevalidation strips only the scheme and path, leaving ports like "example.com:8080" stored in the host column, while recordforhost compares against urihost which excludes the port. an admin who enters an allowed host with a port saves successfully, but that host can never match any referer or embed url because the stored string "example.com:8080" is compared against uri hosts like "example.com" — the operator believes embedding is enabled for their site while every request from it is rejected with invalidaccess.

[advisory] the beforevalidation normalization combined with the format regex has no negative test — embeddablehostspec.rb only asserts three happy-path trims, never that an invalid host (e.g., 'http://eviltrout.com:8080' or 'not a host') is rejected. if the regex or the sub! chain regresses (e.g., port-stripping or a regex that accepts everything), fabricate-driven controller specs keep passing with the fixed 'eviltrout.com' value and admins can save hosts that the embed endpoint will never match.

[bug] the migration's insert is guarded on embeddablehosts && embeddablehosts.cmdtuples > 0, but cmdtuples is the count of rows affected by a command and is 0 for select results in postgresql, so the guarded insert never runs while the paired delete from sitesettings where name in ('embeddablehosts', 'embedcategory') on line 32 runs unconditionally. every site's configured embeddablehosts list is destroyed with no replacement rows created in embeddablehosts, so embedding silently stops working for all forums after migration and the data cannot be recovered without a pre-migration backup.

[bug] the migration deletes the embeddablehosts and embedcategory site settings rows with no export/backup and no rollback path, making the migration irreversible, and it does so in a single step rather than an expand/contract sequence. during a rolling deploy, pods still running old code call sitesetting.embeddablehosts / embedcategory (removed readers in the new models) after the settings rows are deleted, so old pods raise errors on embed requests until restart; and after rollback there is no data to restore — hosts configured by admins are gone.

[advisory] the backfill interpolates the raw setting value directly into sql (insert ... values ('{h}', ...)), bypassing the model layer's parameterization and its beforevalidation normalization (http:// prefix and path stripping), so migrated rows keep http:///path forms the old validation logic stripped. admins on sites with hosts stored as full urls get rows that never match lower(host) = ? lookups in embeddablehost.recordforhost (which compares bare hostnames), so embedding breaks for exactly the hosts the migration was supposed to preserve.

[bug] destroy calls host.destroy on a nil record when params[:id] does not match any embeddablehost, raising nomethoderror and returning a 500 where the api contract for an admin crud endpoint implies a 4xx/not-found. an admin double-deletes or clicks delete on a stale row (already deleted in another tab): the request crashes with a 500 and the admin sees a generic error instead of a not-found response; the client-side destroyrecord promise rejects and the row silently stays in the table.

[bug] update passes nil to savehost when the id is absent (params[:id] nil) or not found, and savehost then executes host.host = ... on nil, raising nomethoderror and returning a 500 instead of a 4xx. any put to /admin/embeddablehosts/:id with a nonexistent or stale id returns a raw 500; the ember save flow's popupajaxerror shows an unspecified server error and the buffered edit state is left dangling.

[bug] the delete action chains destroyrecord().then(...) with no .catch, so a failed destroy is an unhandled promise rejection whose error is never surfaced. if the delete request fails (network error, 500 from the nil-host crash, permission lapse), the user gets no error dialog, the host row stays in the table with no indication anything failed, and an unhandled rejection lands in the console only.

[bug] ruby's strict uri parser raises uri::invalidurierror for stored website strings containing non-ascii idn hosts (e.g. http://例え.jp/profile) or spaces in the path (e.g. http://example.com/my page), so the rescue returns nil, websitename becomes nil while includewebsitename still returns true (website is present), and the {{if model.websitename}} guard in user.hbs hides the website row that the removed client-side website.split("/")[2] computation displayed. users whose saved website url contains any character ruby's uri parser rejects lose the website link from their profile entirely after this change — the globe icon and anchor disappear even though model.website is still set and the old code rendered a host label for exactly these values.

[bug] the display string is built from uri(...).host plus uri(...).path only, discarding the port and the query string: http://example.com:3000/admin?tab=2 renders as example.com/admin on same-domain instances and bare example.com elsewhere, whereas the removed client-side split("/")[2] display preserved the port (example.com:3000). profiles linking self-hosted services on nonstandard ports — common among self-hosted discourse communities — display a label that implies port 80 instead of the real destination, and two links differing only by query string render identically; because websitehost + uri(website.tos).path is duplicated in all three branches (lines 144, 147, 150), fixing it takes three coordinated edits.

[advisory] the same-domain heuristic is asymmetric: a website that is a subdomain of the instance domain (www.example.com/user on instance example.com) falls to the else branch, fails discoursehost.endswith?('.www.example.com'), and shows host-only — while the mirror case (website example.com on instance forums.example.com) and the equal-length sibling case both show the full path. operators running on apex domains (example.com) get the requirement 'show complete path when domains match' satisfied in only one direction: users' www-prefixed links to the very same site render truncated on the profile, while the reverse instance configuration renders them expanded.

[bug] the same-domain matching in websitename is directional: a website host with more labels than the instance host (www.example.com/t/topic/1 when the instance is example.com) fails every branch — the elsif requires equal label counts and the else requires discoursehost to end with ".{websitehost}" — and renders host-only text, even though the elsif itself declares sibling subdomains of the same registrable domain equivalent. a forum hosted at an apex domain (example.com) displays plain "www.example.com" (or "docs.example.com") for links into its own www/subdomain mirror, so the feature this pr exists for silently fails for that entire deployment class, while the mirror-image case (instance www.example.com, website example.com/...) shows the full path — a transitivity break in the code's own equivalence policy; none of the three new specs exercises a website host with more labels than the instance host, so ci cannot catch the gap.

[bug] includewebsitename lacks the trailing ? that the activemodel::serializers include{attribute}? conditional-inclusion hook dispatches, so the guard is never invoked and websitename is serialized for every user. every userserializer payload for a user without a website now carries websitename: null (profiles, cards, admin views), the author's include-only-when-website-present intent silently fails, and because the diff adds no website-absent spec the dead guard ships undetected — a maintainer reading the serializer will believe the attribute is conditionally included when it never is.

[bug] the sibling-equivalence check approximates "same registrable domain" by comparing label counts and joining labels after the first, which has no public-suffix awareness and therefore classifies unrelated tenants under shared registrable domains as the same site. an instance at forum.herokuapp.com (or user.github.io, or foo.co.uk) treats any sibling tenant's url as same-domain and displays its full path — other.herokuapp.com/their/page renders as "other.herokuapp.com/their/page" instead of the previous host-only text — displaying paths of sites unrelated to the instance, an expansion the stated requirement ("website domain is same as instance domain") never asked for.

[bug] websitename builds the displayed text by concatenating uri(website.tos).host with the raw uri(website.tos).path, and uripath returns "/" for scheme-only urls while excluding query string, fragment, and port, so same-domain websites display as example.com/ and query- or port-distinguished urls lose the distinguishing part of the url. a user on instance example.com whose website is exactly http://example.com now shows 'example.com/' where the removed client-side website.split("/")[2] displayed 'example.com'; http://example.com/page?id=3 displays as 'example.com/page' and a same-domain url on :3000 shows no port, so the profile's displayed link text no longer identifies the actual target the href points to.

[bug] websitename returns nil for any stored website that ruby's uri() raises on (rescue nil, e.g. a url with an internal space like http://foo bar.com or unencoded non-ascii), and the template now gates the entire website row on {{if model.websitename}} (user.hbs line 66), whereas the removed client-side website.split("/")[2] displayed the host for those same values. after this deploy, users whose previously-rendered malformed website urls survive in the database lose the globe icon and website link from their profile entirely, with no error anywhere — model.website is still serialized and present but nothing renders it.

[bug] the label-suffix heuristic treats any two hosts sharing two or more trailing labels as the same domain, so for instances addressed by a raw ip a website on a different ip that shares the trailing octets passes the sibling comparison (website http://9.0.0.9/page on instance 10.0.0.9 compares [1..-1] as '0.0.9' == '0.0.9'). intranet/internal discourse instances bound to an ip address display a foreign machine's full path as though it were the same site — the registrable-domain semantics of the parent/sibling rule are meaningless for numeric hosts, and nothing in the guards excludes them.

[bug] includewebsitename is defined without the ? suffix required by the serializer framework's conditional-attribute hook (include{attribute}?, the convention used by includename?/includeemail? throughout this codebase and by the include methods that untrustedattributes generates), so this method is never invoked and the website.present? gate it was written for is inert dead code. websitename is emitted under whatever gate untrustedattributes registers instead of the author's presence check, so every user payload for a user with no website carries "websitename": null — the presence constraint this diff introduces silently fails to hold, and no spec covers the no-website case that would have caught the broken hook.

[bug] the elsif classifies any two hosts with equal label counts greater than 2 as 'same domain' whenever all labels after the first are equal, so on an instance hosted directly under a two-label public suffix (forum.co.uk, forums.com.au, bbs.co.jp) every user website under that same suffix (shop.co.uk, news.com.au) is wrongly matched. on instances hosted under multi-label public suffixes, unrelated external sites receive the full-path treatment the pr reserved for the instance's own domain — a profile displays 'shop.co.uk/deals' as if it were an internal link — a silent widening of the accepted objective 'website domain is same as instance domain' to 'shares a two-label suffix'; the new specs never exercise it because every fixture uses example.com-style two-label tlds.

[advisory] for same-domain websites that are the bare root with a trailing slash (http://example.com/), websitehost + uri(website.tos).path appends the root path '/' and the displayed label renders as 'example.com/'. a user whose website is exactly the instance root url gets 'example.com/' shown on their profile — the one same-domain shape (empty path) the new specs do not cover — which reads as a typo and was never part of the accepted 'show complete url path' intent.

[advisory] the rewritten profile-website anchor keeps target="blank" with no rel="noopener noreferrer" while binding href to the user-controlled model.website, so the opened page retains a live window.opener handle to the discourse tab. any user can set their profile website to a page they control; when a viewer clicks the globe link, the opened page can call window.opener.location to redirect the victim's still-open discourse tab to a phishing clone of the instance (reverse tabnabbing) — this diff re-emits exactly this anchor markup for the user-supplied url and leaves the opener protection absent.

[bug] the elsif branch compares registrable domains by dropping only the first label (split('.')[1..-1]), so two unrelated registrations under the same multi-label public suffix compare equal. on an instance hosted at e.g. blog.com.br, a user's website 'http://loja.com.br/products' is classified as same-site and the profile displays the full 'loja.com.br/products' instead of the host alone; because no test in this diff executes this branch at all, the misclassification ships undetected.

[advisory] the else branch detects same-site only in the parent direction (discoursehost.endswith?("." << websitehost)), so 'http://www.example.com/page' on an instance hosted at 'example.com' returns host-only, while the semantically identical sibling case ('www.example.com' on 'forum.example.com') returns the full path. admins of apex-hosted instances (hostname 'example.com') see the feature silently not apply to their own www-prefixed profile websites; no test pins this asymmetry and nothing in the diff documents it as intended, so it reads as an oversight of the 'same as instance domain' contract in the pr title.

[bug] the elsif branch matches any two hosts whose labels after the first are identical, so on an instance whose hostname is a registrable domain under a multi-label public suffix (discourse.currenthostname = 'example.co.uk'), a website on a completely different registrable domain ('http://other.co.uk/some-page') is treated as the instance's own domain and serialized with its full path. users on .co.uk/.com.au/.org.uk-style instances see the complete url path rendered as the website name for sites that are not the instance's domain (e.g. 'other.co.uk/some-page' instead of 'other.co.uk'), violating the feature's stated rule (show the full path only when the website domain is the instance domain) and misleading profile viewers; the href stays correct so nothing crashes or links wrong.

[advisory] t.cleanup for the annotation/annotationtag tables is registered only after createtestannotations succeeds, and the shared fakesql is reused across subtests, so any partial failure during the new 40003-row insertmulti leaves rows that leak into the subsequent subtests' assertannotationcount. a mid-creation failure in one subtest (now far more likely with the new 40003-row case) corrupts the counts asserted by later subtests, producing confusing cross-test failures instead of an isolated failure.

[bug] the maxcount cleanup and orphaned-tag cleanup reuse the same r.log.error debug pattern, logging the entire fetched id slice at error level on every batch. with annotationcleanupjobbatchsize in the thousands, each batch emits thousands of ids at error level, producing multi-megabyte log lines per cleanup run and corrupting the log contract that errors indicate failures.

[bug] the new batching code logs routine informational messages ('annotations to clean by time', 'cleaned annotations by count', 'tags to clean', 'cleaned tags') at error level via r.log.error, including an 'err' key that is provably nil at those call sites. every successful cleanup cycle (now running every minute per the cleanup.go ticker change) emits error-level log lines with nil errors containing full id lists, spamming operator alerting and making real errors indistinguishable from normal operation; no test asserts log levels so this passes silently.

[advisory] createtestannotations now inserts 500 annotations per insertmulti call (~7500+ bound parameters per statement), which only works because modern sqlite (>= 3.32.0) raised sqlitemaxvariablenumber to 32766 — the exact limit the new 40003-row test case is nominally probing. on an environment with sqlite < 3.32.0 (999-parameter limit) the test fixture itself fails with 'too many sql variables' before the cleanup logic under test is ever reached, producing a confusing fixture failure rather than a meaningful signal; the test's own name acknowledges the version dependency but the insert path does not guard against it.

[advisory] the sqlite >999-parameters workaround is keyed on r.cfg.annotationcleanupjobbatchsize rather than on len(ids), and other backends have parameter limits too (postgresql caps at 65535), so a batch size configured above those limits still builds one giant placeholder list on non-sqlite databases. an operator on postgresql who raises annotationcleanupjobbatchsize above 65535 (the config allows it) gets 'number of parameters must be between 0 and 65535' errors every cleanup cycle, deleting nothing; chunking the placeholder list in deletebyids regardless of dialect removes the per-backend limit knowledge.

[bug] cleanup success paths are logged at error level with a nil err field ('r.log.error("annotations to clean by time", ... "err", err)' and 'r.log.error("cleaned annotations by time", ...)', repeated identically in the maxcount block and in cleanorphanedannotationtags). every successful batch emits error-level log lines containing an "err": null key, so operators running error-based alerting on grafana's logs see a flood of spurious 'errors' from this background job on every cleanup run; the debug strings are clearly intended as temporary logging left in the shipped code.

[advisory] detectprovider now resolves multiple providers by order, but defaultcryptoprovider, wildflyelytronprovider and fips1402provider all return order() == 200, so a tie between the server-side providers is broken by unspecified serviceloader ordering. any deployment that ends up with two of the three order-200 providers on one classpath gets a nondeterministically chosen provider (fips vs non-fips) depending on classpath enumeration order — a silent, environment-dependent security-relevant behavior change from the old hard failure; the order() mechanism as shipped does not actually order the providers it was written to order.

[bug] removing the multiple-provider error and replacing it with order-based selection makes ties (all three existing providers return order 200) resolve by arbitrary serviceloader/classpath iteration order. a fips deployment that accidentally has both crypto/fips1402 and crypto/default (or crypto/elytron) jars on the classpath previously failed fast with 'multiple crypto providers loaded'; now defaultcryptoprovider can be silently selected over fips1402provider (or vice versa) depending on jar classpath order, so a fips-mode server runs with the non-fips provider with no error or log line above debug level.

[bug] the authz-client jar globally registers authzclientcryptoprovider as a cryptoprovider service, so embedding authz-client on any classpath with keycloak-common silently installs a stub provider whose getalgorithmprovider, getsignature, getpemutils, etc. all throw unsupportedoperationexception. any application that adds keycloak-authz-client for the authorization api and also uses other keycloak-common functionality (pem parsing, cert utils, aes ciphers, signature instances) crashes with unsupportedoperationexception at runtime when no higher-order provider is present; conversely, in the keycloak server itself the authz-client jar now participates in crypto-provider selection, a boundary the authz client module previously did not cross.

[bug] getbouncycastleprovider() returns the jvm default keystore provider (typically sun) instead of a bouncycastle provider, violating the cryptoprovider contract every existing implementation honors. any keycloak-common code path that calls cryptointegration.getprovider().getbouncycastleprovider() to obtain or register bc (the documented purpose of the method) silently receives the wrong provider in a standalone authz-client deployment, producing algorithm-not-found or wrong-provider failures instead of a clear error.

[bug] detectprovider silently replaces the previous fail-fast illegalstateexception on multiple crypto providers with silent selection of the highest-order provider, changing an accepted safety invariant of the server without any human-accepted requirement. a keycloak server deployment with both the fips and default providers on the classpath used to abort startup with 'multiple crypto providers loaded' — an operator in a fips-mandated environment now gets a silently non-fips defaultcryptoprovider (order tie at 200 resolved by arbitrary serviceloader classpath order) and processes secrets under non-validated crypto with no error.

[bug] defaultcryptoprovider.order() returns 200, identical to fips1402provider and wildflyelytronprovider, so the 'higher order wins' selection rule cannot actually discriminate between the server crypto providers and falls back to arbitrary serviceloader ordering on the tie. when default and fips1402 (or elytron) jars coexist on the server classpath, which crypto provider the server runs with is decided by classpath jar order, not by any declared preference — the stated intent of the order field ('higher number has preference') is unfulfilled for exactly the multi-provider cases the field was added to resolve.

[advisory] the change removes the fail-fast on multiple cryptoproviders on the classpath and silently selects the highest-order one, converting a detectable misconfiguration into a silent provider downgrade. an operator who accidentally ends up with both a fips and a non-fips crypto provider on the classpath (e.g., by adding authz-client, which now ships its own meta-inf/services cryptoprovider at order 100, into a server deployment) gets no error and runs with whichever provider wins the order comparison; in a fips-compliance-required deployment the previously-loud illegalstateexception that caught this now only emits a debug-level log line nobody reads, so a non-compliant crypto stack ships silently. tie orders (defaultcryptoprovider and wildflyelytronprovider both return 200) make the winner dependent on serviceloader iteration order, which is jvm/jar-order dependent.

[advisory] asn1dertoconcatenatedrs accepts der integers of arbitrary size/sign and integertobytes silently truncates (keeps only the low qlength bytes) when the decoded r or s exceeds the expected coordinate length, and also accepts negative integers, instead of rejecting malformed signatures. signature bytes coming from an untrusted jwt are mangled rather than rejected during the concatenated-rs conversion used in es256/384/512 verification: a signature with an oversized or negative r/s is converted to a wrong-but-well-formed value and fails verification with a confusing non-security error (or, for values whose truncated form collides, relies entirely on the downstream verifier for rejection), where the keycloak defaultcryptoprovider equivalents validate lengths; anyone debugging token verification against a hostile issuer gets garbage-in behavior instead of a clean 'invalid signature encoding' rejection.

[bug] getbouncycastleprovider() returns the jvm's default keystore provider (typically sun), not a bouncycastle provider, despite the method contract and name. any caller that requests getbouncycastleprovider() to obtain bc-specific algorithms (e.g., bc pem handling, bc keystore formats) silently gets the default jdk provider and fails at runtime with nosuchalgorithmexception or missing-function errors that name the wrong provider during debugging.

[bug] dayjs(override.start.tostring()).tz(override.timezone) passes availability.timezone, which is nullable in the prisma schema, straight into .tz(); a null/undefined timezone produces a dayjs object with invalid timezone and utcoffset() of 0 (or throws, depending on plugin version), silently or catastrophically corrupting the offset arithmetic. for users whose availability.timezone is null (falling back to the default), the organizer offset is computed as 0 while the invitee offset is real, producing overrides shifted by the invitee's full offset — slots appear at wrong local times, and in plugin versions where .tz(null) throws, getslots crashes for that request.

[bug] when a date override exists for the slot's day, checkifisavailable returns true immediately via if (dateoverrideexist) return true;, bypassing the busy-time check entirely. any slot falling on a date-override day is returned as available without consulting busy, so slots overlapping existing bookings are offered and double-booking occurs on override days.

[bug] in the workinghours rejection block, const end = slotstarttime.hour() 60 + slotstarttime.minute(); duplicates the start computation instead of using slotendtime, so end > workinghour.endtime compares the slot's start minute against the working-hour end. a slot whose start is within working hours but whose end extends past the last working-hour end (e.g. a 60-minute event starting at the final hour boundary) is incorrectly rejected as outside working hours; the slot-end boundary is never actually checked.

[bug] dayjs(date.start).add(utcoffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcoffset, "minutes") compares two dayjs object instances with ===, which is always false. zero-length overrides (start === end) are never detected, so the intended 'override with no availability rejects all slots' case falls through to the other comparisons and zero-length overrides leak the day's normal working hours instead of blocking the day.

[bug] the workinghours find returns true (outside working hours) if the slot start is before any same-day workinghour block's starttime, rather than checking containment across the union of blocks. with split working hours on one day (e.g. 9-12 and 13-17), a 10:00 slot is rejected because 600 < 780 for the second block, even though it falls inside the first block — valid slots disappear.

[bug] checkifisavailable applies a single organizertimezone to every dateoverride, but the dateoverrides passed in (built at lines 408-415) carry per-user timezone values that are ignored. for team/round-robin event types with hosts in different timezones, each host's override is day-matched using the organizer's timezone instead of its own, so overrides are matched to the wrong utc day and slots are wrongly offered or withheld on override days.

[bug] dayjs(override.start.tostring()).tz(override.timezone) uses the server's local timezone when override.timezone is undefined, and parsing date.tostring() via dayjs is locale/server-dependent. on hosts running in utc while overrides were defined in another timezone (or where availability.timezone is null), the computed organizerutcoffset is wrong, shifting override working hours by the offset difference and producing incorrect slot times.

[bug] dayjs(date.start).add(utcoffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcoffset, "minutes") compares two distinct dayjs object references with ===, which is always false; the intended .issame() comparison makes the start===end special case dead code. a zero-length date override (start equals end) never takes its intended early-return path and instead falls through to the range checks, which then mark the slot unavailable for the wrong reason; the special case the author wrote cannot ever execute.

[bug] the timezone offset is negated before being applied: const utcoffset = dayjs.tz(date.start, organizertimezone).utcoffset() -1; then dayjs(date.start).add(utcoffset, "minutes") shifts the utc instant in the wrong direction (local wall time = utc + offset, but the code applies utc − offset). for an organizer in utc+6 the override's calendar day is computed 12 hours off, so a slot is matched against the wrong date's override: overrides silently fail to apply (or apply to the wrong day) for organizers east or west of utc, and the checkifisavailable override gating returns wrong availability.

[bug] when a date override exists for the slot's day and the slot falls inside the override window, the function returns true immediately via if (dateoverrideexist) return true;, skipping the subsequent busy/booking conflict check entirely. existing bookings on a date-override day are ignored, so two invitees can book the same slot — a double-booking regression that the pre-diff code (which always ran the busy check) prevented.

[bug] dayjs(override.start.tostring()) parses date.prototype.tostring() output (server-local formatting like "wed jan 01 2025 10:00:00 gmt+0000") instead of the date itself, making the offset computation depend on the server's local timezone and on string parsing of a non-iso format. on any deployment whose tz is not utc, dayjs parses the localized string differently and both organizerutcoffset and inviteeutcoffset are computed for the wrong instant, producing wrong override start/end minutes; the result also silently degrades if override.timezone is null/undefined, since dayjs.tz falls back to the host timezone.

[advisory] the new organizertimezone-dependent logic silently degrades to offset 0 (: 0) when organizertimezone is undefined, and the dateoverrides spread passes availability.timezone which is nullable — no validation or fallback to a computed organizer timezone occurs. a user/availability row with a null timezone yields utc-assumed override matching with no error or log, so misconfigured data produces subtly wrong availability that operators cannot detect; a defensive default here also means the sign/conversion bugs above hide rather than fail loudly.

[bug] the working-hours availability check computes end from slotstarttime instead of slotendtime, making end always identical to start. the condition end > workinghour.endtime can never fire based on the slot's actual end, so a slot that starts inside working hours but extends beyond workinghour.endtime is reported as available, allowing bookings past the end of the working day.

[bug] the guard dayjs(date.start).add(utcoffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcoffset, "minutes") compares two distinct dayjs object instances with ===, which is always false. the intended zero-length/equal-start-and-end override case is dead code; the branch can never trigger, so slots on such an override day fall through to the wrong availability branch instead of being handled as intended.

[bug] when a date override exists for the slot's day, checkifisavailable returns true immediately (if (dateoverrideexist) { return true; }) before ever evaluating the busy array. on any day that has a date override, existing bookings (the busy list) are ignored entirely, so slots overlapping a confirmed booking on an override day are offered as available — enabling double-booking exactly on override days, the days most likely to be manually curated.

[advisory] the override-day offset in checkifisavailable is derived from organizertimezone, while the parallel offset computation for the same overrides in packages/lib/slots.ts (line ~212) is derived from override.timezone (the availability's own timezone) — two different sources for the same semantic value. when a user's availability timezone differs from the organizer/eventtype/schedule timezone, the two computations disagree: getslots shifts the override to one day while checkifisavailable tests membership on another, so overrides are silently misclassified for multi-host or mismatched-timezone setups.

[advisory] the new organizertimezone argument is optional and its call sites pass values (schedule.timezone, userschedule?.timezone) that can be undefined, in which case checkifisavailable silently assumes utc offset 0. for any availability/schedule without a resolvable timezone, override-day detection computes offsets as 0 and slots on override days are dropped or wrongly kept, with no error signal — a silent wrong-availability failure rather than an explicit configuration gap.

[bug] checkifisavailable computes slotend from slotstarttime instead of slotendtime ('const end = slotstarttime.hour() 60 + slotstarttime.minute()'), so the end-of-slot working-hours boundary is never actually checked. a slot whose start is inside working hours but whose end spills past workinghour.endtime is treated as fully inside working hours and returned as bookable, contradicting the function's stated intent of rejecting slots outside working hours.

[bug] the date-override comparison 'dayjs(date.start).add(utcoffset,...) === dayjs(date.end).add(utcoffset,...)' compares dayjs object references with ===, which is always false. the zero-length-override guard is dead code; zero-length overrides fall through to the range checks and are handled by accidental rather than intended logic, silently deviating from the written intent.

[advisory] checkifisavailable has grown from a pure busy-conflict predicate into a date-override + working-hours filter with three nested find blocks and side-effecting dateoverrideexist mutation, a structural smell that makes the next availability change risky. the next contributor touching availability must reason about three interacting early-return paths plus a mutable flag set inside a find callback; the mutation-inside-find pattern is easy to break (e.g. reordering conditions flips dateoverrideexist) and already obscured the intent (the dead === comparison).

[bug] the zero-length-override guard compares two distinct dayjs objects with === (dayjs(date.start).add(utcoffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcoffset, "minutes")), which is always false for objects, so this branch is dead code. a date override with identical start and end never short-circuits via this check; the code falls through to the isbefore/issame and isafter checks instead. the intended zero-duration handling silently never executes, and no test in the diff exercises a zero-length override to catch it.

[bug] in the working-hours check, end is computed identically to start (const end = slotstarttime.hour() 60 + slotstarttime.minute();) — the slot's end time is never computed, so the upper bound check end > workinghour.endtime tests the slot start twice. a slot that starts inside working hours but whose duration extends past workinghour.endtime is incorrectly rejected or, more importantly, the endtime bound is meaningless — slots are judged only by their start minute against both bounds. any test asserting slot end-boundary behavior would fail; none exists in the diff.

[bug] when a slot falls inside a date override, dateoverrideexist is set to true and the function returns true at if (dateoverrideexist) return true; before the busy-times check ever runs, so bookings during a date override cannot block the slot. a user with an existing booking inside their date-override window still sees that slot offered as available; double-booking becomes possible on override days. before this change, the busy check ran for every slot.

[advisory] the new organizer-timezone offset math (dayjs.tz(date.start, organizertimezone).utcoffset() -1) treats the utc date's wall-clock fields as if they were local time in organizertimezone and then negates the offset — a sign-flip hack whose semantics differ from the dayjs(...).tz(...).utcoffset() computation in packages/lib/slots.ts for the same overrides. for availability whose timezone differs from eventtype.timezone/schedule.timezone (both are fed into organizertimezone), the date-override day matching in checkifisavailable and the slot shifting in slots.ts can disagree, producing slots attributed to the wrong override day. the single added test only covers a case the comment asserts should be unchanged, so this divergence is untested.

[bug] the zero-length-override guard compares two dayjs objects with ===, which is reference equality and always false. dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...) never evaluates to true, so a start==end date override (a fully blocked day) is never detected by this branch; the slot then falls through to the range checks where a slot inside the degenerate window is wrongly treated as available, so slots are offered on a day the organizer blocked with an all-day override.

[bug] the working-hours check computes end from slotstarttime instead of slotendtime, so end always equals start. const end = slotstarttime.hour() 60 + slotstarttime.minute(); duplicates the start computation, making end > workinghour.endtime compare the slot's start minute against the workday end; a long booking whose start is inside working hours but whose end extends past them (e.g. 30-minute slot starting 30 min before close) is not filtered out and is offered outside the organizer's working hours.

[bug] the date-override window math mixes server-local dayjs rendering with a timezone offset derived via dayjs.tz, producing different results on any server whose local timezone is not utc. dayjs(date.start) (line 106, 112, 117) renders the stored utc date in the host machine's local timezone, then adds utcoffset -1; on a server running in e.g. america/newyork every shifted boundary is off by the server offset (300 minutes), so the override-day match format('yyyy mm dd') and the inside/outside comparisons are wrong and slots on override days are offered or withheld incorrectly. the test suite (utc ci) cannot catch this.

[bug] the override offset computation calls .tz(override.timezone) on a value that is optional and may be undefined, and parses via .tostring() which is a deprecated/ambiguous dayjs parse path. timerange.timezone is declared optional in packages/types/schedule.d.ts and is only populated by the getschedule router path; any caller of getslots whose overrides lack timezone (existing consumers, seeded data) passes undefined to dayjs.tz, which resolves to the server's local timezone, giving a wrong organizerutcoffset; additionally dayjs(override.start.tostring()) parses a locale/zone-formatted string rather than the date, so the parsed value's offset is environment-dependent and the computed starttime/endtime minutes silently shift for all pre-existing callers that don't set timezone.

[advisory] when dateoverrideexist is true the function returns true immediately, skipping the busy (existing booking) intersection check entirely. a slot on a date-override day is reported available regardless of existing bookings that overlap it, so the date-override day allows double-booking; anyone relying on checkifisavailable to also consult busy for override days gets confirmed-overlapping bookings.

[advisory] the working-hours fallback uses slotstarttime.day()/hour()/minute() in utc rather than the organizer timezone used for the override check, so the day-of-week match is wrong for organizers whose local day differs from the utc day. for an organizer in utc+6 whose working hours are on their local monday evening (already utc tuesday), slotstarttime.day() matches the utc weekday, so the new out-of-working-hours guard either rejects valid slots or accepts invalid ones for any organizer offset far enough from utc to cross midnight; the previous behavior delegated day matching to getaggregateworkinghours input which was built in the right reference frame.

[bug] when a date override exists for the slot's day, checkifisavailable returns true before the busy-time check, so existing bookings are ignored on override days. on any day with a date override, the if (dateoverrideexist) { return true; } branch short-circuits past the busy.every(...) check (and the currentseats seat check has already returned), so slots are offered as available even when the organizer has a calendar booking overlapping them — inviting double bookings that the pre-diff code (busy-only path) prevented.

[bug] the slot end time in the working-hours check is computed from slotstarttime instead of slotendtime (const end = slotstarttime.hour() 60 + slotstarttime.minute();), so end > workinghour.endtime can never fire except when the start itself is past closing. a slot that starts inside working hours but ends after them (e.g., a 60-minute slot starting 16:45 against hours ending 17:00, or the last slot of a shorter workinghour interval) passes the outside-working-hours filter and is offered as bookable even though it extends past the organizer's availability.

[bug] the zero-length-override guard compares two distinct dayjs instances with === (dayjs(date.start).add(utcoffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcoffset, "minutes")), which is always false, making the branch dead code. an override whose start equals its end never short-circuits and instead falls through to the before/after window checks; combined with the dateoverrideexist early-return this silently produces 'whole day available' behavior instead of whatever the equality branch was meant to guard, and the comparison reads as intentional logic to future maintainers.

[advisory] dayjs(override.start.tostring()).tz(override.timezone) silently falls back to the server-local timezone when override.timezone is undefined, since timerange.timezone is optional in packages/types/schedule.d.ts. any call path into getslots whose dateoverrides were not annotated with timezone by this diff (getschedule annotates them, but getslots has other callers) computes organizer/invitee offsets from the deployment server's tz, producing different slot windows depending on where the code runs; a regression here surfaces only as subtly wrong availability with no error.

[bug] the public members endpoint now applies a default limit of 50 to every group, but the public group members template (group/members.hbs) gained no pagination controls, so only the first 50 members are ever fetched and rendered. group pages for groups with more than 50 members silently lose members 51+ — previously the page listed every member of manual groups (automatic groups were capped at 200); the remaining members become unreachable from the ui.

[bug] update now reads top-level params but still unconditionally executes group.visible = params[:visible] == "true", so a request using the old nested group:{...} payload has params[:visible] == nil and the group's visible column is silently flipped to false while the response reports success. during the deploy window (browsers still running the old admin js that puts group:{name, aliaslevel, visible, usernames}) and for existing api clients, every group save silently hides the group and drops its name/aliaslevel/membership changes with a 200 response.

[bug] update no longer branches on request.patch? nor reads params[:changes], so patch requests carrying changes:{add:[...], delete:[...]} return successjson without applying any membership change. existing automation that managed membership through the patch endpoint silently stops working — it keeps receiving 200 responses while group membership never changes, and patches against automatic groups now return 200 instead of the old 403 invalidaccess.

[bug] create reads params[:name] at the top level and no longer accepts usernames, so old clients posting the nested group:{name:..., usernames:...} payload get name set to '' and no initial members. existing api clients that create groups with members have their requested name and membership silently discarded — the call either fails validation on the blank name or persists an empty group, with no error indicating the payload contract changed.

[bug] addmembers calls params.require(:usernames).split(",") without type coercion, so a request whose usernames parameter is a json array raises nomethoderror (undefined method split' for array) and returns a 500 instead of a 4xx. api clients sending usernames as an array — the shape the old patch changes:{add:[...]} endpoint accepted — get an unhandled 500 from this admin endpoint rather than a validation error.

[bug] findmembers builds the request url from the live name property, which is two-way bound to the editable name text-field on the admin group form, so paginating or adding members after editing the name (before saving) queries a group name that does not exist. an admin who types a new name and then clicks next/previous or add triggers get /groups/<edited-name>/members.json, which 404s; the member list silently fails to refresh, so addmembers appears to do nothing even though the put succeeded.

[bug] offset = params[:offset].toi (and likewise limit) is passed straight into activerecord's offset/limit without clamping, so a negative value such as ?offset=-1 produces 'offset -1' sql that postgresql rejects with an error, returning a 500. any client — including anonymous visitors, since this is a public endpoint — can force a 500 on a group members page with one malformed query parameter; previously the offset param was only honored for automatic groups and ignored for manual ones.

[bug] the members action now caps every group at limit = (params[:limit] || 50).toi (previously custom groups returned all members and automatic groups 200), but the public template group/members.hbs only got {{each m in members}} — no pagination controls, route wiring, or next/previous actions were added for the public page. any group with more than 50 members, previously fully listed on the public group page, now silently shows only the first 50 members to visitors with no way to see the rest; the admin template got a pager but the public group-members route/controller/template did not.

[advisory] the admin update endpoint switched from a nested params[:group] payload (plus the patch changes[add]/[delete] path, deleted entirely) to flat params and dropped usernames handling, so an old-format caller's params[:visible] is nil and group.visible = params[:visible] == "true" evaluates to false. existing api consumers/scripts sending group[visible], group[usernames], or patch changes receive 200 success while the group's visibility is silently flipped to false and membership changes are silently dropped — the old incremental-membership api is removed with no compat path.

[bug] in the maxage cleanup loop, the batch's affected count is taken from x (rows deleted by deletebyids), so if rows are deleted between fetchids and deletebyids (e.g. a second grafana instance in ha running the same cleanup job), the batch returns affected=0 and the retry loop terminates even though ids were fetched and remaining matching rows still exist. in multi-instance deployments where each node runs the cleanup service, two instances racing on the same batch cause one to observe 0 affected rows and stop the whole maxage (and maxcount) sweep early, leaving stale annotations that are only removed on a later cycle; combined with the code comment's acknowledged under-delete, this makes cleanup completion non-deterministic per run. the loop should terminate on len(ids) == 0 (rows fetched) rather than on affected rows deleted.

[advisory] cleanup success paths log at error level and dump the full id list of every batch into the log message. every cleanup cycle emits r.log.error('annotations to clean by time', 'ids', ids, ...) and 'cleaned annotations by time' even when the operation succeeds (err is nil), so operators' error dashboards/alerts fire on routine cleanup and large batches (batch size can be 32767) flood logs with thousands of ids per cycle at 1-minute ticker frequency.

[advisory] fetchids and deletebyids run in separate sessions/transactions with no locking, so concurrent deletes/inserts between the select and the delete make affected < len(ids) silently. the comment acknowledges under-deletion for inserts, but a concurrent delete of an already-fetched id makes the batch report fewer affected rows; since untildoneorcancelled terminates on affected==0, a batch whose rows were all deleted concurrently ends the whole loop early even though qualifying rows still exist — cleanup silently does less work than the reported total implies. tolerable per the stated 'next cycle' rationale, but the loop-termination-on-zero-affected interaction means the next cycle may also see zero affected rows for the maxcount case if the remaining rows fall under the offset window.

[advisory] sendaddguestsemails sends the full attendeescheduledemail to brand-new guests whose name is the empty string (handler creates attendees with name: ""), while existing attendees get the shorter attendeeaddguestsemail. new guests receive a scheduling confirmation email addressed to a blank name and carrying a duplicate calendar invite (method request, status confirmed) for an event they never booked; if their mail client already has the event, the blank-name invite confuses the roster, and the new guests get no indication they were added by someone else rather than having booked themselves.

[bug] the permission gate computes isteamadminorowner as isteamadmin(...) && isteamowner(...), requiring the caller to be both admin and owner instead of either. a team admin who is not the owner, adding guests to their team's booking, receives forbidden even though the pr's own variable name and intent state admin-or-owner should be allowed; conversely the gate silently grants nothing to plain admins — the authorization check does not match its stated invariant.
