[advisory] backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write: authorize decrypts the whole array, nulls one slot, and rewrites the full array with a plain prisma.user.update — no transaction, no optimistic concurrency — so concurrent sign-ins validate against the same pre-update snapshot. when two requests race (e.g., an attacker replaying a code observed on a printed sheet while the owner logs in), the second write overwrites the first's consumption and resurrects the already-used code, converting a single-use credential into a reusable one with no error logged anywhere.

[bug] req.body.backupcode is used as a string without validation: a json body sending a non-string (e.g. {"backupcode": 123}) passes the truthiness guard at line 48 and throws typeerror on .replaceall, which the handler does not catch. any non-browser client that sends a numeric or structured backupcode gets an unhandled 500 with a stack trace in the logs instead of the 400 incorrectbackupcode the endpoint's error contract defines, polluting error monitoring and breaking the documented api surface.

[bug] handleenable's success path replaces the onenable() call with setstep(setupstep.displaybackupcodes), leaving the modal's only success notification wired to the backup-codes close button, so dismissing the dialog at that step via escape, the header x, or a backdrop click (all routed to onopenchange/oncancel) completes the enable server-side without ever notifying the parent. the settings ui keeps showing 2fa as disabled while the account is actually protected; when the user next clicks the switch the setup endpoint re-runs and overwrites the stored backupcodes, silently invalidating the codes the user already saved, and the parent never runs its onenable side effects (state refresh/query invalidation).

[bug] the copy button fires navigator.clipboard.writetext without awaiting it and without any rejection handler, then unconditionally shows the 'backup codes copied!' success toast before the write can complete. when the clipboard write rejects (firefox without the clipboard-write permission, unfocused document) the user is told the codes were copied when they were not, and on non-https self-hosted deployments navigator.clipboard is undefined so the handler throws a typeerror and shows no feedback at all — in both cases the user closes the dialog believing the recovery codes are saved and is locked out when they later lose the authenticator.

[bug] the backup-code branch of the disable endpoint fails by unhandled throws — a raw error on a missing calendsoencryptionkey and an unguarded symmetricdecrypt/json.parse of user.backupcodes — instead of the res.status().json({error}) envelope every other branch of this handler returns. these failures surface as non-json next.js 500s; disabletwofactormodal unconditionally calls response.json() on non-200 responses, which throws into the generic catch, so the structured incorrectbackupcode/missingbackupcodes mapping is bypassed and the user only sees 'something went wrong' — and after a calendsoencryptionkey rotation on a self-hosted instance, every backup-code disable attempt returns an opaque html 500 instead of a parseable 4xx json error.

[bug] authorize() decrypts and json.parses user.backupcodes with no guard, so a failed decrypt (rotated calendsoencryptionkey since the codes were stored) or corrupted column throws a raw crypto/parse error instead of an errorcode. the raw error message propagates as res.error to login.tsx, matches no known error code, and renders as a generic 'something went wrong' — a user attempting backup-code login on a rotated-key instance gets an opaque, unactionable failure on every attempt with nothing distinguishing it in logs from a real auth failure.

[bug] backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read–decrypt–null–re-encrypt–write with no transaction or concurrency guard, so two concurrent sign-ins each read the full code array and last-write-wins resurrects a code the other request already consumed. a user signing in from two devices in quick succession (or a replaying holder of a shoulder-surfed code) double-spends a code the product's own instructions promise 'can be used exactly once', silently breaking the single-use invariant the feature states to users.

[bug] the missingbackupcodes message instructs 'please generate them in your settings', but no code path in this product can generate backup codes for an account with 2fa already enabled — codes are only written by the setup endpoint inside the enable flow — and a user receiving this error on the login page cannot reach settings without logging in first. the exact users this error targets — locked-out users without backup codes on the login screen, and disable-modal users sitting in settings — are directed to perform an action that is impossible from where they stand, leaving both audiences with dead-end recovery guidance that masks the absence of any recovery path.

[bug] when all ten codes have been consumed, the stored column is the json array [null×10] rather than null (consumption writes backupcodes[index] = null), so the !user.backupcodes guard never fires and further attempts throw incorrectbackupcode instead of missingbackupcodes. a user who exhausted their codes and lost their authenticator is told 'backup code is incorrect' on every attempt instead of learning that no codes remain, so they keep retrying dead codes instead of seeking account recovery.

stored xss: rss/atom feed content is imported and served completely unsanitized — pollfeed.rb feeds raw item html to topicembed.rb which sets cookmethod: rawhtml, post.rb's cook returns raw verbatim with no sanitize pipeline, and it is rendered via raw post.cooked in best.html.erb:23 and as cooked throughout the forum ui; anyone who publishes, compromises, or mitms the feed (fetched over plain open()) can execute arbitrary script on the discourse origin and steal viewer sessions.
the importremote readability path whitelists tags but not url schemes, so <a href='javascript:...'> survives sanitization as an additional live xss vector.

app/models/topicembed.rb:13 interpolates url unescaped into a single-quoted href after only a prefix check (url =~ /^https?\:\/\//); urls legally containing a single quote (e.g. slugs like /it's-alive.html) terminate the attribute early and corrupt the stored html, and a crafted feed link such as http://host/x' onmouseover='... performs attribute injection that lands as live markup since the post is rawhtml-cooked (second xss path).

topicembed.rb:31-34 update path assumes embed.post is non-nil when passing it to postrevisor.new; nothing removes topicembeds rows when a topic/post is destroyed, so an orphaned embed makes postrevisorinitialize nomethoderror mid-loop inside pollfeed's rss.items.each with retry: false — every feed item after the orphaned one is never imported every hour and the embed request for that url fails persistently, silently degrading the feed import.

lib/topicretriever.rb:26-29: $redis.setnx and $redis.expire are not atomic; if the process dies between them the retrieved:<url> key has no ttl and lives forever, permanently throttling that embed url so performretrieve never runs again and the page shows 'loading discussion...' indefinitely. use a single set ... ex 60 nx.

topicembed.rb:64-76 (absolutizeurls) mangles protocol-relative urls: //cdn.example.com/img.jpg passes startwith?('/') and then sub(/^\/+/, '') strips both leading slashes, producing http://<embed host>/cdn.example.com/img.jpg — a broken path on the wrong host, breaking images/links in imported posts.

app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17: the origin check is substring-based (discourseurl.indexof(e.origin) === -1) rather than exact equality, so any origin that is a substring-prefix of the forum url (e.g. http://fo matching http://forum.example.com) can post discourse-resize messages and drive the iframe height arbitrarily; the check should be e.origin === discourseurl.

embedcontroller.rb:9-16 / topicretriever.rb:15-18: embedurl is never validated as a string — params.require(:embedurl) happily returns an array/hash (?embedurl[]=x), and uri(@embedurl) in invalidhost? raises typeerror (not uri::invalidurierror) which escapes the rescue, so each such request enqueues a job that crashes on its first statement and burns through sidekiq retries — anonymous-triggerable job churn. validate it's a string before enqueueing.

embedcontroller.rb: the referer gate relies on the spoofable, fully client-controlled request.referer header, so it stops browsers but not scripted callers; any request with a faked referer and a novel embedurl enqueues retrievetopic, and with feedpollingenabled each such job synchronously re-polls and re-parses the entire feed (jobs::pollfeed.new.execute({})) plus a readability fetch — enabling anonymous queue-flooding / forced-feed-refresh amplification. a global rate limit on the controller is needed.

lib/tasks/disqus.thor:143: the importer rewrite from postcreator.new(..., createdat: date.parse(t[:createdat]), category: categoryid) to topicembed.importremote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title]) silently drops both timestamps and category support — imported disqus topics are dated 'now' (reordering listing pages and breaking embed dates), always land in uncategorized, and the -c cli option was removed; importremote should at least forward createdat.
there is no mutex between the scheduled and inline poll paths, and if the inline poll runs longer than the 60s throttle ttl, concurrent jobs re-enter and duplicate the work.

unbounded remote download into memory with no size/time policy: app/models/topicembed.rb:48 (open(url).read) and pollfeed.rb:29 buffer the full remote body into a string and parse it (readability + nokogiri, several times the document size in memory) with no max-size cap, bounded only by open-uri's default 60s timeouts; any large resource served on the embeddablehost will be fully downloaded and parsed in a sidekiq worker.

no enqueue-time dedupe and no negative caching on the retrieve path (app/controllers/embedcontroller.rb:15, app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:8-10, lib/topicretriever.rb:21-33): every embed impression enqueues a job, so a page whose topic can never be imported floods the sidekiq queue with near-duplicate jobs whose only work is a failed setnx; the 60s throttle only applies inside job execution and is set before retrieval regardless of outcome, so permanently failing urls (404, readability-empty, fetch error) are re-fetched up to once per minute indefinitely as long as they have viewers.
the redis setnx/expire throttle operations are non-atomic: a crash between them throttles that url forever.

force: true was added to the already-shipped migration db/migrate/20131223171005createtoptopics.rb:3 — inert day-to-day since normal deploys skip recorded migrations, but any db:migrate:redo or reset against an environment with data silently drops toptables... toptopics; reads like a local-dev convenience accidentally committed, and the same pattern in the brand-new createtopicembeds migration (20131217174004) sets a bad precedent.

ssrf via redirect: the host allowlist is checked only on the initial url (lib/topicretriever.rb:15), but the actual fetches via open-uri (app/models/topicembed.rb:36, app/jobs/scheduled/pollfeed.rb:29) follow cross-origin redirects, so an open redirect on the embeddable host can pivot the discourse server to fetch internal endpoints (169.254.169.254, localhost services) whose content is then readable via the public topic/embed; the referer gate is a forgeable header, so no on-host presence is even needed to trigger retrieval
no fetch timeout or size cap is set on the open() fetches, so retrieval/poll jobs can be hung or oom'd

pollfeed crashes on common rss 2.0 feeds: i.content.scrub at app/jobs/scheduled/pollfeed.rb:35 raises nomethoderror because simplerss exposes rss 2.0's content:encoded as contentencoded and plain rss items have no content; with sidekiqoptions retry: false (:12) the hourly import dies mid-feed and items after the crash point are never imported, silently breaking the documented rss/atom support for the most common feeds (wordpress et al.); stringscrub also requires ruby >= 2.1

absolutizeurls corrupts protocol-relative urls: the href.startwith?('/') check at app/models/topicembed.rb:61-72 treats //cdn.example.com/img.png as a root-relative path and, after stripping leading slashes, produces http://<embeddable-host>/cdn.example.com/img.png, breaking links and images in every feed containing // urls

embed url matching is a byte-exact string contract across three independently produced values — the stored embedurl (app/models/topicembed.rb:78-80), the client snippet's discourseembedurl (app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:7), and the feed's i.link (app/jobs/scheduled/pollfeed.rb:32) — with no normalization layer anywhere, so any divergence (trailing slash, scheme, www, query params) means the embed never matches and the user sees the loading page reloading every 30s indefinitely while the server re-enqueues retrievals

the retrievetopic job is enqueued before any validation of user input (app/controllers/embedcontroller.rb:15) — the host allowlist runs only later inside the job (lib/topicretriever.rb:15) and the referer gate is a forgeable header, so an anonymous client with a forged referer: http://<embeddable-host>/ can enqueue unbounded jobs (varying embedurl to bypass the per-url throttle), and each first-time retrieval synchronously re-runs the entire feed import inline

the embeddablehost setting is silently config-sensitive: it must be a bare host string — an admin entering https://example.com or a host with a port never string-matches uri(...).host, and the feature fails silently with no validation or documentation of the expected format

pollfeed's rss.items.each loop has no begin/rescue around topicembed.import, so a single bad feed item (nil field, bad url, postcreator failure, recordnotunique race) permanently poisons all feed importing — the job aborts, and with retry: false and hourly scheduling the next run dies on the same item, so later items are never imported; the unused feedkey also leaves no way to skip or flag a bad feed.

topicretrieverperformretrieve runs the entire feed poll inline in every retrieve job with no lock: jobs::pollfeed.new.execute({}) fetches and imports the whole feed synchronously once per unique embedurl per 60s, effectively ddos-ing the embeddable host, racing the check-then-insert in topicembed.import into activerecord::recordnotunique exceptions, and failing retrieve jobs on any pollfeed failure.

external feed content is stored and served as unsanitized raw html: the rss path has no sanitization at all before content becomes cooked, the readability path whitelists tags but permits javascript: urls in href/src attributes, and the feed-supplied url is interpolated unescaped into html — a malicious or hijacked feed yields stored script running on the discourse origin.

outbound http calls (open(sitesetting.feedpollingurl) and open(url).read) have no explicit opentimeout/readtimeout, no redirect policy, and no response-size cap, so a slow feed server ties up sidekiq workers and a huge response is slurped wholesale into memory before being persisted with no post-length bound.

/embed/best enqueues a retrievetopic background job on every request with no rate limiting — the referer host check in ensureembeddable is a client-controlled, trivially spoofed header, so varying the embedurl param generates unbounded queue growth; the 60s redis throttle limits fetch frequency, not enqueue volume.

no lifecycle cleanup for topicembeds: nothing deletes a topicembed when its topic or post is deleted, leaving a stale topicid that makes topicview.new 404, permanently blocking re-creation for that url because performretrieve short-circuits on the existing embed, and causing a nomethoderror when postrevisor.new(post) receives a nil post.

the embed loading page reloads forever with no failure state or retry cap, and failure is silent on both client and operator side: retrieval silently no-ops when embedbyusername is unset or the user was deleted, when the host doesn't match, or when retrieval fails, and no poll/retrieve path logs anything — with no circuit breaker, a permanently-bad embed url is re-fetched once a minute indefinitely.

feed item parsing assumes i.content exists, but simple-rss exposes namespaced content:encoded as contentencoded, so rss 2.0 description-only feeds raise nomethoderror on i.content.scrub, and combined with the missing error isolation one such item kills the entire poll.

the setnx/expire throttle in topicretriever is not atomic: if the worker dies between the two calls, the retrieved:<url> key persists with no ttl and that url is throttled permanently until manual redis intervention; should use set(key, "1", nx: true, ex: 60).

importremote fetches the url before validating its scheme: open(url) executes before the ^https?:// check in import, so a schemeless string like //eviltrout.com/x passes invalidhost? and hits kernelopen's local-file semantics instead of http.

<%- end if %> in app/views/embed/best.html.erb is a typo (presumably meant <%- end %>) that only renders correctly by accident of erb's chunk emission order, and is one template edit away from a semantics change or a syntaxerror that breaks every embed render with a topic present.

createtable ..., force: true in production migrations (createtopicembeds, createtoptopics) can silently drop any pre-existing table without warning if the migration is re-run, and modifying the already-shipped createtoptopics migration is a no-op on already-migrated databases that only adds risk.

the disqus import loop now performs network i/o with no rescue: topicembed.importremote(user, t[:link], ...) inside parser.threads.each means a single 404 or timeout on an old export permalink aborts the entire cli run partway through.

jobs::pollfeed's core feed-to-topic pipeline has zero behavioral coverage: the spec stubs pollfeed itself, so simplerss parsing, the link fallback, cgi.unescapehtml(i.content.scrub), the missing-user early return, and the handoff to topicembed.import are never executed, and no test anywhere verifies a feed item produces a topic/post. this untested path hides a latent crash: i.content.scrub (pollfeed.rb:35) raises nomethoderror on feeds/items lacking a content element (common in plain rss 2.0 feeds with only <description>), and since the job is sidekiqoptions retry: false, it dies silently every hour.

the embed controller's success-path tests verify mock interactions, not behavior: 'tells the topic retriever to work' asserts topicretriever.new/retrieve are called instead of asserting jobs.enqueue(:retrievetopic, ...) args, and topicretriever.expects(:new) matches any arguments; 'creates a topic view' mocks topicview.new returning nil. with view rendering off, nothing verifies the best template renders posts or that the loading template renders on the no-embed path — a broken template (e.g. @topicview.posts on a stale/deleted topic id) ships green. no renderviews/integration spec exists for either new template.

[bug] legacy.create runs concurrently on the shared obj while the caller may serialize or mutate it, causing a data race on the object returned to the client. the goroutine calls d.legacy.create(ctx, obj, ...) after the function has returned obj to the caller; legacy storage implementations and the client serializer can mutate obj (e.g., set resourceversion) concurrently with the response write, producing torn responses or -race failures under load.

[bug] on the update storage-error path, the failure is recorded with recordlegacyduration instead of recordstorageduration, mislabeling unified-storage failures as legacy failures. dashboards and rollout gates that track storage vs legacy latency/error rates read wrong signals, so a unified-storage outage is misattributed to the legacy side and can trigger wrong mode-rollback decisions during the migration.

[bug] the deletecollection legacy goroutine records its duration with recordstorageduration instead of recordlegacyduration. legacy delete-collection latency/errors are counted in the storage series, corrupting the migration metrics used to decide when it is safe to advance dual-writer modes.

[bug] legacy writes in create are fired-and-forgotten in a goroutine whose only failure handling is a metric recording — the error is never logged and never surfaced to the user, so the api returns success while the legacy copy silently fails. in mode 3 the contract is 'write to both storages'; a legacy create failure (e.g. the 10s timeout, or legacy validation rejecting the mutated object) leaves the object present in unified storage but absent in legacy storage with no log line beyond a counter, so the drift is invisible and unfixable without noticing a metric.

[bug] the update goroutine passes the raw objinfo to d.legacy.update instead of the updatewrapper wrapping the resolved object that the old code built, so legacy storage re-resolves updatedobject from a nil/absent old object it cannot see. objinfo.updatedobject(ctx, old) requires the old object from unified storage; legacy storage has no access to that resolution, so legacy updates are computed from the wrong basis (or fail validation), producing divergent legacy data — a silent partial write on every mode 3 update.

[bug] the background legacy goroutine derives its context from the request context (context.withtimeoutcause(ctx, ...)), which is cancelled when the http handler returns, so the 10-second timeout almost never protects the legacy write. the legacy create/update/delete in the goroutine is aborted with 'context canceled' as soon as the response is flushed, meaning the async legacy write fails spuriously and only shows up as a failing legacy-duration metric — the dual-write guarantee is effectively best-effort-by-accident.

[bug] on the storage.update error path d.recordlegacyduration(true, ...) is called where the storage duration metric is intended, mislabeling the failed operation. unified-storage update failures are counted in the legacy metric series, corrupting both metrics and any mode-migration health reporting built on them.

[bug] the delete goroutine swallows legacy delete errors entirely (no log, metric only), and the pre-existing behavior of ignoring apierrors.isnotfound is gone, so a legacy delete of an already-absent object is recorded as a failure with no distinguishing signal. every delete of an object missing in legacy storage emits a failure metric and zero diagnostic output; operators see rising legacy-delete failure rates that are partly benign notfound noise with no way to tell real failures from expected misses.

[bug] destroy calls host.destroy on a possibly-nil record when the id does not exist, raising nomethoderror and returning a 500. double-delete of the same host (e.g. retry after a timeout) produces a 500 instead of idempotent success or a 404.

the unsubscribe url is a state-mutating, token-less get with toggle semantics (watching/tracking to regular, regular/muted to muted): corporate mail scanners and link unfurlers (mimecast/proofpoint-style) prefetch the url and each fetch flips the level, so a scanner pass can downgrade watching to regular and a second fetch (or scanner plus user click) fully mutes the topic with zero user action; re-clicking an old link after re-watching downgrades again, and concurrent gets race so one toggle is lost. needs a confirmation step, post, or per-user token.

the end state contradicts what the email and confirmation page promise: the email footer says 'to stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here' and the page unconditionally renders 'you will stop receiving notifications for <title>', but for watching/tracking users (the majority of recipients) the code sets regular, which still sends notifications for replies, mentions and quotes; only users already at regular/muted end up muted. should either go straight to muted or render the message from the actual resulting level.

the unsubscribelink locale now hard-requires %{unsubscribeurl} for every opting-in mailer: email::messagebuilderhtmlpart renders i18n.t('unsubscribelink', templateargs) for any email built with addunsubscribelink: true, and i18n raises missinginterpolationargument when the key is absent, so any other caller (e.g. digest mailer or plugins) that doesn't supply unsubscribeurl now fails to build/send the email. all addunsubscribelink callers need auditing.

tu.save! bypasses topicuser.change, so no messagebus notificationlevelchange message is published to /topic/<id>: every other path that changes notificationlevel publishes it, meaning a tab that already has the topic open keeps showing the stale watching/tracking state (button and reason text) until a manual refresh, and the codebase now has two divergent write paths for the same state. using topicuser.change fixes this and the missing-row case together.

state-changing get on an email-embedded url: notificationlevel is mutated on a plain get (app/controllers/topicscontroller.rb:98-115) with no confirmation step or csrf token, making it csrf-able against logged-in users via to silently mute topics, and exposing it to email scanner/prefetcher probe traffic on the site's highest-volume mail class

the new unsubscribe route (topicsunsubscribe) permanently mutates topicuser.notificationlevel via a plain get request authenticated only by the session cookie — no per-user token, no confirmation step, exempt from rails csrf protection, and with checkxhr explicitly skipped — so any external site can embed and silently change the notification level of every logged-in visitor
email link scanners and av gateways that prefetch get urls will trigger the unsubscribe mutation for users who merely opened the email without clicking the link

the unsubscribe action is a toggle rather than an idempotent unsubscribe: a page refresh or second fetch escalates regular → muted, so the user's final state depends on how many times the link was fetched

topicuser.findby result is dereferenced without a nil check (tu.notificationlevel immediately after findby), raising nomethoderror and returning a 500 when the logged-in user has no topicuser row (e.g., forwarded email, shared browser, different account) — the controller also bypasses topicuser.change, which is the method that creates the row if missing and publishes the notificationlevelchange messagebus event that open tabs rely on

the shared unsubscribelink locale key / email::messagebuilder contract was changed to interpolate %{unsubscribeurl}, but templateargs only contains unsubscribeurl if the caller passes it — any mail built with addunsubscribelink: true + htmloverride without the new opt now raises i18n::missinginterpolationargument at build time and fails to send entirely; the pr updates only one caller with no guard or fallback for other core/plugin mailers using this public builder option

the unsubscribe copy overpromises: the action only drops watching/tracking users to regular, a level that still notifies and emails the user on replies and mentions, so users who click 'stop receiving notifications' keep receiving notifications for that topic — only a second fetch reaches muted
direct tu.save! bypasses topicuser.change, so there is no upsert and no notificationlevelchange messagebus publish, leaving other open tabs of the topic out of sync

the beforefilter configuration for :unsubscribe needs verification: if it is in an except: list rather than ensureloggedin ... only:, currentuser is nil for anonymous clicks and every logged-out click 500s at currentuser.id

the unsubscribe email link is a state-changing get with no token or confirmation that permanently mutates notificationlevel; mail-gateway link scanners/prefetchers and cross-site embedding (e.g., with no samesite cookies) can silently mute a user's topic, and revisiting the url keeps stepping the level down (watching → regular → muted)

the unsubscribe step-down logic maps watching/tracking to regular, which still emails the user when replied to/mentioned/quoted in that topic, contradicting the email and landing page text claiming they will stop receiving notifications; watching users must click twice to actually stop notifications

the client route topic-unsubscribe.js.es6 shows unconditional success text ('you will stop receiving notifications for title') even though no server mutation occurs when the url is reached via client-side navigation; the success text should be conditioned on the actual details.notificationlevel

the per-topic unsubscribe link interpolated into emails is site-relative: topicurl returns a relative path and nothing absolutizes the new unsubscribeurl key (unlike userpreferencesurl, which messagebuilder absolutizes), so the mailer likely interpolates '/t/slug/99/unsubscribe' into the email cta — an anchor that cannot resolve in a mail client, leaving the feature's primary cta dead.

the unsubscribe behavior contradicts the email/page copy: watching/tracking users are only stepped down to regular, which still sends notifications on replies/mentions, despite the copy saying 'you will stop receiving notifications' — and no test encodes the intended level-transition matrix that would have forced a decision on intended behavior.
the unsubscribe get endpoint is non-idempotent: each repeat get of the same url mutates state again, stepping watching → regular → muted across refreshes or repeat clicks.

new route topicunsubscribe is declared after the topic resource whose child fromparamsnear (/t/:slug/:id/:nearpost) already matches /t/slug/123/unsubscribe; ember's router recognizes in declaration order, so the unsubscribe route never activates and the new route, controller, view, template, and scss are unreachable dead code, while email click-throughs trigger a bogus post-stream refresh with a non-numeric nearpost

the unsubscribe action hand-rolls mutation (findby + attribute assignment + save!) instead of using the canonical topicuser.change api, duplicating logic, skipping the messagebus publish so other open tabs never learn the level changed, embedding toggle business logic in the controller, and converting validation failures into 500s

breaking api contract changes shipped with no compatibility consideration: the members response changed from a bare array to a {members, meta} envelope and admin create/update params changed from nested group[...] to flat params, so external consumers (plugins, admin-api clients) break silently, and an old-style put /admin/groups/:id now finds the params nil and silently resets visible to false while ignoring the intended change (groupscontroller.rb:30-33, admin/groupscontroller.rb:22-40)

unbounded limit on the public members endpoint: (params[:limit] || 50).toi has no maximum clamp, so any client can request /groups/:name/members?limit=1000000 and the new meta contract echoes it back; the old hole existed only for automatic groups but this pr extends the parameter to every group (groupscontroller.rb:24)

the new admin group template renders raw {{usercount}} instead of using the existing usercountdisplay presentation logic (whose documented purpose is to hide the ugly zero), so empty groups display (0) and 0/0 pagination, and the same datum now has two divergent display paths that will drift (admin/templates/group.hbs:14 vs group.js:12-16)

inconsistent group-name normalization between create and update: create strips whitespace via (params[:name] || '').strip but update assigns group.name = params[:name] with no strip, so the same input ' bob ' is accepted on create but rejected or stored dirty on update; normalization belongs in one place such as the model (admin/groupscontroller.rb:24 vs :40)

admin-group.js.es6: totalpages = math.floor(usercount / limit) + 1 is off-by-one when usercount % limit == 0 (100 members, limit 50 yields totalpages 3 when only 2 pages exist), so showinglast fails on the real last page and 'next' stays enabled; correct math is math.ceil(usercount/limit) (or floor((usercount-1)/limit)+1).

admin/groupscontroller.rb create only assigns name and visible, silently discarding the aliaslevel sent by the rewritten asjson(): new groups persist with aliaslevel 0 while the form keeps displaying the admin's selection, so the save appears green while the real value was dropped, and the divergence persists until a second save. the new .create spec suite covers only name-stripping and asserts nothing about aliaslevel, hiding this silent pass.

usernames is singleton ember controller state that is never reset — setupcontroller only sets the model and addmembers deliberately doesn't clear the input — so text typed while editing group a remains when navigating to group b, and clicking 'add' then adds those users to the wrong group (membership grants permissions); after a successful add, the retained text also invites a duplicate re-submission. regression from the old code that derived usernames from members per model.

groupscontroller.rb addmembers is a silent no-op for unknown usernames: the user.findbyusername guard skips non-matching names with no error, no report, and successjson, so a typo'd username (also whitespace-padded names, since split(',') isn't trimmed) 'succeeds' while nothing happened, leaving the admin zero feedback as the ui reloads an unchanged list.
the public get /groups/:name/members response changes from a bare serialized array to {members, meta}, silently breaking every existing consumer of that endpoint (plugins, scripts, mobile clients).

admin update unconditionally assigns group.visible = params[:visible] == 'true' with no .present? guard (unlike aliaslevel), and admin create/update now require flat top-level params instead of group: {...}, so any legacy admin-api caller using the old payload shape that doesn't send top-level visible silently flips the group to invisible while getting a 200 back.
eviction can remove the root-span payload while hasrootspankey still marks the segment as rooted, causing flushed segments to lack their root span.
reducing redirect traversal from 10,000 to 1,000 breaks joining traces with redirect/nesting chains over 1,000, leaving their spans in separate buffers.

[bug] processbatch reads val["endtimestampprecise"] unconditionally, so any span event on the topic produced by an old producer (or lacking the field) raises keyerror and kills processing of the batch. during a rolling deploy, messages serialized before this code ships crash the consumer batch instead of being skipped; use of .get with a default (e.g. timestamp) would avoid hard data-loss/ poisoning of the partition.

[bug] the redirect-resolution loop limit is silently lowered from 10000 to 1000, so parent chains deeper than 1000 now exit the loop without joining, a correctness regression the removed comment explicitly acknowledged as a known tradeoff. deep segment trees longer than 1000 no longer merge into the correct set; their spans land in a stale setkey and are flushed attached to the wrong parent, with no metric or log marking the bail-out.

[advisory] the maxsegmentspans guard (count-based skip with its own metric 'spans.buffer.flushsegments.segmentspancountexceeded') was deleted and replaced only by the byte-size check, removing the count-exceeded safety path. segments composed of many tiny spans now pass the byte check but can exceed the previously enforced span-count ceiling; the deleted metric disappears, so that failure signal is gone from dashboards.

[bug] optimizedcursorpaginator extends basepaginator but its getresult dereferences attributes (self.maxlimit, self.buildqueryset, self.counthits, self.desc, self.key, self.postqueryfilter) that are defined on cursorpaginator, not basepaginator; instantiating or calling getresult on this class raises attributeerror. the first real request through the optimized path fails with attributeerror instead of paginating, meaning the new endpoint branch was never exercised.

[advisory] the redirect-chain walk limit is silently lowered from 10000 to 1000 with no requirement or comment, halving the maximum segment-tree depth that can be correctly joined. traces with parent-redirect chains deeper than 1000 (previously supported, per the deleted comment) will fail to join to their true segment root, misattributing spans — a behavior regression hidden inside an unrelated pr.

[bug] processbatch now requires val["endtimestampprecise"] unconditionally, but the ingest-spans schema/producer was not changed in this diff to guarantee the field. any in-flight or legacy message lacking the key (e.g. during a rolling deploy, or from producers not updated to the new schema) raises keyerror in the consumer, poisoning the batch and stalling span ingestion until offsets are skipped.

[bug] the new eviction path zpopmin's the lowest-score (oldest endtimestamp) members whenever the set exceeds 1000, permanently deleting those spans from the buffer with no metric, log, or flush. on high-volume traces exceeding 1000 spans per set, older spans are silently discarded and never written to storage — unbounded trace fan-out now causes unreported data loss rather than the previous explicit too-large-segment skip path.

[bug] the redirect-chain loop limit was cut from 10000 to 1000 while deleting the comment that documented the tradeoff, with no handling for chains longer than 1000. legitimate redirect chains deeper than 1000 (previously joined, even if slowly) now terminate the loop with setspanid unresolved, so spans attach to the wrong segment parent — a silent correctness regression for deep traces.

[bug] the maxsegmentspans guard was deleted, leaving only the byte-size cap, so a segment composed of many tiny spans now accumulates without any span-count bound. a segment with millions of one-byte-ish payloads stays under maxsegmentbytes and is materialized fully in payloads[key], creating unbounded memory materialization in the flusher where the previous code skipped the segment by count.

[bug] optimizedcursorpaginator subclasses basepaginator but calls self.maxlimit, self.key, self.buildqueryset, self.counthits, self.postqueryfilter, and self.desc, which are attributes/methods of cursorpaginator, not basepaginator, so any request with optimizedpagination=true crashes with attributeerror instead of paginating. every audit-log request that activates the new 'optimized' path returns a 500; the feature the diff adds has never been executable as written.

[bug] the negative-offset branch slices queryset with a negative start index (queryset[startoffset:stop] with startoffset < 0), which django orm forbids (assertionerror: 'negative indexing is not supported'), so any advanced-features request with a negative cursor offset raises instead of returning data. the advertised 'negative offset support' path 500s on first use; the comment claiming 'the underlying django orm properly handles negative slicing automatically' is factually wrong and the code was never run against this path.

[bug] processbatch now requires val["endtimestampprecise"] with no default, so any kafka span message produced before this deploy (or by an old producer during a rolling deploy) that lacks the field crashes the consumer with keyerror. rolling-deploy skew: old producers and new consumers cannot coexist; every pre-upgrade message in the ingest-spans topic raises keyerror and stalls/blocks partition processing until offsets are skipped or the field is backfilled.

[bug] the eviction path (zpopmin when spancount > 1000) silently deletes the oldest span payloads from the buffered segment, replacing the previous explicit 'too large segment' skip-and-metric behavior in loadsegmentdata with silent data loss at insert time. for segments exceeding 1000 spans, older spans are permanently evicted before flush, so flushed trace data is silently incomplete; the deleted maxsegmentspans guard and its 'segmentspancountexceeded' metric in buffer.py mean operators lose both the data and the signal that limits were hit, without explicit human acceptance of the data-loss tradeoff.

new integration test testintegrationbeyonddevicelimit sets updatedat but not createdat in the device literal, writing 0001-01-01 00:00:00 into createdat, which is outside mysql's datetime range (starts at 1000-01-01) and should fail under mysql integration ci even though sqlite/postgres accept it locally.

device identity is attacker-mintable, enabling quota-exhaustion lockout (anonimpl/impl.go tagdevice/device-id derivation + anonstore/database.go createorupdatedevice): device ids derive from client-controlled inputs (user-agent/ip) with no rate limiting on new device creation, so a single unauthenticated attacker can fill the entire devicelimit quota in minutes with unique uas and hold all slots indefinitely with cheap keep-alive requests (rows held 30 days), causing every legitimate new anonymous visitor to be rejected with errdevicelimitreached — a fail-closed one-actor kill switch for anonymous access
the independent 2-minute context.background() timeout for device tagging was removed, so a slow query or exhausted connection pool can stall anonymous requests up to pool/request timeouts

check-then-act race in createorupdatedevice (database.go:108-115): countdevices and the insert run on separate sessions with no transaction, select ... for update, advisory lock, or constraint, so concurrent requests all observe count < devicelimit and all insert, letting the device limit overrun by the burst size and making enforcement only correct for serial traffic

persistent anonymous-lockout vector: device ids are client-controlled (cookie/header-supplied), so an unauthenticated attacker can fabricate device ids to exhaust the limit and deny service to genuinely new anonymous devices for up to 30 days (until rows age out or deletedevicesolderthan cleans up); there is no rate limiting, challenge, or eviction for garbage devices on this externally reachable boundary.

the device limit is not enforced atomically — count-then-insert race: countdevices and the subsequent insert/update in anonstore/database.go are separate, non-transactional statements, so concurrent first-time requests from distinct devices all observe count < devicelimit and all insert, overshooting the configured limit (potentially far beyond it under burst/bot traffic); no row lock, transaction, or unique-slot mechanism guards the check.

mysql rowsaffected semantics can produce a false "device limit reached" for an existing, in-window device: go-sql-driver/mysql reports rows changed, not matched (no clientfoundrows), so if the update sets identical clientip/useragent/updatedat (e.g., same-second re-tag with same ip/ua across pods, since the 29-min cache is per-instance and mysql datetime truncates sub-second precision), rowsaffected() returns 0 and a legitimate device is blocked; postgres/sqlite count matched rows so behavior diverges across supported databases and sqlite integration tests can't catch it.

a required (non-optional) property was added to the published grafanaconfig interface: anonymousdevicelimit: number | undefined uses | undefined instead of ?, so any external implementer constructing a grafanaconfig-typed object in @grafana/data now fails type-check unless they add the key; additionally the type never matches the actual wire format since the go dto (frontendsettingsdto, no omitempty) always emits an integer (0 = unlimited).

device limit check is not atomic (toctou): createorupdatedevice (database.go ~103-118) performs countdevices(...) as a standalone statement and then separately performs the upsert when count < devicelimit, with no transaction, row locking, or db-side constraint tying the insert to the count, so concurrent cache-miss requests can all observe count < limit and all insert, overshooting the limit by roughly the number of in-flight requests

updatedevice (database.go ~89-94) treats rowsaffected() == 0 as errdevicelimitreached, but on mysql rowcount() reports rows changed rather than rows matched (unless clientfoundrows is set in the dsn), so an update that matches a row but sets identical values (e.g., two instances handling parallel requests from the same device in the same second) yields 0 affected rows and spuriously rejects a legitimate, active, returning device with an auth failure

updatedevice treats rowsaffected == 0 as the sole signal for errdevicelimitreached, causing false hard auth failures for legitimate, under-limit devices: mysql changed-rows semantics (clientfoundrows not set in the dsn) make a concurrent same-second re-tag of the same device a no-op update returning 0 rows (very reachable on cold-cache page-load bursts once the limit is saturated), and the between updatedat - 30d and updatedat + 1min window is computed from client-supplied device.updatedat rather than db time, so >1min clock skew between grafana instances yields 0 rows and a false 'limit reached'; the only new test (testintegrationbeyonddevicelimit) covers the reject path, not these false-positive or update-success paths (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:72-110)

toctou race in device-limit enforcement: countdevices and the subsequent create/update run in separate sessions with no transaction, locking, or constraint tying the insert to the count, so n concurrent requests from new devices (or bursts across multiple instances) can all read count < limit and all insert, pushing the device count above the configured cap — needs a single transaction or dialect-appropriate conditional upsert covering count+write (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:112-121)

unauthenticated device-id stuffing turns the cap into a lockout primitive with db amplification: device ids are client-supplied (header/cookie) and unvalidated, and tagging requires no credentials or rate limiting, so an attacker can send devicelimit cheap requests with random device ids to fill the table and cause hard auth failures for every new (or 30-day-expired) anonymous visitor for up to 30 days, effectively closing a public dashboard to new users; additionally, rejected devices are not negatively cached, so every blocked request still costs a count + update round-trip, amplifying db load — needs rate limiting, negative caching of rejections, or a soft handling path (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:112-121, client.go:45-47)

[bug] narrowing cachemu in buildindex to only guard the final cache insertion removes the serialization that previously protected the whole build, so concurrent buildindex calls for the same namespacedresource can run simultaneously against the same file-backed directory (bleve.new on an already-created path errors, and any cache read outside the lock races with the b.cache[key] = idx write, which can panic on concurrent map access). two concurrent index builds for one tenant (e.g., a full rebuild racing an event-driven rebuild) either fail with 'index already exists' from bleve.new on the shared dir, or both construct an index and the loser's open index handle is leaked when the winner overwrites b.cache[key]; under contention the unlocked cache lookup can also trigger a fatal concurrent-map-read panic in the storage server process.

[bug] addguests.handler loads the booking with no status filter and bookinglistitem adds the 'additional guests' action to the base menu unconditionally, so guests can be added to cancelled or still-pending bookings. new guests of a cancelled booking receive an ics request with status:confirmed plus a 'guests added' email for a meeting that does not exist, updatecalendarattendees mutates the calendar entry of a cancelled event, and for pending bookings guests are told the event is confirmed before the organizer has accepted it.

[bug] for event types with seatspertimeslot the handler creates attendee rows directly with no capacity check and no attendeeseatreference, so guests added through this endpoint exceed the booked seat count and exist outside the seat-reference model the seats feature is built on. a seated booking already at capacity gains additional attendees (overbooking the time slot, since seat availability is derived from booking attendees), and seats-driven logic that reads each attendee's seat reference encounters attendees without one.

[bug] the mutation's onsuccess closes the dialog and resets the email list but never calls setisinvalidemail(false), so after a failed validation followed by a successful add, the red 'emails must be unique and valid' banner is still rendered the next time the dialog is opened. the user reopening the add guests dialog sees a validation error above an empty, valid form until they cancel or submit again; the banner is also never cleared while the user corrects the emails after a failed attempt.

[advisory] sendaddguestsemails failures are caught and reduced to console.log('error sending addguestsemails') with the error object discarded, and the handler still returns success. the organizer sees the 'guests added' success toast while some or all attendees received nothing, and the log line carries no error detail or structured-logger context, making the failure undiagnosable in production.

[advisory] when every submitted guest is filtered out because they are already an attendee or blacklisted, the handler throws badrequest with message 'emailsmustbeuniquevalid', which is false in both cases. a user adding an already-invited colleague (the dialog only checks uniqueness within the current input, not against existing attendees) is told their emails are invalid instead of 'already invited', prompting confused retries with the same result.

[bug] the permission check joins isteamadmin and isteamowner with && while naming the result isteamadminorowner, so team admins who are not owners are denied instead of allowed. a team admin (role admin) who is not the booking's organizer or an attendee gets forbidden when adding guests to their team's bookings — the admin portion of the intended permission matrix (organizer/admin/owner/attendee) is silently dropped; under exclusive membership roles the && can only ever pass for owners.

[bug] addguestshandler never checks booking.status, and the new 'addmembers' action is added to bookinglistitem's actions array unconditionally (unlike the roundrobin conditional directly below it), so guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, or pending bookings. new guests receive attendeescheduledemail invites with a hardcoded status:'confirmed' ics request (organizer-add-guests-email.ts / attendee-add-guests-email.ts) for an event that was cancelled or never confirmed, re-adding a dead event to their calendars, and existing attendees get 'guests added' notices for it.

[bug] zaddguestsinputschema enforces only per-string email format with no uniqueness, and the handler's filter (addguests.handler.ts:74-78) only exact-matches existing attendees, so duplicate or case-variant emails create duplicate attendee rows. adding 'john@x.com' when attendee 'john@x.com' already exists — reachable through the dialog, whose uniqueness check only covers the input array — persists a second attendee row for the same person who then receives two different guest emails; a direct api caller can pass the same email twice for the same result.

[bug] eventmanager is constructed from the acting user's credentials (getuserscredentials(ctx.user)) even though the permission check deliberately admits non-organizer actors, so for attendee or team-admin actors the calendar update runs without the organizer's calendar credentials. when anyone other than the organizer adds guests, updatecalendarattendees cannot authenticate against the organizer's destination calendar, so the calendar event's attendee list is never updated (or the mutation errors after attendees were already persisted at line 92), leaving the organizer's calendar and the booking permanently out of sync — the organizer's credentials are already loaded in booking.user.credentials but are not used.

[bug] for seated event types the handler creates bare attendee rows via createmany with no seatspertimeslot capacity check and no bookingseat records, even though it passes seatspertimeslot/seatsshowattendees into the calendarevent (lines 145-146). guests added to a seated booking exceed the seat limit with no guard, and per-seat flows (seat-only cancellation, sendscheduledseatsemails, seat counts on the booking page) never see these attendees because they have no bookingseat records — the seat-gated sibling path of the attendee model this diff touches was left unchecked.

[bug] onsuccess resets multiemailvalue but never resets isinvalidemail, so the 'emails must be unique and valid' error banner persists into the next dialog session. after one failed validation followed by a successful add, reopening the dialog shows the red error banner over a fresh empty form (until cancel is clicked); the banner also never clears while the user corrects the emails, since nothing resets it on change.

[bug] the remove-button tooltip uses the hardcoded literal 'remove email' instead of a t() key, unlike every other user-facing string in the component. non-english users see an untranslated english tooltip in a shared @calcom/ui component that is exported for reuse beyond this dialog.

[advisory] any authenticated attendee may add an unbounded number of guests in a single call (no max on the guests array, no rate limit), and each address receives a calendar invite email replyto'd to the organizer. an attendee can use an organizer's booking as an invite/email cannon to arbitrary third parties with messages that look like they come from the organizer (phishing surface); the only guard is the global blacklistedguestemails env var, which is not per-event-type and is case-broken per the separate bug.

[bug] neither the handler nor the new bookinglistitem action (bookinglistitem.tsx:193-200, added unconditionally to the actions array) checks booking.status or start time, so guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, pending, and past bookings. adding guests to a cancelled booking emails every attendee an ics request with status confirmed and runs updatecalendarattendees against the cancelled event, re-confirming a cancelled meeting on attendees' calendars; the ui exposes this directly from the cancelled tab of the bookings list.

[bug] the blacklist entries are lowercased (line 71) but the guest email is compared raw (line 77) and the existing-attendee check uses === on raw strings (line 76), so neither comparison is case-normalized. a blacklisted address submitted as 'spam@x.com' bypasses blacklistedguestemails and receives the invite, and re-adding an existing attendee with different letter case creates a second attendee row so that person is emailed twice and appears twice on the calendar event.

[bug] the server schema omits the uniqueness refine that the client's inline duplicate of this schema enforces (addguestsdialog.tsx:26-29 re-declares the schema instead of importing it), and the handler's filter (addguests.handler.ts:74-78) does not dedupe within the guests array either. a non-ui client can send guests: ['a@x.com','a@x.com'], which passes server validation and persists two identical attendee rows via createmany, emailing the same address twice and duplicating it on the calendar event.

[bug] updatecalendarattendees runs with the calling user's credentials (getuserscredentials(ctx.user)) instead of the booking organizer's, even though the authorization block at lines 52-56 explicitly admits non-organizer actors. when anyone other than the organizer triggers addguests, the calendar update targets a calendar that does not contain the event and silently no-ops or fails, leaving the organizer's google/outlook event without the new attendees while the database and emails report them as added.

[bug] the remove-email tooltip uses the hard-coded literal 'remove email' instead of t(), the only untranslated user-facing string in the component. non-english users see an english 'remove email' tooltip in the add-guests dialog while every surrounding label is localized.

[bug] isinvalidemail is set on failed validation but never reset on input change or on the success path (onsuccess at lines 36-41 resets only multiemailvalue), so the error banner outlives the condition that triggered it. after an invalid submit, removing the rows and successfully adding a valid guest leaves isinvalidemail true, so reopening the dialog shows the 'emails must be unique and valid' error over an empty form.

[advisory] the endpoint authorizes any booking attendee to add guests, an actor class the ui never exposes (the bookings list is organizer-only), making this api-only capability an expansion not traceable to the stated organizer-facing feature. any logged-in user who is an attendee on a booking can inject arbitrary email addresses as guests, causing calendar invites (ics request with reply-to the organizer) to be sent to addresses they choose — an invite-injection vector the organizer-centric requirement does not call for.

[bug] for event types with seatspertimeslot the handler creates plain attendee rows via createmany without creating bookingseat records or routing through the seat-booking flow, even though it copies seatspertimeslot/seatsshowattendees into the calendarevent (lines 145-146). on seated event types the new guest consumes no seat (the slot still shows as available) and seat-scoped attendee handling is skipped, so the booking's seat occupancy and its attendee list disagree.

[bug] isteamadminorowner computes isteamadmin(user.id, teamid) && isteamowner(user.id, teamid), an and that contradicts its own name, so a team admin who is not the owner (or an owner who is not an admin) evaluates false and is rejected. team admins/owners who are not both roles get forbidden when adding guests to their team's bookings unless they happen to also be the organizer or an attendee; the feature the variable name promises is denied to exactly the staff roles it was built for.

[bug] the server-side zaddguestsinputschema omits the uniqueness refinement that the client-side copy in addguestsdialog.tsx (lines 26-29) enforces, and the handler's filter (lines 74-78) only dedups against existing attendees, never within the submitted batch. a direct api call with guests: ["a@x.com", "a@x.com"] passes validation and createmany inserts two attendee rows for the same person on the same booking; the invariant exists only in one client's ui and any other caller (api consumer, future client, the two already-drifted copies) silently corrupts the attendee list.

[bug] the existing-attendee dedup compares guest === attendee.email case-sensitively while attendee emails are stored exactly as entered, so the write path and the compare path disagree on canonical form. re-adding an existing attendee with different casing (john@x.com vs john@x.com) passes the filter, creating a duplicate attendee row for the same person, who then receives both a full attendeescheduledemail (as a 'new' guest) and an attendeeaddguestsemail (as an existing one) for the same event.

[bug] the eventmanager that executes updatecalendarattendees is built from the calling user's credentials (getuserscredentials(ctx.user)) while the calendar event being mutated belongs to the booking organizer. for the attendee and team-admin callers the permission model explicitly admits (lines 46-56), the calendar update runs without the organizer's calendar credentials, so the external calendar event is never updated with the new guests — the feature's core promise silently half-fails for every non-organizer caller the design intentionally supports.

[bug] the booking is fetched by id alone with no status guard anywhere in the handler, so guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, or pending bookings, and the new emails (attendee-add-guests-email.ts, organizer-add-guests-email.ts) attach an ics request with status:confirmed. adding guests to a cancelled booking sends every attendee a request/confirmed icalendar payload that re-confirms the cancelled event in their calendar clients, resurrecting an event the organizer cancelled; the action button is also rendered unconditionally in bookinglistitem, so cancelled bookings in the list are one click away from this path.

[advisory] the operation is a three-step sequence (db commit at line 92, external calendar update at line 165, email fan-out at line 168) with no transactional coupling or compensation between steps. if updatecalendarattendees throws after the attendee rows are committed, the caller sees an error toast but the guests are persisted; retrying the identical submission now hits uniqueguests.length === 0 and is rejected with badrequest 'emailsmustbeuniquevalid', stranding the user in a state where the error message is false and the action cannot be retried.

[advisory] booking.userid || 0 feeds 0 into findfirstorthrow when the booking has no userid, converting a nullable-organizer booking into a guaranteed miss. a booking with a null userid makes the mutation throw an unhandled prisma not-found error (500) instead of a graceful notfound/forbidden response; the || 0 sentinel exists only to satisfy the type, not to handle the case it silences.

[bug] the team-staff permission check joins isteamadmin and isteamowner with '&&' even though the variable is named isteamadminorowner; since a team membership holds a single role, the admin-or-owner grant collapses to owner-only (or to nothing, if isteamadmin excludes owner). a team admin who is not the booking's organizer and not an attendee receives forbidden when adding guests to their team's booking; the feature's access objective was silently narrowed from 'admins or owners' to 'owners only', and both membership queries always execute even when the first is false.

[bug] addguestshandler loads the booking by id alone and never checks booking.status, and the new list action (bookinglistitem.tsx:193-200) is offered unconditionally, so guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, pending, or already-past bookings. new guests on a cancelled or unconfirmed booking receive calendar request invites with status confirmed plus 'guests added' emails for a meeting that was cancelled or never accepted, misleading them into showing up; the happy-path assumption 'existing booking = active booking' was never validated against the data model.

[bug] the server schema accepts duplicate emails (z.array(z.string().email()) with no uniqueness refinement) while the dialog's hand-copied schema (addguestsdialog.tsx:26-29) enforces uniqueness only client-side, and the handler's filter dedupes only against existing attendees, never within the input array. a direct api call with ['a@b.com','a@b.com'] creates two attendee rows for the same address and sends that person two 'booking confirmed' emails with a duplicated calendar attendee list; the client and server schemas are parallel hand-maintained copies that have already drifted.

[bug] the dedupe and blacklist filter compares emails case-sensitively (guest === attendee.email, blacklistedguestemails.includes(guest)) even though the blacklist entries are lowercased at lines 70-71. adding 'user@x.com' when 'user@x.com' already attends creates a second attendee row for the same person with duplicate notification emails, and the same casing trick bypasses the blacklistedguestemails control entirely.

[bug] eventmanager is constructed from the caller's credentials (getuserscredentials(ctx.user)) instead of the booking owner's, even though the query at lines 35-40 fetches booking.user.credentials, so updatecalendarattendees runs against whatever calendar connections the caller happens to have. when a permitted attendee (line 54) adds guests, updatecalendarattendees cannot resolve the organizer's calendar connection from the caller's credential set, so the organizer's calendar event is left without the new attendees while the db write and success-path emails proceed — the calendar silently diverges from the booking record.

[bug] the attendee db write (lines 92-106) is followed by an unguarded 'await eventmanager.updatecalendarattendees', so any calendar api failure rejects the mutation after the guests are already persisted. an expired calendar token turns the add into a 500 after partial persistence: attendees exist in the database but received no invite, and a retry with the same emails is rejected with badrequest 'emailsmustbeuniquevalid', stranding the user in a state the ui cannot represent.

[bug] the handler passes seatspertimeslot through to the calendar event but performs no seat-capacity check and creates plain attendee rows without seat records, so seated event types accept unlimited extra guests. a seated event type with seatspertimeslot=1 that is fully booked gains any number of additional attendees via addguests, each receiving calendar invites, while seat accounting never increments — the slot is overbooked outside the seat system.

[bug] onsuccess resets the email list and closes the dialog but never clears isinvalidemail, so the error banner set by a failed validation attempt survives into the next open of the dialog. reopening the add-guests dialog for the same booking shows the red 'emails must be unique and valid' banner over an empty form with no invalid input present.

[advisory] blacklisted emails are silently filtered out of the guest list while the handler still returns success. an operator maintaining blacklistedguestemails gets no signal, and the acting user sees the 'guests added' toast while the blacklisted address was never added — a silent partial application of the requested action.

[advisory] the remove-guest tooltip uses the hardcoded literal 'remove email' in an otherwise fully localized component. every non-english locale shows an english tooltip on the remove button of the new shared multiemail control used in the guest dialog.

[advisory] the new 174-line handler ships with no test covering its three-way permission matrix, the dedupe/blacklist filter, or the db-then-calendar-then-email ordering. the '&&' permission defect and the case-sensitive dedupe both reached the diff unnoticed precisely because no test exercises them; any future refactor of this authorization and dedupe logic lands equally unverified.

[bug] the blacklistedguestemails blocklist is lowercased at load time but compared against raw-case guest input via case-sensitive includes, so any case variation bypasses the blocklist. with blacklistedguestemails='spam@evil.com', a caller submits 'spam@evil.com'; blacklistedguestemails.includes(guest) is false, the attendee row is created and invite emails are sent to the blacklisted address, defeating the abuse control the env var exists for.

[advisory] guests: z.array(z.string().email()) has no maximum length, so a single addguests mutation accepts an unbounded email list. one authenticated call from an organizer or attendee creates thousands of attendee rows via createmany, fires thousands of outbound emails in sendaddguestsemails, and pushes the full list into updatecalendarattendees — a one-request spam/dos amplifier that burns the sender's mail reputation and the organizer's calendar api quota, with no cap or rate limit anywhere in the path.

[bug] addguestshandler appends attendees without consulting eventtype.seatspertimeslot capacity or the booking's payment state, so guests added through this endpoint bypass seat accounting entirely. on a paid per-seat event type, an organizer or attendee adds any number of guests via the mutation; each receives the calendar invite and meeting link without a seat record or payment, bypassing the per-seat revenue and capacity limits enforced at booking time.

[bug] the server schema omits the uniqueness refinement that the client dialog enforces (addguestsdialog.tsx refine on set size), and the handler's filter dedupes only against existing attendees with a case-sensitive comparison, so duplicate guests within one request are accepted. a direct call to trpc.viewer.bookings.addguests with guests ['a@b.com','a@b.com'] (or 'a@b.com' when 'a@b.com' is already an attendee) inserts duplicate attendee rows for the same person and sends duplicate invite emails; only the client-side set check prevents this for ui users, so any non-ui caller corrupts the attendee list.

[bug] isteamadminorowner combines the admin and owner role checks with &&, requiring the caller to hold both roles simultaneously, so a team admin who is not the team owner is denied despite the check's name and the feature's team path. team admins get forbidden on team bookings they administer; the defect fails closed (no over-grant), but the team-authorization path of the feature is dead for admins and the misleading name invites an unreviewed flip to || later.

[advisory] the handler never validates booking.status before appending guests and sending mail, while the new email templates hardcode ics status confirmed with method request. guests added to a cancelled or rejected booking (or an already-past one) receive confirmed calendar invites that resurrect the cancelled meeting in their calendars — an attendee can keep emitting confirmed-looking invites from a dead booking (packages/emails/templates/attendee-add-guests-email.ts:15).

[advisory] updatecalendarattendees is executed with the caller's own credentials (getuserscredentials(ctx.user)) instead of the booking organizer's, so a non-organizer caller's calendar credentials are used against the organizer's destination calendar event. when an attendee adds guests, the organizer's calendar event is never updated — the db attendee rows are already committed at line 92-106, so the caller either gets a 500 after a partial write (retry creates duplicate attendees) or a silent calendar/db divergence.

[advisory] the authorization disjunction grants any authenticated user whose email exactly matches an existing attendee the right to append guests to the booking, not just the organizer. a booking participant with a cal.com account can unilaterally add arbitrary addresses that then receive method:request calendar invites and the meeting's video-call details under the organizer's identity; the organizer's only visibility is a single summary email after the sends have already gone out.

[bug] email send failures are silently swallowed: sendaddguestsemails is wrapped in a try/catch whose body is only console.log("error sending addguestsemails") — the caught error object is not even logged — and the handler then returns { message: "guests added" } as success. new guests never receive the calendar invite/ics email while the organizer sees a 'guests added' success toast; the dropped notifications are invisible to users, and the single log line contains no error detail, so operators cannot diagnose the failure either.

[bug] await eventmanager.updatecalendarattendees(evt, booking) runs with no error handling after prisma.booking.update (lines 92-106) has already committed the new attendees, so a calendar api failure throws a 500 after the db write — and the retry path is bricked, because the attendee-existence filter (lines 74-78) then reduces uniqueguests to zero and returns badrequest 'emailsmustbeuniquevalid'. one transient google/outlook api error leaves the booking's attendee list permanently out of sync with the calendar event: the user sees an error toast, every retry fails with a misleading validation error (the emails are unique and valid — they are already attendees), and no code path can ever push the guests to the calendar.

[bug] isteamadminorowner is computed with && between isteamadmin and isteamowner — a conjunction that can never authorize a team admin (a membership holds a single role, so under any role semantics the and excludes admins), contradicting the 'adminorowner' name that signals ||. team admins (and under strict admin-only/owner-only helpers, owners too) who are not the organizer or an existing attendee receive forbidden 'youdonothavepermission' when adding guests to their team's bookings, making the team-management path of this feature unreachable for exactly the users it names.

margin-left: auto on .panel (header.scss:37) is a no-op in the 2009 flexbox spec (display: -webkit-box / -moz-box) that the flexbox() mixin emits for older safari (≤6.0/ios ≤6), firefox (≤21), and old chrome; auto margins don't absorb free space on the main axis in that spec (alignment was done via box-pack), so legacy browsers render the panel next to the title instead of right-aligned — a box-pack: end fallback should be considered if those browsers are in the support matrix.

inconsistent prefix matrix in mixins.scss: flexbox() emits display: -moz-box and inline-flex() emits display: -moz-inline-box, but the align-items() mixin emits no -moz-box-align counterpart (unlike order(), which does emit -moz-box-ordinal-group), so legacy firefox renders the 2009 box layout with default stretch alignment instead of the declared center/baseline

.panel's right-alignment in header.scss rests solely on margin-left: auto with no fallback for the legacy engines the mixins explicitly target (ie10, old webkit), where auto-margin packing was incompletely/buggily implemented; if auto margins aren't honored, the panel silently renders flush against the title instead of at the right edge (era-standard fallback would be -ms-flex-pack: end / -webkit-box-pack: end)

[advisory] every denied check writes a permdenialcache entry keyed by attacker-influenced (name, parent) values with no size bound or rate limit on distinct entries created. a low-privilege or unauthenticated caller enumerating nonexistent dashboard/folder uids creates one local-cache entry per distinct denied name until ttl cleanup runs, so sustained probing inflates per-process memory on the authz service — a resource-exhaustion vector introduced by caching negatives on arbitrary, user-chosen keys.

[bug] the new permdenialcache is written on every denied check but has no invalidation path anywhere in the codebase — permission/role/team changes invalidate userpermcachekey entries only, never userpermdenialcachekey entries, so denial is ttl-only while the existing permission cache follows invalidate-on-change semantics. when an admin grants a user access to a resource (role change, team add, direct permission), the previously-denied check result stays pinned in permdenialcache for shortcachettl and keeps returning allowed=false even after permcache has been correctly invalidated and refetched — the user is denied access the ui says they have, and this pr silently changed the accepted propagation guarantee (grant-visible-on-invalidation) into ttl-bounded staleness without an explicit decision.

[bug] the async legacy-write goroutines derive their 10s timeout context from the http request context (ctx = klog.newcontext(ctx, ...) at the top of each method), so the 'background' legacy.create/update/delete/deletecollection is cancelled almost immediately when the request handler returns, making the 10-second timeout and the async design illusory. legacy writes/deletes are aborted mid-flight for most requests (context canceled), producing spurious legacy-duration failure metrics and actually reducing legacy-write success rate versus the old synchronous code; the same cancellation also kills re-run validation funcs (deletevalidation/updatevalidation) that depend on request-scoped context values, so legitimate legacy writes fail with 'context canceled' errors that no one asked for.

[bug] the async legacy update passes the raw objinfo instead of the previously wrapped updatewrapper containing the resolved updated object, so legacy storage re-computes updatedobject against its own (possibly stale) old object rather than receiving the exact object the unified store just accepted. legacy and unified stores receive different updates when their old objects diverge (rv conflicts, divergent fields), and legacy update can fail validation or write different content than what the client was told succeeded — a silent data-integrity drift that the removed updatewrapper mechanism existed specifically to prevent.

[bug] delete no longer falls through to legacy.delete when the unified store returns notfound (the old code explicitly ignored apierrors.isnotfound and proceeded to delete from legacy), so objects existing only in legacy storage are now undeletable through the mode-3 path. during any real migration from mode 0/1 to mode 3, pre-existing legacy-only objects cannot be deleted via the unified api: the call returns notfound and the legacy row persists forever, resurfacing in legacy api reads and blocking migration completion; the old behavior cleaned them up as a side effect.

[bug] the deletecollection legacy goroutine calls d.recordstorageduration instead of d.recordlegacyduration for the legacy operation, mislabeling legacy delete-collection outcomes as unified-storage metrics. dual-writer dashboards and migration readiness signals read wrong: legacy deletecollection failures/successes are counted in the storage bucket, so a failing legacy path during migration looks healthy and a healthy one looks duplicated; the metric by name is the contract other grafana migration tooling consumes.

[bug] in create (lines 45-47) and update (lines 129-132), the unified-storage error path records the failure with d.recordlegacyduration instead of d.recordstorageduration, misattributing storage failures to the legacy store. every unified-store create/update failure inflates the legacy-duration failure metric and skews per-store latency/failure ratios, corrupting exactly the observability this pr was adding to monitor dual-writer migration health.

[bug] the async legacy.create goroutine derives its 10s timeout context from the request context, so when the http handler returns the parent context is cancelled and the legacy write aborts almost immediately — the 10-second timeout is unreachable in the production request path. in mode 3 the legacy write silently fails for essentially every create issued over http (the goroutine records a duration but the error is discarded), so unified storage and legacy storage diverge from day one; rows are missing at migration cutover and the divergence is invisible because no error is surfaced or logged.

[bug] the async legacy.delete goroutine inherits the request context, which is cancelled as soon as the delete handler returns, so the legacy delete is aborted before the 10s timeout can apply. deleted objects are removed from unified storage but frequently remain in legacy storage (or vice versa if cancellation lands mid-call), producing persistent dual-store divergence on every delete and polluting the legacy-failure metric with cancellation errors.

[bug] the async legacy.update goroutine inherits the request context, which is cancelled when the update handler returns, aborting the legacy update regardless of the 10s timeout. legacy storage stops receiving updates in the request path, so the legacy copy drifts from unified storage on every write — the exact inconsistency mode 3 exists to prevent during migration.
