[bug] the legacy update goroutine receives the raw client-supplied objinfo instead of the resolved, validated object (the previous code wrapped it via updatewrapper with the object actually written to unified storage), so legacy.update re-resolves the update against its own possibly divergent old object. the resourceversion/optimistic-concurrency precondition enforced on the unified-storage write is not applied to the legacy write: a stale update rejected by unified storage can still be applied onto legacy's old state, writing an object to legacy that differs from unified storage and bypassing the concurrency control during the migration window.

[advisory] the download control nests a <button> (which renders a <button> element) inside an <a> anchor, which is invalid interactive-content nesting. clicking the inner button in some browsers/assistive tech triggers inconsistent behavior (the anchor's download navigation may be swallowed or double-activated), and the keyboard focus order exposes two competing interactive elements to screen-reader users on the backup-codes step.

[advisory] backup codes are generated and persisted to the user row in the setup endpoint (the password-confirmation step), before the user has actually enabled 2fa or even seen the codes. a user who opens the enable dialog, confirms their password, then cancels has silently had any previously issued backup codes overwritten (or new ones created) without ever viewing them — and since the login/disable paths reject a backupcode attempt only after password validation, a user who later 'loses access' and tries a code they saved from an earlier setup attempt gets incorrectbackupcode with no hint that their stored list is stale.

[bug] the login form's zod schema (formschema, used via zodresolver on the same useform that registers backupcode) is not updated for the new backupcode field, so zodresolver strips the unknown key and credentials.backupcode is undefined when passed to the credentials provider, making the backup-code login path in next-auth-options.ts unreachable from the login page. users who click 'lost access' and enter a valid backup code still get secondfactorrequired / never authenticate via backup code on the login page, because the submitted values are parsed through the untouched zod schema before reaching signin.

[advisory] backup codes are generated, persisted, and returned in plaintext in the setup response before the user has confirmed anything, and a user who abandons the flow after step one ends up with stored backupcodes the user has never seen (they were never displayed since displaybackupcodes only runs after enable), while the enable endpoint (totp/enable.ts, untouched by this diff) has no sanity check that backupcodes still match the setup that produced the displayed qr code. a user who starts setup, sees the qr code, but closes and later re-runs setup before enabling ends up displaying/enabling against a fresh secret while stale-looking backup codes from an intermediate setup run may have been shown or downloaded — the codes shown at displaybackupcodes step come from the first setup response held in component state, which is correct, but a dialog closed via onopenchange (x button) does not run resetstate, so reopening the modal resumes at the stale displaybackupcodes step with codes from the prior user's session state rendered again.

[bug] backup codes are generated and persisted during the setup step, before 2fa is ever confirmed, and the only place they are shown to the user is after successful enable — a user who runs setup and abandons the flow (or closes the modal at the qr/totp step) has 10 valid, never-revealed backup codes silently stored against their account. users who enabled 2fa via any earlier path or who abandoned setup have stored backup codes they never saw and cannot view again; the single-use consumption in login then deletes codes the user never knew existed, and the codes were accepted as valid second factors without ever being delivered.

[bug] at setupstep.displaybackupcodes the footer omits the cancel/reset wiring that other steps have, and the dialog's onopenchange path (esc / outside click) neither calls resetstate() nor onenable(), so the parent component's 2fa state is never updated when the dialog is dismissed that way. a user who dismisses the backup-codes step with esc sees the settings toggle still read 'disabled' even though 2fa is fully enabled server-side; the ui and server state diverge until a page refresh.

[advisory] the tabindex={-1} change to passwordfield's visibility toggle is not traceable to the 2fa backup-code requirement and is an unrelated behavioral change bundled into this pr. keyboard users across every password field in the app lose the ability to tab to the show/hide password toggle; the change ships unannounced inside a feature pr, so the accessibility regression is easy to miss in review.

[advisory] setup.ts calls symmetricencrypt with process.env.calendsoencryptionkey without the presence guard that the login and disable handlers added in this same diff, so the new backupcodes write path throws an unhandled typeerror when the key is unset rather than returning a structured error. operators running without calendsoencryptionkey get a raw 500 from /setup with no console.error breadcrumb, inconsistent with the sibling handlers that handle the same condition explicitly in this pr.

[advisory] the disable handler throws new error(errorcode.internalservererror) on a missing encryption key instead of returning a json error response like every other branch in the same handler. the client's response.json() in disabletwofactormodal parses an html 500 error page and throws, surfacing 'something went wrong' via the catch path instead of a clean internalservererror message shown to the user.

[bug] the 'no codes' sentinel is unrepresentable: missingbackupcodes is only raised when the backupcodes column is null, but consumption writes json arrays of null entries, so a user who has burned all 10 codes has a non-null column of nulls. a user with zero remaining codes gets 'backup code is incorrect' on every attempt instead of the 'missingbackupcodes' guidance ('generate them in your settings'), permanently and misleadingly — the same check exists in disable.ts and fails identically there.

[advisory] the setup endpoint regenerates and persists a fresh backupcodes set on every invocation, and the only place the codes are ever displayed to the user is the final displaybackupcodes step of the enable flow. a user who confirms their password (triggering setup) and then cancels at the qr/totp steps has their previously-issued backup codes silently invalidated with no notice; they will later hit 'backup code is incorrect'/'missing backup codes' with codes they carefully saved. the user-facing consequence appears at next-auth-options.ts:131.

[advisory] backup codes are stored reversibly encrypted (symmetricencrypt of the plaintext codes) in a single text json column instead of one-way hashed per-code rows, unlike one-time-code best practice. anyone with db read access plus the calendsoencryptionkey (a single shared secret, no rotation) recovers all valid unused codes for every user; hashed per-code rows in a child table would also fix the consumption atomicity and the null-array sentinel problems in one shape change.

[bug] backup code consumption uses a read-decrypt-modify-encrypt-write sequence with no transaction or conditional update, so the same backup code can be replayed in concurrent requests. two simultaneous logins submitting the same backup code both pass the indexof check before either write lands (next-auth credentials callbacks run concurrently), so a single one-time code grants two sessions — defeating the single-use guarantee the copy promises ('each backup code can be used exactly once') and letting an attacker who sniffed/copied a code use it even after the legitimate user already consumed it, if requests race.

[advisory] backup codes are generated with crypto.randombytes(5).tostring('hex'), yielding only 40 bits of entropy per code, well below the conventional 80+ bits for backup/recovery codes. an attacker who can submit many login attempts (e.g. via the credentials endpoint where rate limiting is per-ip and trivially distributed) has a materially better chance of guessing a valid code than against an 80-bit code; users with weak/leaked passwords get a second factor that is meaningfully brute-forceable.

[advisory] backup code verification uses backupcodes.indexof(credentials.backupcode...) — a plain, early-exiting string comparison rather than a constant-time comparison (timingequal/crypto.timingsafeequal), and the same non-constant-time indexof appears in disable.ts. each failed attempt leaks how many leading characters of a candidate code match positions in the stored list (indexof short-circuits per element, === per character); combined with the 40-bit code size this measurably aids online guessing by an automated attacker. rebuttal: per-request timing jitter makes the leak impractical — but with 10 ordered codes and 40-bit values the leak compounds across attempts rather than being neutralized.

[bug] fetcherrordetails materializes every error event for a replay via an unbounded nodestore getmulti: errorids comes straight from the snuba response with no limit/cap, and nodeids = [event.generatenodeid(...) for id in errorids] issues one bulk fetch of all of them on a synchronous user-facing get. a replay associated with hundreds or thousands of errors (the exact replays a user would want summarized) makes the endpoint fetch all of their nodestore documents into memory and embed all of their messages into the seer request payload, turning a bounded paginated segment read into an unbounded fan-out that times out or ooms the api worker on the busiest replays.

[advisory] the new validation-failure path logs the raw attacker-controlled report body ('rawreport': report) plus serializer errors at warning level from an unauthenticated, csrf-exempt endpoint. any unauthenticated internet caller can write arbitrarily chosen, unlimited-volume content into warning-level operational logs (log flooding/storage cost, and injection of attacker-authored entries into log streams that on-call and alerting tooling consume); the payload is reflected verbatim into log pipeline before any allowlist filtering.

[advisory] the new pr-comment template interpolates the user-controlled issue title (and, via getenvironmentinfo, the environment name) into markdown posted to github/gitlab without any escaping. an attacker who controls event data (any sdk user) can craft an issue title containing markdown metacharacters (e.g. 'x](https://evil.example) [y'), which break out of the '[{title}]({url})' construct and inject arbitrary links/formatting into sentry-bot-authored pr comments on third-party repositories — a phishing/link-injection vector in developer-facing surfaces; the 50-char truncation does not strip markdown syntax.

[bug] the endpoint validates every report before processing any, so a single invalid report in a multi-report post returns 422 and discards all valid reports in the same batch (metrics.incr never runs for them). browsers deliver reports in batches; one malformed or unrecognized report type (e.g., a new spec report type added by a browser before browserreporttypes is updated) silently drops the metrics for every valid report in that request, since per the reporting api non-2xx responses cause reports to be discarded rather than retried individually.

[bug] mergedprsingleissuetemplate ends with a literal \n while both call sites assemble the list with "\n".join(...), producing a blank line between every issue entry plus a trailing blank line, where the deleted per-integration templates produced a compact list. github and gitlab merged-pr comments render with an empty line between each issue bullet and a trailing empty line before the footer, a visible formatting regression versus the previous single-newline list; existing tests that assert the exact comment body will either fail (catching it) or were updated to encode the double-spacing as expected behavior.

[bug] fetcherrordetails catches every exception from nodestore.backend.getmulti and returns [], so a nodestore outage or deserialization failure silently degrades the summarize response to an error-free summary while the endpoint returns http 200. the caller (frontend summarize flow) cannot distinguish 'this replay had no errors' from 'error fetching failed', so seer generates and the user receives a breadcrumb summary that silently omits all error context; the only trace is a captured sentry event operators may not act on. this is exactly the invisible-failure pattern: the user-facing operation reports success while dropping work.

[advisory] errorevents is fetched once and captured via functools.partial into onresults, but genrequestdata resets erroridx to 0 per call, so every paginated page's seer request includes the replay's full error list merged against only that page's segments. errors from later time ranges are injected into earlier pages' prompts (and every error appears in every page's summary request), so multi-page replays produce duplicated and chronologically wrong summaries, and each page's seer payload grows with the total error count rather than the page's share.

[advisory] analytics.record("preprodartifact.api.assemble", ...) fires at the top of post() before the feature gate and all validation, so requests that are subsequently rejected are recorded as assemble events. the preprodartifact.api.assemble analytics series counts 403 feature-gate denials and later validation failures as successful assemble invocations, and attributes them to the requesting user — anyone consuming this event for adoption/funnel metrics gets inflated, unfaithful data.

createthreadqueueparallelworker reuses a factory-owned queue pool that strategy shutdown closes, so replacement strategies after rebalances receive stopped workers and closed queues; failed submissions are marked complete, allowing unprocessed messages to be committed.
orderedqueueworker.run marks offsets complete in its finally block even when processing fails, allowing commits to skip failed results permanently.
fixedqueuepool uses unbounded queues without submission backpressure, allowing queued payloads and tracked offsets to grow without limit and potentially exhaust consumer memory.
simplequeueprocessingstrategy.close stops the commit thread before workers finish, leaving results completed during shutdown uncommitted.
simplequeueprocessingstrategy.close sets worker shutdown flags without draining queues, abandoning pending work during normal shutdown.
simplequeueprocessingstrategy.close allows workers that exceed the five-second join timeout to continue processing after partition ownership is relinquished.

p2: feature-gating the removal listener (adminpermissions.java ~78) silently disables permission-resource cleanup in the default feature-off mode — previously roleremovedevent/clientremovedevent/groupremovedevent handlers ran unconditionally deleting removed entities' v1 permission resources and dependent policies from the realm-management authorization server; now with the flag off (the default for a preview feature) nothing is cleaned, and with the flag on the roles()/groups() branches run v1 implementations against the v2 resource server (root.realmresourceserver()), so v1 cleanup effectively never happens in either mode, accumulating orphaned resources/policies unboundedly; if v1 permission management is dead the listener body should be removed rather than gated.

client deletion with adminfinegrainedauthz enabled routes the clientremovedevent cleanup listener (adminpermissions.java ~90-92) into clientpermissionsv2.setpermissionsenabled (~191-194), which unconditionally throws unsupportedoperationexception — since the listener guard and the v2 selection share the same feature flag, every client deletion either propagates the exception and fails/rolls back delete /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id}, or the exception is swallowed and cleanup silently never runs while logging a stack trace

in haspermission(clientmodel, string), the 'all-clients' type-level fallback only fires when no per-client resource exists; once a per-client resource exists, evaluation runs only against that resource and the type-level resource is never consulted. since deleting a scope permission (the standard authz admin api, used in the tests' @aftereach) removes the policy but not the resource, an orphaned policy-less per-client resource permanently shadows type-level grants: after deleting a client-specific permission and later granting an 'all clients' manage permission, that one client returns 403 forever. the same shadowing occurs with a live per-client resource holding a grant for a different scope (e.g., per-client view + all-clients manage still denies manage for that client), contradicting the 'all-clients' semantics the fallback comment describes. the pr's tests never delete a per-client permission and then rely on a type-level grant, so this isn't covered.

clientpermissionsv2 throws raw unsupportedoperationexception from methods still declared on the shared clientpermissionevaluator/clientpermissionmanagement interfaces (setpermissionsenabled, ispermissionsenabled, resource, getpermissions, canexchangeto, exchangetopermission, managepermission, etc.), while the clientremovedevent listener (touched by this pr) still calls management(...).clients().setpermissionsenabled(client, false) on every client removal, and token-exchange and the v1 permission rest endpoints also call into this surface — so any v2-mode caller reaching these methods gets an unhandled 500 instead of graceful behavior; in particular, if management() dispatches to the v2 evaluator, deleting a client throws (or cleanup is silently skipped if the provider-event manager swallows listener exceptions).

[bug] the webauthn conditional-ui setup in authenticate() was moved from a user==null condition to isconditionalpasskeysenabled(context.getuser()) which requires user != null, inverting when passkeys data is filled for the no-user case. in a realm/flow where usernamepasswordform is reached with context.getuser() == null (e.g. the password form is the first browser execution, or a flow that skips usernameform), the conditional-ui form attributes are no longer populated on the initial challenge, so passkey autocompletion/conditional ui silently disappears for fresh logins — a regression of the behavior the old 'user is not already selected' branch explicitly provided.

[bug] challenge(context, error, field) flipped its guard from context.getuser() == null to isconditionalpasskeysenabled(context.getuser()) (user != null), so the two webauthn fill sites now cover disjoint user states with no site covering the complementary case. after a failed password attempt on a path where the context user was cleared (the state the old condition explicitly handled), webauthnauth.fillcontextform is skipped and the error challenge page loses the passkey/conditional-ui controls that were present before this change; symmetrically, the user!=null case in authenticate() is now double-filled (authenticate and later error challenge both call fillcontextform), while the user==null case is covered by neither.

[bug] the webauthn form-data setup was moved out of the user==null branch and is now gated on isconditionalpasskeysenabled(context.getuser()) which requires user != null, so passkeys conditional ui is silently dropped on the initial username/password page where no user is identified — the exact case the removed comment ('setup webauthn data when the user is not already selected') existed to cover. on a realm with passkeys enabled, a fresh login through the username+password form no longer renders conditional-ui webauthn data before a user is selected, changing first-login behavior in a pr whose stated intent is only fixing re-authentication; the accompanying challenge() override has the same inversion (old code required context.getuser() == null, new code requires user != null).

[bug] the passkey/conditional-ui setup condition in usernamepasswordform is inverted for the not-yet-identified-user case: authenticate() previously called webauthnauth.fillcontextform(context) whenever passkeys were enabled (no user check), and challenge(string,string) previously required context.getuser() == null; both now require context.getuser() != null via isconditionalpasskeysenabled(usermodel), so the combined username+password login page rendered with user == null never gets webauthn data. in realms that use usernamepasswordform as the first (combined) login form with passkeys enabled, the initial login page and the error challenge after a failed login with an unknown username no longer render the webauthn conditional-ui form, so discoverable-key (resident-key) passkey authentication is silently unavailable on that page — a functional regression for first-login passkey users, not just a re-authentication change.

[advisory] the reader thread is a non-daemon thread with an unbounded while loop; if any statement between thread start and deletedall.set(true) throws (e.g. a delete fails), the thread spins forever and leaks, hanging the test jvm's shutdown for non-daemon threads. a failing assertion or exception in the delete loop leaves the busy-loop thread running for the remainder of the suite, wasting cpu and potentially timing out the test runner; wrap the loop body/flag in try/finally or use a daemon thread with a join timeout.

[bug] isattendee grants any existing attendee the right to mutate the booking's attendee list, an authorization surface broader than the original 'organizer manages guests' intent with no human sign-off visible in the diff. any attendee of any booking can invite arbitrary additional email addresses to the event (and trigger calendar updates plus emails to everyone), enabling attendee-initiated spam/invitation propagation that the review iterations never explicitly accepted.

[bug] the server-side zaddguestsinputschema lacks the uniqueness refinement that exists only in the client dialog's inline schema, so duplicate guests submitted directly through the api create duplicate attendee rows. a non-ui caller (or a stale client) posting {guests: ['a@b.com','a@b.com']} passes validation, createmany inserts two identical attendees, the calendar event and emails then list the guest twice — the client-only refine silently changed the contract by not being lifted into the shared schema.

[bug] isinvalidemail is set on validation failure but never reset on a successful subsequent add, so the error banner remains after the user fixes the emails and the mutation succeeds. the user sees 'emails must be unique and valid' plus the success toast simultaneously, concluding the add failed and retrying, producing duplicate-guest server responses that the server schema also fails to dedupe.

[advisory] the handler loads the booking with no status filter, so guests can be added to cancelled or rejected bookings, generating confirmed ics request emails for events that no longer exist. attendees receive calendar invitations that re-confirm a cancelled meeting, corrupting their calendars; who gets bitten is every organizer or attendee who touches the add-guests action on a past/cancelled booking row in the list.

[bug] the admin/owner authorization check joins the two role queries with && instead of ||, so only a user who is simultaneously team admin and team owner passes, and plain team admins are denied despite the error message implying broader access. team admins (non-owners) who should be able to manage guests on their team's bookings get a 403 forbidden, or conversely the intended permission matrix is silently narrower than designed; either way the authorization decision does not match the intended policy.

[bug] the blacklistedguestemails deny-list is lowercased at build time but compared against the raw (non-lowercased) guest input with includes(guest), so any mixed-case variant of a blacklisted address bypasses the block. an operator who blacklists an address (e.g. an abuser or an opted-out party) is defeated by the attacker typing 'victim@x.com' instead of 'victim@x.com'; the blacklisted party still receives calendar invites/emails, defeating the control this env var exists to provide.

[bug] guest emails are persisted and compared with no normalization: the duplicate check guest === attendee.email and the attendee.email === user.email authorization check are both case-sensitive exact matches, so the same address can be added twice in different case and a user whose stored email case differs from the attendee row is not recognized as an attendee. duplicate attendees accumulate in bookings (duplicate calendar/email sends to the same mailbox), and the isattendee fallback authorization silently fails for users whose email is stored with different casing, producing inconsistent permission outcomes.

[advisory] the booking lookup is prisma.booking.findfirst({ where: { id: bookingid } }) with no team/user scoping in the query itself, and the subsequent authorization widens access to any authenticated attendee of the booking. any logged-in user who was once an attendee of any booking (including bookings belonging to a team they are not a member of) can permanently mutate that booking's attendee list, trigger calendar updates via the booking owner's credentials path, and cause emails to arbitrary addresses; the authorization is a post-fetch in-memory check rather than a scoped query, so future query changes (pagination, select reordering) can regress into a full idor, and attendees gain write access to resources owned by an organizer/team they have no other relationship with.

[advisory] zaddguestsinputschema accepts an unbounded array of guest emails with no .max() cap and no per-request rate limit, and each entry fans out into createmany rows plus one or more outbound emails. any attendee or organizer can submit thousands of addresses in one mutation, creating thousands of attendee rows on a single booking and triggering mass email sends — an email-bombing/abuse vector against third-party mailboxes sent from the platform's mail domain (deliverability and reputation damage for the instance).

[advisory] email-sending failures are swallowed by catch (err) { console.log("error sending addguestsemails"); }, discarding the error object and reporting success to the caller. when guest-add emails fail (smtp outage, template error), the organizer sees 'guests added' success and never learns attendees were not notified, and operators debugging production have no stack trace or context because the error itself is not logged — the attendees exist in the db but were never emailed, an unrecoverable silent divergence.

[advisory] the write prisma.booking.update({ where: { id: bookingid } }) re-derives authorization only from the earlier in-memory check with no ownership predicate in the update's where clause, and the guests are created before calendar/email work with no rollback path. attendee rows are persisted even if eventmanager.updatecalendarattendees or email sending subsequently fails, leaving the booking's stored attendee list, the remote calendar event's attendee list, and the sent invitations permanently out of sync (added guests see the event in db responses but were never invited or calendared).

[bug] the admin/owner authorization check combines isteamadmin and isteamowner with &&, so team admins who are not owners are denied even though the variable name and the check's intent (isteamadminorowner) is an or. a team admin attempting to add guests to a team booking gets a forbidden error; only owners (or organizers/attendees) can use the feature, contradicting the permission model the code claims to implement.

[bug] the blacklist and existing-attendee dedup filters use exact string equality while blacklistedguestemails is lowercased, so 'spam@x.com' bypasses a blacklist entry 'spam@x.com', and a guest differing only in case from an existing attendee is not deduplicated. blacklisted addresses receive event emails/ics invites by simply varying case, and case-variant duplicates of existing attendees are inserted as new attendee rows, producing duplicate emails and duplicate calendar attendees.

[bug] the server-side zod schema validates only email format and does not enforce uniqueness (unlike the client-side copy in addguestsdialog), so duplicate guests in one request pass validation and are inserted twice by createmany. a crafted or retried request creates duplicate attendee rows for the same email; the server trusts a client-side refine that an api caller bypasses entirely.

[bug] handleadd sends the raw multiemailvalue array (which the ui initializes to [""] and keeps as an empty row when a user removes/leaves blanks) instead of validationresult.data, so any remaining empty string fails z.string().email() and blocks the whole submission. a user who adds two emails, fills one, and leaves the second row empty always sees the 'emails must be unique and valid' error with no indication which row is the problem; the mutation never fires.

[advisory] the addmembers action is added unconditionally to every booking's actions array with no gating on booking status (cancelled/rejected bookings) or seat-based event types, unlike neighboring actions that carry conditions. users can open the add guests dialog and mutate attendees on cancelled bookings or seated event types (where seatspertimeslot capacity exists but is never checked in addguestshandler), overbooking seated events.

[bug] isteamadminorowner is computed with && between isteamadmin and isteamowner, so it is only true for users who are simultaneously admin and owner, and the permission check falls through for plain admins or owners. a team admin (but not owner) or owner (but not admin) attempting to add guests to their team's booking is denied with forbidden even though the code clearly intends 'admin or owner' to be an authorized role; the condition is also evaluated twice with two separate awaits instead of one role query.

[bug] duplicate-guest detection compares the submitted email case-sensitively against booking.attendees and does not normalize case, while the blacklist comparison lowercases only the blacklist entries, not the guest email. adding 'user@example.com' when 'user@example.com' is already an attendee creates a duplicate attendee row for the same person (duplicate db rows and a duplicate attendee on the calendar event), and a guest email listed in blacklistedguestemails with different casing bypasses the blacklist and still gets booked and emailed.

[bug] the booking row is updated with createmany of attendees but the new attendee emails are never pushed to the existing calendar event attendees before eventmanager.updatecalendarattendees, and guests already present on the booking's calendar entry are not reconciled with the evt attendee list ordering. depending on eventmanager.updatecalendarattendees semantics, the calendar event can be rebuilt with an attendee list that includes the just-created db rows, so any failure between the prisma update and the calendar update leaves the database and the external calendar event permanently out of sync (attendees on the booking but not invited on the calendar event), with no rollback of the created attendee rows.

[advisory] the booking lookup has no ownership scoping in the where clause (only id: bookingid), deferring all authorization to the post-fetch role checks. every fetch loads the full booking with attendees, references, and user credentials before authorization; correctness depends entirely on the (buggy) role check staying in sync, and any future caller that reuses this fetch pattern without the checks leaks other users' bookings.

[bug] the db update commits before eventmanager.updatecalendarattendees runs, and a calendar-update failure throws a raw 500 after the guests are already persisted, so retries are impossible. guests are inserted into the booking, but if the calendar update fails the caller gets an error; on retry the dedup filter finds the guests already in booking.attendees, uniqueguests.length === 0, and the user gets badrequest 'emailsmustbeuniquevalid' instead of the calendar update being retried — the calendar is permanently out of sync with the booking and the operation reports failure for work that actually succeeded.

[bug] isteamadminorowner combines the two checks with && so only a team owner (who is both admin and owner) passes; team admins are denied. a team admin who manages the booking's event type but is not the owner is told 'youdonothavepermission' even though the intended gate (admin or owner, matching the variable name and the permission model used elsewhere) would allow them; the permission check is stricter than the design intends, silently excluding admins.

[bug] blacklist filtering compares raw-case guest emails against a lowercased blacklist, so 'spam@x.com' bypasses blacklistedguestemails while 'spam@x.com' is filtered. blacklistedguestemails entries are lowercased but the incoming guest string is not, so a mixed-case variant of a blacklisted address skips the filter: the guest is added to the booking and emailed, and because the dedup check (guest === attendee.email, also case-sensitive) stores the cased variant, the same address can be added again as 'other case' — the blacklist is silently bypassable and duplicate-variant emails accumulate.

[bug] when every submitted guest is filtered out (already an attendee or blacklisted), the error returned is 'emailsmustbeuniquevalid', which misdescribes what went wrong. an organizer re-adding an existing attendee, or one whose guests are all blacklisted, sees 'emails must be unique and valid' for perfectly valid, unique emails — the message points debugging in the wrong direction and the user has no way to learn the real cause (duplicate/blacklisted).

[bug] findfirstorthrow on the organizer with id coerced from booking.userid || 0 throws a raw prisma error surfaced as a 500 when the booking has no user. for a booking with userid null (the || 0 sentinel), findfirstorthrow rejects with a prisma p2025 error that trpc surfaces as an internal server error instead of a 4xx, and the client's t(err.message) toast renders a raw prisma message.

[bug] the guests array has no max length cap, so a single request can create an unbounded number of attendee rows and trigger an unbounded fan-out of emails and calendar updates. an authorized attendee can submit thousands of emails in one mutation: createmany inserts thousands of attendee rows, sendaddguestsemails fans out thousands of emails and n calendar operations — storage and outbound amplification with no count cap on a request path.

[bug] the organizer email subject uses this.calevent.attendees[0].name, which is the first attendee rather than the booking counterpart, and crashes with a typeerror if attendees is empty. if the attendee list is ever empty the subject construction throws 'cannot read properties of undefined (reading name)' inside getnodemailerpayload, which the handler's catch swallows into a bare console.log while the api still returns success — and when non-empty, the subject names an arbitrary guest instead of the person the email is about (existing organizerscheduledemail usage passes the real attendee).

[advisory] isinvalidemail is set on validation failure but never cleared on subsequent input or on success, so the stale error banner persists while the user fixes the emails. a user who triggers the validation error, corrects the emails, and submits successfully sees the red 'emails must be unique and valid' banner still displayed underneath the (now valid) fields until they cancel and reopen the dialog — confusing feedback that misrepresents the current state.

[advisory] list items are keyed by array index while rows can be removed via splice, so react reuses dom/state for the wrong email fields after a middle-row deletion. after removing an email from the middle of the list, the controlled values shift but react keys stay positional, producing misplaced focus/caret and transiently stale rendered values for the rows after the removed one — a classic index-key defect that bites the next edit of this component.

[advisory] the event manager is built from ctx.user credentials while the booking/evt data is derived from the booking's organizer, so on behalf-of flows (attendee-triggered adds) the calendar update runs with the caller's credentials, not the organizer's. when an attendee (allowed by the permission check) adds guests, updatecalendarattendees executes against the attendee's connected calendars, which hold no event for this booking — the calendar update is a silent no-op or fails, and the new guests never appear on the organizer's calendar event.

.env.example:242-245 — the comment states calcomappcredentialencryptionkey "must be 32 bytes for aes256 encryption algorithm" but the accompanying example command is openssl rand -base64 24, which generates only 24 raw random bytes (base64-encoded to 32 characters, not 32 raw bytes); a self-hoster following the doc literally gets a 24-byte key, which will fail or misbehave against an aes-256 cipher expecting a 32-byte key .

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/calendarservice.ts:96 — await prisma.credential.update(...) uses prisma but the file only imports getappkeysfromslug and parserefreshtokenresponse from utils plus various @calcom/ packages, with no import prisma from "@calcom/prisma" anywhere in the file, so prisma is an undefined identifier and this fails to compile

packages/app-store/utils/oauth/parserefreshtokenresponse.ts:25-27 — when a refresh response omits refreshtoken, the helper substitutes the literal placeholder string "refreshtoken" for the real value; in packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/calendarservice.ts:263-271 this placeholder is spread over (and overwrites) the previously-valid o365authcredentials.refreshtoken before being written back with prisma.credential.update, so any refresh cycle where microsoft doesn't return a fresh refreshtoken silently destroys the stored real token, requiring the user to fully re-authenticate .

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57 — symmetricdecrypt(...) followed by json.parse(...) throws uncaught if the ciphertext is malformed or calcomappcredentialencryptionkey is wrong/empty, producing a raw unhandled 500 rather than a controlled error response

packages/app-store/utils/oauth/refreshoauthtokens.ts:15 — the sync-path response is returned to callers without checking response.ok/status, and packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/calendarservice.ts:94 destructures res?.data straight from that raw fetch response (which has no .data field), so token is undefined and the resulting typeerror is swallowed by the outer catch (googlecalendar/lib/calendarservice.ts:103-108), silently returning the old, potentially expired mygoogleauth as if refresh succeeded

packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/calendarservice.ts:177 — when the sync path is active, refreshoauthtokens returns a raw, unvalidated fetch response cast to hubspottoken; hubspotrefreshtoken.expiresin is undefined so expirydate becomes nan and accesstoken is undefined, yet this is written to prisma.credential.update (line 193) and hubspotclient.setaccesstoken(undefined) is called with no thrown error, silently persisting a corrupted credential as if the refresh succeeded

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31-91 — the webhook trusts a single static shared secret to authorize writes to an attacker-chosen userid in the request body with no per-user scoping/signature, so leaking or brute-forcing one calcomwebhooksecret grants an attacker write access to overwrite oauth credentials for every user in the instance

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25-26 — the webhook secret is compared with !==, a non-constant-time string comparison, allowing a timing side-channel attack to incrementally recover calcomwebhooksecret over many requests
packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:142 — the working-hours end check reuses the slot start, so a booking that starts before closing but ends after it is accepted.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:114 — the date-override equality check compares two newly created dayjs objects by reference, so equal start/end sentinel overrides are never detected.

addguests.handler.ts:158-163 — eventmanager is built with ctx.user and the caller's credentials, but calendar/video references belong to booking.user (organizer), so updatecalendarattendees runs with wrong credentials when an attendee or team admin invokes it; should use booking.user and its credentials

addguests.handler.ts:82-84 — booking status/time/seat semantics are ignored: guests can be added to cancelled/rejected bookings, past bookings, or bookings exceeding seatspertimeslot limits

addguestsdialog.tsx:44-46 — onerror builds message as a template string that is always truthy, so the t('unabletoaddguests') fallback never fires and errors without a code show 'undefined: ...'
addguestsdialog.tsx:55-62 — isinvalidemail is never reset to false on successful add or when the user edits emails, so the error banner persists after correction
multiemail.tsx:26 — list items use key={index} combined with splice on remove, causing react to reuse wrong emailfield dom/state when deleting a middle entry

[bug] updateevent's fallback branch evaluates event.destinationcalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalid === externalcalendarid) inside the branch where externalcalendarid is already falsy, so the search compares externalids against a null/undefined key, always returns undefined, and calendar.events.update is invoked with calendarid: undefined. rescheduling any booking whose stored reference lacks externalcalendarid (every booking created through the no-credentialid destination branch, which passes no externalid to calendarmanager.createevent) fails the google update with a missing/invalid-calendarid error that calendarmanager swallows as a failure result, leaving the google event at the old time while the cal.com booking and attendee emails show the new time.

[bug] deleteevent uses the same dead fallback — find((cal) => cal.externalid === externalcalendarid) when externalcalendarid is already falsy — so calendarid is always undefined for references without an externalcalendarid. canceling such a booking throws inside calendar.events.delete (caught and logged), and the event stays on the host's google calendar after cancellation, complete with its conferencing link, while cal.com frees the slot — ghost events for attendees and double-booked time for the host.

[bug] the no-credentialid branch calls createevent(c, event) without the third externalid argument that the credentialid branch passes (createevent(credential, event, destination.externalid)), so calendarmanager returns externalid: undefined and eventmanager persists booking references with no externalcalendarid. bookings whose destinationcalendar rows lack a credentialid store calendar references that google's update/delete falsy-externalid fallbacks cannot resolve, permanently breaking reschedule and cancellation for exactly those bookings — the previous code stored evt.destinationcalendar.externalid on every reference.

[bug] createevent resolves the target calendar exclusively via destinationcalendar.find((cal) => cal.credentialid === credentialid)?.externalid with a 'primary' fallback, so a destination calendar without a credentialid matches nothing and the event is created on the credential's primary calendar instead of destinationcalendar.externalid. for every destinationcalendar row with a null credentialid, events silently relocate from the user's selected calendar (the old code used destinationcalendar.externalid directly) to the account's primary calendar, and the resulting reference stores no externalcalendarid, which then triggers the update/delete failures above on the next reschedule or cancel.

[bug] createevent builds the graph events url from mainhostdestinationcalendar?.externalid — the first destination calendar — while eventmanager now invokes createevent once per host credential, so every host's token targets the first host's calendar id. collective bookings with multiple office 365 hosts (the exact case this pr adds) post to /me/calendars/{firsthostcalendarid}/events with each secondary host's token; graph returns 404 for a calendar outside that host's mailbox and the event is never created on the secondary host's calendar, leaving their slot booked in cal.com but empty on their calendar.

[bug] createevent (and createattendees at lines 161-166) resolves calendarid from the first element of event.destinationcalendar only, ignoring which host's credential the event is being created for. multi-host collective bookings create all lark events in the first host's selected calendar — duplicated when the tenant app token has access, or rejected with permission errors for every other host's credential — while each other host's own selected calendar stays empty.

[bug] basecalendarservice.createevent filters every credential's calendar list against mainhostdestinationcalendar.externalid — the first destination calendar — on every create call, regardless of which host's credential is in use. for multi-destination collective events, a secondary host's caldav/apple credential contains none of the first host's calendar urls, so the filter yields an empty calendar list and no event is created on that host's calendar at all — the collective multi-host fix silently no-ops for every non-first caldav host.

[bug] createevent sets the google organizer attendee email from the first destination calendar's externalid (mainhostdestinationcalendar) even when selectedcalendar was resolved to a different host's calendar by credentialid. in the multi-host collective case this pr introduces, each secondary host's google event is created advertising the first host's calendar address as organizer, misattributing the organizer in attendee uis and misrouting google's attendee-response handling for those events.

[bug] evt.destinationcalendar is assigned null when neither eventtype nor organizeruser has a destination calendar, so the optional-chained evt.destinationcalendar?.push(...teamdestinationcalendars) silently discards every teammate's collected destination calendar. collective events whose organizer has no selected destination calendar — the default configuration for users who never picked an installed-app calendar — skip the multi-host calendar creation this pr exists to deliver; teammates' selected calendars are ignored and their events fall back to primary calendars.

[bug] updateevent reuses the same first-destination-calendar organizer email, re-stamping mainhostdestinationcalendar.externalid onto the event payload on every update regardless of which host's calendar is being targeted. every reschedule of a multi-host collective booking rewrites secondary hosts' google events to list the first host's calendar address as the organizer, misattributing the organizer on each reschedule of exactly the bookings this feature targets.

[bug] inside the new per-reference loop, the recurring-cancellation path still resolves each remaining booking via updbooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("calendar")), taking only that booking's first calendar reference. canceling a recurring collective booking deletes each remaining occurrence only from the first host's calendar — and re-attempts that same deletion once per outer reference, duplicating delete calls — leaving every secondary host's calendar populated with events for occurrences the organizer canceled.

[bug] the new catch block returns calendarreference?.map(...) ?? [], which is an empty array for any error thrown before calendarreference is assigned (e.g., the newbookingid lookup at the top of the try). a prisma/db failure during reschedule now resolves to an empty result list that callers treat as 'no calendar references to update', so the reschedule completes in the database without any calendar update and without the success:false failure entry the old catch returned — the failure signal is gone.

[bug] office365calendarservice.createevent resolves the target calendar from destinationcalendar[0] (mainhostdestinationcalendar) and ignores both the per-credential destination and the new externalid argument, so every per-host invocation from createallcalendarevents targets the first host's externalid. for a collective booking with multiple office365 hosts, host 2's event is created via /me/calendars/{host1's calendarid}/events using host 2's token — microsoft returns 404 and the additional host never receives a calendar event, while the booking proceeds; the pr's headline multi-host fix silently holds only for google.

[bug] larkcalendarservice.createevent (and createattendees) resolve calendarid from destinationcalendar[0] regardless of which host's credential is performing the creation. collective bookings with multiple lark hosts attempt host 2+'s creation against host 1's calendarid with the wrong tenant credential, the lark api rejects it, and additional hosts end up with no calendar event for the booking.

[bug] the prisma booking write connects only evt.destinationcalendar[0], permanently discarding the additional team hosts' destination calendars that evt carries for collective events. requiresconfirmation and payment-gated collective bookings create their calendar events later from the persisted single destination calendar (confirm.handler, stripe and paypal handlepaymentsuccess all rebuild evt from booking.destinationcalendar), so team hosts never get calendar events — the multi-host fix silently vanishes on every deferred-creation flow.

[bug] deleteevent contains the same dead find — when externalcalendarid is falsy the find can never match, so calendarid resolves to undefined instead of falling back to the event's destinationcalendar as the old code did. cancelling a booking whose calendar reference has no externalcalendarid throws "missing required parameter: calendarid" inside events.delete, leaving the google event orphaned on the user's calendar after cancellation.

[bug] the merge-delete still uses booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("calendar")) even though the same function was converted to process all calendar references, so only the first calendar reference's event is deleted. reschedule-with-merge (the newbookingid path) of a multi-reference collective booking leaves stale events on every host after the first, orphaning those calendar entries with no error surfaced.

[bug] evt.destinationcalendar is set to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, and the later evt.destinationcalendar?.push(...teamdestinationcalendars) silently no-ops on null. a collective event whose organizer lacks a destination calendar but whose members have them collects the members' calendars into teamdestinationcalendars and then discards them, so no calendar event is created for any member host.

[bug] createevent (and the mirrored code in updateevent) stamps the organizer email as destinationcalendar[0]'s externalid on every host's copy, so events created on additional hosts' google calendars claim the first host's calendar address as organizer. every non-first host's event copy carries first-host organizer metadata — attendees and hosts see the wrong organizer on those copies and each reschedule rewrites the same wrong value via updateevent.

[bug] when a flusher running as a threading.thread (producetopipe path, used by tests and the pipe consumer) is declared hung, ensureprocessesalive skips killing it but calls createprocessforshards for the same shard list, leaving the old hung thread alive alongside a new thread both polling the same redis shards. two flusher threads race to fetch-and-delete segments from the same shards, producing duplicate kafka span payloads or interleaved partial flushes; the hung thread is never reaped, so each hang+restart leaks a live thread and multiplies redis load.

[advisory] in join, when the shared deadline expires mid-loop, break skips both waiting on and terminate()-ing all remaining flusher processes, so only the first process is reliably terminated on timeout. a consumer shutdown that hits its join timeout leaves n-1 spawned flusher processes alive holding redis segment leases; they keep flushing and producing after the consumer is considered down, so operations teams see ghost producers during any timed-out deploy or crash-loop restart.

[bug] the computed index keys [z.string().tostring()] / [z.string().optional().tostring()] do not create a catch-all index signature — they evaluate to a single static string key at module load, so the comment 'assume that any property with a number is the expiry' describes behavior the schema does not implement. in sync mode the parsed data contains only accesstoken (plus one junk literal key); every other property (expiry, scope, instanceurl for salesforce) is silently stripped, so callers relying on those fields in tokenresponse.data get undefined and the schema's advertised permissiveness is an illusion.

[advisory] the findfirst-then-update/create sequence is a check-then-insert with no unique constraint on (userid, appid) backing it. two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user+app both see no existing credential and both insert, leaving duplicate credential rows; downstream code that does findfirst will pick one arbitrarily and the other becomes unreachable stale credentials.

[advisory] the decrypted keys are json.parse'd and written to credential.key with no schema validation, unlike every other credential write path which parses through an app-specific zod schema. a partially-synced or wrongly-shaped payload from the parent application is persisted verbatim; the failure surfaces later at booking time inside the app's service class, far from the write that caused it, and with no validation error pointing at the sync endpoint.

[bug] review iteration silently changed what gets persisted: key passed to prisma.credential.update is now the safeparsereturn wrapper object from parserefreshtokenresponse (shape {success, data, error}) instead of the previously-stored parsed credential object from googlecredentialschema.parse(). after any token refresh with credential sharing enabled, credential.key in the db becomes {success:true,data:...} instead of the credential payload; every consumer that reads key.accesstoken / key.expirydate (calendarservice itself on next invocation, booking flows) reads undefined and google calendar sync breaks for refreshed users.

[bug] the helper fabricates a literal 'refreshtoken' placeholder string and callers persist it to the db whenever the (loose) minimumtokenresponseschema response lacks refreshtoken, changing the stored credential schema. with credential sharing enabled, the sync endpoint's response (accesstoken + expiry only) causes every refreshed credential in google/o365/zoom paths to have key.refreshtoken overwritten with the fake string 'refreshtoken'; if sync is later disabled, all those credentials attempt to refresh with a junk refresh token and permanently fail, requiring re-auth.

[bug] minimumtokenresponseschema's catch-all keys are computed from z.string().tostring() (which does not produce a wildcard/passthrough key), so unknown properties like refreshtoken are stripped from the parsed output, and the function then writes the literal string "refreshtoken" into data.refreshtoken, which callers persist to the credential record. the first credential-sync refresh overwrites the user's real oauth refresh token in the db with the placeholder string "refreshtoken"; every subsequent real-provider refresh fails permanently, silently breaking the user's calendar/video integration until manual re-auth. callers (googlecalendarservice.ts, office365calendarservice.ts, zoom videoapiadapter.ts) all write the returned object straight into prisma.credential.update.

[bug] when credential sharing is enabled, refreshoauthtokens returns a raw fetch response, but this code reads res?.data as if it were the googleapis token response, so token is undefined and token.accesstoken throws a typeerror. with appcredentialsharingenabled on, every google calendar token refresh throws instead of refreshing, so all google calendar integrations fail once the cached access token expires; the catch block then persists stale credentials (or the calendar calls fail outright).

[advisory] the webhook secret is compared with !== (not a constant-time comparison such as crypto.timingsafeequal), and this single shared static secret is the only authorization for writing credentials to any user. a party holding the shared secret (which the .env.example design explicitly distributes to the external cal.com instance) can also recover it byte-by-byte via timing side channels over many requests, gaining the ability to plant attacker-controlled credentials for arbitrary userids.

[advisory] the decrypted keys payload is json.parse'd and written directly into credential.key with no schema validation, and the handler performs no check that the caller is authorized for the target userid beyond the shared secret. any holder of the webhook secret can overwrite any user's credentials for any installed app with arbitrary attacker-chosen values (e.g. an attacker-controlled calendar endpoint), exfiltrating event data or hijacking the integration; nothing validates the keys match appmetadata's credential schema.

[advisory] detectprovider now resolves multiple providers by order, but defaultcryptoprovider, wildflyelytronprovider and fips1402provider all return order() == 200, so a tie between the server-side providers is broken by unspecified serviceloader ordering. any deployment that ends up with two of the three order-200 providers on one classpath gets a nondeterministically chosen provider (fips vs non-fips) depending on classpath enumeration order — a silent, environment-dependent security-relevant behavior change from the old hard failure; the order() mechanism as shipped does not actually order the providers it was written to order.

[bug] removing the multiple-provider error and replacing it with order-based selection makes ties (all three existing providers return order 200) resolve by arbitrary serviceloader/classpath iteration order. a fips deployment that accidentally has both crypto/fips1402 and crypto/default (or crypto/elytron) jars on the classpath previously failed fast with 'multiple crypto providers loaded'; now defaultcryptoprovider can be silently selected over fips1402provider (or vice versa) depending on jar classpath order, so a fips-mode server runs with the non-fips provider with no error or log line above debug level.

[bug] the authz-client jar globally registers authzclientcryptoprovider as a cryptoprovider service, so embedding authz-client on any classpath with keycloak-common silently installs a stub provider whose getalgorithmprovider, getsignature, getpemutils, etc. all throw unsupportedoperationexception. any application that adds keycloak-authz-client for the authorization api and also uses other keycloak-common functionality (pem parsing, cert utils, aes ciphers, signature instances) crashes with unsupportedoperationexception at runtime when no higher-order provider is present; conversely, in the keycloak server itself the authz-client jar now participates in crypto-provider selection, a boundary the authz client module previously did not cross.

[bug] getbouncycastleprovider() returns the jvm default keystore provider (typically sun) instead of a bouncycastle provider, violating the cryptoprovider contract every existing implementation honors. any keycloak-common code path that calls cryptointegration.getprovider().getbouncycastleprovider() to obtain or register bc (the documented purpose of the method) silently receives the wrong provider in a standalone authz-client deployment, producing algorithm-not-found or wrong-provider failures instead of a clear error.

[bug] detectprovider silently replaces the previous fail-fast illegalstateexception on multiple crypto providers with silent selection of the highest-order provider, changing an accepted safety invariant of the server without any human-accepted requirement. a keycloak server deployment with both the fips and default providers on the classpath used to abort startup with 'multiple crypto providers loaded' — an operator in a fips-mandated environment now gets a silently non-fips defaultcryptoprovider (order tie at 200 resolved by arbitrary serviceloader classpath order) and processes secrets under non-validated crypto with no error.

[bug] defaultcryptoprovider.order() returns 200, identical to fips1402provider and wildflyelytronprovider, so the 'higher order wins' selection rule cannot actually discriminate between the server crypto providers and falls back to arbitrary serviceloader ordering on the tie. when default and fips1402 (or elytron) jars coexist on the server classpath, which crypto provider the server runs with is decided by classpath jar order, not by any declared preference — the stated intent of the order field ('higher number has preference') is unfulfilled for exactly the multi-provider cases the field was added to resolve.

[advisory] the change removes the fail-fast on multiple cryptoproviders on the classpath and silently selects the highest-order one, converting a detectable misconfiguration into a silent provider downgrade. an operator who accidentally ends up with both a fips and a non-fips crypto provider on the classpath (e.g., by adding authz-client, which now ships its own meta-inf/services cryptoprovider at order 100, into a server deployment) gets no error and runs with whichever provider wins the order comparison; in a fips-compliance-required deployment the previously-loud illegalstateexception that caught this now only emits a debug-level log line nobody reads, so a non-compliant crypto stack ships silently. tie orders (defaultcryptoprovider and wildflyelytronprovider both return 200) make the winner dependent on serviceloader iteration order, which is jvm/jar-order dependent.

[advisory] asn1dertoconcatenatedrs accepts der integers of arbitrary size/sign and integertobytes silently truncates (keeps only the low qlength bytes) when the decoded r or s exceeds the expected coordinate length, and also accepts negative integers, instead of rejecting malformed signatures. signature bytes coming from an untrusted jwt are mangled rather than rejected during the concatenated-rs conversion used in es256/384/512 verification: a signature with an oversized or negative r/s is converted to a wrong-but-well-formed value and fails verification with a confusing non-security error (or, for values whose truncated form collides, relies entirely on the downstream verifier for rejection), where the keycloak defaultcryptoprovider equivalents validate lengths; anyone debugging token verification against a hostile issuer gets garbage-in behavior instead of a clean 'invalid signature encoding' rejection.

[bug] getbouncycastleprovider() returns the jvm's default keystore provider (typically sun), not a bouncycastle provider, despite the method contract and name. any caller that requests getbouncycastleprovider() to obtain bc-specific algorithms (e.g., bc pem handling, bc keystore formats) silently gets the default jdk provider and fails at runtime with nosuchalgorithmexception or missing-function errors that name the wrong provider during debugging.

[bug] the isaccesstokenid matcher has an off-by-one and an inverted condition: it reads items[0].substring(3, 5) (characters 3-4) instead of substring(4, 6) (characters 4-5) for the grant shortcut, and it returns false when the extracted value equals the expected shortcut. for a correctly encoded id like 'onrtac:uuid', substring(3,5) is 'ta', which never equals 'ac', so the guard if (...equals(expectedgrantshortcut)) return false; is never taken by the intended path — but for ids where chars 3-4 happen to equal the expected shortcut the matcher rejects the correct id, and it accepts any id whose chars 3-4 differ from the expected shortcut, so every expectation either fails or asserts nothing about the real grant shortcut; the updated expectcodetotoken/expectrefresh/expectdevicecodetotoken/expectauthreqidtotoken assertions in this diff verify the wrong bytes.

[bug] the signup error response now echoes user.errors.tohash and the submitted name/username/email back to any anonymous client, untraceable to the stated blocked-email requirement. unrelated scope expansion of a public unauthenticated endpoint: anonymous attackers can use the structured errors/values payload to enumerate which emails are on the blocklist (distinct 'blocked' message vs 'notallowed' message) and to probe username/email uniqueness rules, with no requirement in this pr calling for it.

[bug] routine per-batch cleanup progress is logged with r.log.error (including the 'annotations to clean by time', 'cleaned annotations by time', 'annotations to clean by count', 'cleaned annotations by count', 'tags to clean', 'cleaned tags' call sites) even on the success path where err is nil and y is nil. every cleanup batch emits an error-severity log line on a healthy system; operators with error-level alerting (or grafana's own log-based alert rules) get paged every minute per batch, and real errors are buried in the noise.

[bug] routine cleanup progress is logged at error level ('annotations to clean by time', 'cleaned annotations by time', and the count branch equivalents) with the err field always nil on the success path. every cleanup cycle on every grafana instance emits multiple error-level log lines for normal operation, paging on-call / tripping alert rules keyed on error logs and burying real errors; the intent of the original code (silent successful cleanup) silently drifted during review iteration without an accepted decision to make routine cleanup log at error severity.

[advisory] routine success-path cleanup work is logged via r.log.error with the full id list and condition string, e.g. r.log.error("annotations to clean by time", "count", len(ids), "ids", ids, "cond", cond, "err", err). every cleanup batch (batch size configurable up to 32767, and the loop runs continuously in production every minute now that the cleanup ticker is 1 minute) emits an error-level log line carrying thousands of ids; operators' error telemetry/alerting is flooded with non-errors, and large ids slices are serialized into log lines, degrading log storage and obscuring genuine errors. any log-based alerting on annotation-cleanup errors will fire constantly on healthy operation (three error lines per batch across cleanannotations and cleanorphanedannotationtags).

[bug] in the maxage cleanup loop, the batch's affected count is taken from x (rows deleted by deletebyids), so if rows are deleted between fetchids and deletebyids (e.g. a second grafana instance in ha running the same cleanup job), the batch returns affected=0 and the retry loop terminates even though ids were fetched and remaining matching rows still exist. in multi-instance deployments where each node runs the cleanup service, two instances racing on the same batch cause one to observe 0 affected rows and stop the whole maxage (and maxcount) sweep early, leaving stale annotations that are only removed on a later cycle; combined with the code comment's acknowledged under-delete, this makes cleanup completion non-deterministic per run. the loop should terminate on len(ids) == 0 (rows fetched) rather than on affected rows deleted.

[advisory] cleanup success paths log at error level and dump the full id list of every batch into the log message. every cleanup cycle emits r.log.error('annotations to clean by time', 'ids', ids, ...) and 'cleaned annotations by time' even when the operation succeeds (err is nil), so operators' error dashboards/alerts fire on routine cleanup and large batches (batch size can be 32767) flood logs with thousands of ids per cycle at 1-minute ticker frequency.

[advisory] fetchids and deletebyids run in separate sessions/transactions with no locking, so concurrent deletes/inserts between the select and the delete make affected < len(ids) silently. the comment acknowledges under-deletion for inserts, but a concurrent delete of an already-fetched id makes the batch report fewer affected rows; since untildoneorcancelled terminates on affected==0, a batch whose rows were all deleted concurrently ends the whole loop early even though qualifying rows still exist — cleanup silently does less work than the reported total implies. tolerable per the stated 'next cycle' rationale, but the loop-termination-on-zero-affected interaction means the next cycle may also see zero affected rows for the maxcount case if the remaining rows fall under the offset window.

[bug] the eventmanager is constructed with the requesting user (...user, credentials from getuserscredentials(ctx.user)) instead of the booking organizer (booking.user), while evt.organizer is built from the organizer. when an attendee (a permitted non-organizer caller per the isattendee check) adds guests, updatecalendarattendees runs with the attendee's credentials, so the organizer's external calendar event is never updated with the new guests (or the update crashes on missing calendar credential); only the organizer caller works.

[bug] isinvalidemail is set true on validation failure but is never reset when the user edits the emails and retries via handleadd, and is not cleared on dialog open — only the cancel button clears it. after one invalid submission, the 'emails must be unique and valid' error stays rendered even after the user fixes the input and clicks add again with valid emails (validation succeeds, mutation fires, but the stale error remains until success closes the dialog), telling the user their now-valid input is still wrong.

[advisory] the sendaddguestsemails failure is swallowed with a bare console.log that drops the error object and any stack. when smtp or template rendering fails, guests are persisted as attendees but no one is notified and no organizer-visible error surfaces — the api still returns 'guests added' success, and an operator triaging the incident has no error details in logs to diagnose why notifications were silently lost.

[advisory] the addmembers menu item is added unconditionally to every booking's action list, with no gating on booking status (cancelled/rejected) or event type, unlike the surrounding items which are conditionally included. users see 'additional guests' on cancelled and rejected bookings where adding guests is meaningless, and clicking it lets them add attendees to a cancelled booking's roster, generating 'guests added' emails for an event that will never occur.

[advisory] sendaddguestsemails sends the full attendeescheduledemail to brand-new guests whose name is the empty string (handler creates attendees with name: ""), while existing attendees get the shorter attendeeaddguestsemail. new guests receive a scheduling confirmation email addressed to a blank name and carrying a duplicate calendar invite (method request, status confirmed) for an event they never booked; if their mail client already has the event, the blank-name invite confuses the roster, and the new guests get no indication they were added by someone else rather than having booked themselves.

[bug] the permission gate computes isteamadminorowner as isteamadmin(...) && isteamowner(...), requiring the caller to be both admin and owner instead of either. a team admin who is not the owner, adding guests to their team's booking, receives forbidden even though the pr's own variable name and intent state admin-or-owner should be allowed; conversely the gate silently grants nothing to plain admins — the authorization check does not match its stated invariant.

[bug] the duplicate-attendee check guest === attendee.email is case-sensitive while the blacklist comparison lowercases the list entry, so the filter is inconsistent on email case. submitting guest@example.com when guest@example.com is already an attendee creates a duplicate attendee row (two ics attendees, two emails to the same person), and guest@example.com bypasses the blacklistedguestemails blacklist because the comparison compares a raw-case guest against lowercased entries.

[advisory] the new blacklistedguestemails env var silently drops emails rather than surfacing a validation error, and the filter is undisclosed to the caller. an operator sets the blacklist and an organizer adds a mixed list: some guests are silently not added while the ui shows 'guests added', leaving the organizer with no signal that anyone was excluded; the env var itself has no documentation or schema/typing entry anywhere in the diff.

[bug] .panel swaps float: right for margin-left: auto, but auto-margin alignment does not exist in the old flexbox syntaxes the new mixins deliberately emit (display: -ms-flexbox, -webkit-box, -moz-box in mixins.scss), so on those browsers the panel is never pushed to the header's right edge. in ie10 (where -ms-flexbox is the only recognized display value from the mixin) and old-spec-only webkit/firefox builds, .panel renders immediately after the title in the flex row instead of pinned right, stranding the search/avatar/login controls mid-header; the mixin file's own -ms-flexbox/-webkit-box/-moz-box lines declare these browsers in the intended support set, so the layout technique contradicts the fallback matrix the same pr ships.

[bug] .extra-info-wrapper becomes a flex item of the now-flexible .contents with the default min-width: auto in a single-line (no flex-wrap) row, so its minimum width is pinned to the full rendered width of the topic title it contains and the row cannot shrink it. for a long topic title, or a title containing a long unbroken word/url (common in pasted-link titles), the wrapper's min-content width exceeds the space beside the logo and panel; the flex row overflows and .panel is pushed past the header's right edge and clipped, whereas the deleted float layout let the title block occupy only the space between the floats and wrap/ellipsize there. the same min-width exposure applies to the .title flex item for long text-only site titles.

[bug] the float declarations that produced the header layout (float: left on .title, float: right on .panel) are deleted rather than retained ahead of the flex declarations, so a browser that recognizes none of the five display values emitted by flexbox() falls back to block layout with nothing positioning the children horizontally. on browsers with no flexbox support at all (ie9, opera mini), the logo, topic title, and panel stack vertically inside the fixed-height header and the panel is clipped out of view; the sibling conversion in topic-post.scss keeps the base .topic-avatar { float: left } rule so .small-action still degrades to the float layout, showing the header conversion dropped the fallback its sibling kept — retaining the floats before @include flexbox() is the standard no-cost fix since floats are ignored on flex items.

[bug] the new flexbox mixin emits display:-webkit-box/-moz-box, so 2009-spec-only engines (android 4.1-4.3 stock browser, ios 6 safari) activate the old box model, where margin-left:auto on a flex item computes to 0 instead of absorbing free space - and margin-left:auto is now .panel's sole right-alignment mechanism after float:right was removed. on exactly the legacy engines the vendor prefixes are written to support, the header panel renders immediately after the title/extra-info-wrapper instead of at the right edge - a visible regression versus the float layout it replaces, which worked on those engines; the mixin abstraction advertises cross-spec flexbox support while the layout technique it lays out with is modern-spec-only.

[bug] the align-items mixin emits -webkit-box-align and -ms-flex-align but no -moz-box-align, while its companion flexbox()/inline-flex() mixins emit display:-moz-box/-moz-inline-box and order() emits -moz-box-ordinal-group - so on firefox builds whose newest supported display value is -moz-box (pre-firefox 22), every @include align-items() in this diff resolves to no alignment declaration at all. header .contents and .small-action lose their vertical centering and the .bullet category badge loses baseline alignment on those firefox builds (items fall back to the engine default alignment) because the mixin family covers gecko's old-spec display and ordering properties but not its alignment property - the registry is internally inconsistent across the spec generations it claims to span.

[bug] replacing .panel's float: right with margin-left: auto is not behavior-preserving on the 2009-spec tier the new mixins themselves emit first: in -webkit-box/-moz-box layout auto margins compute to 0, so the panel loses its right-edge alignment. on browsers that resolve display to -webkit-box/-moz-box (android stock 2.3–4.3, firefox ≤21, safari ≤6) the header buttons render immediately after the site title instead of flush right — a regression on the very browsers the vendor-prefix mixins claim to support.

[advisory] the new align-items mixin emits -ms-align-items, a property no browser has ever implemented (ie's real property -ms-flex-align is already emitted one line above), and omits -moz-box-align even though the sibling flexbox() mixin emits display: -moz-box and order() emits -moz-box-ordinal-group. the hand-maintained prefix list is internally inconsistent the moment it lands: in the old-firefox engines that display: -moz-box exists to serve, align-items: center/baseline silently falls back to the default stretch, misaligning the header contents, small-action rows, and bullet badges there, and every future caller of the mixin inherits the same silent gap; the -ms-align-items line is dead bytes shipped on every call site.
