[advisory] the diff bundles tabindex={-1} on the shared passwordfield visibility toggle — an app-wide keyboard-navigation change affecting every password input in the product — into a 2fa backup-codes pr, with no backup-code requirement it traces to. keyboard-only users lose tab access to the show/hide control on all password fields product-wide, and because the change rides in an unrelated security pr it cannot be bisected or reverted independently when the a11y regression is reported.

[bug] the diff removes onenable() from the successful-enable handler and defers it to the backup-codes close button (lines 261-272), so the dialog's built-in x (wired to onopenchange) at the displaybackupcodes step exits without ever notifying the parent that 2fa was enabled. a user who enables 2fa and dismisses the codes screen via x leaves the settings page showing the 2fa switch unchecked while 2fa is in fact enabled server-side, and may re-attempt setup or misjudge their account's security state from the stale ui.

[bug] the login page collects backupcode (registered by the new backupcode component, typed in loginvalues) but the diff never transmits it: neither the zod formschema behind zodresolver (untouched by any hunk, and zodresolver strips keys absent from the schema out of the submitted data) nor the signin('credentials', ...) payload in handlesignin (no hunk touches that call) is updated, so credentials.backupcode is always undefined in authorize() and the lost-access login branch is unreachable. a user who lost their authenticator and enters a valid backup code is bounced back to the totp prompt with secondfactorrequired forever — the feature's primary recovery flow authenticates no one, and the diff's own e2e todo confirms login-with-backup is untested, so nothing catches it.

[bug] backup-code consumption in authorize() is an unguarded read-modify-write: the array is read and decrypted, matched with indexof, nulled in memory, and the whole blob rewritten with no unique constraint, version column, or conditional update, so two concurrent sign-ins presenting the same code both pass. two parallel posts to the auth callback with one backup code both create sessions — the 'used exactly once' invariant the ui explicitly promises ('each backup code can be used exactly once') is violated, and concurrent logins with different codes resurrect already-consumed codes via lost update, leaving burned codes valid for later replay.

[advisory] storing all backup codes as a single encrypted json text blob on user is the wrong data structure for single-use consumption: the column cannot enforce per-code uniqueness, cannot expose per-code used-state to the database, and forces whole-blob read-modify-write on every use. this shape is the direct enabler of the toctou in authorize() — a backupcode child table (hashed code, unique(user, code), atomic update ... where usedat is null checking rowcount) would make single-use enforceable at the data layer; with the blob it is unenforceable without application locking.

[advisory] the missingbackupcodes error tells users to generate codes in their settings, but backup codes are generated exclusively inside setup.ts's enable-2fa flow — no settings path anywhere in the diff can generate or re-display codes, so the remediation the error text instructs is impossible to perform. every user who enabled 2fa before this feature shipped (backupcodes null) — exactly the population most likely to have lost their authenticator — gets a dead-end message on lost-access login; obtaining codes requires disabling 2fa, which itself requires the totp they lost, so lost-access users are fully locked out.

[advisory] onenable is no longer called when enable succeeds (the success handler now only advances the step) — the callback fires solely from the new displaybackupcodes 'close' button, so closing the modal via esc/x/overlay after enabling skips both resetstate and onenable. the parent settings component's 2fa switch state is left stale because its only refresh signal was onenable, and since the codes exist only in modal react state with no re-view path, an accidental esc at the codes step permanently destroys the only presentation of codes that are already persisted and active.

[bug] the pre-toggle 2fa assertion expect(page.locator(...).ischecked()).tobetruthy() checks the truthiness of a promise object and therefore always passes — the diff's own added fixme admits this ('this passes even when switch is not checked') yet ships the broken assertion unchanged. the e2e suite claims to verify the 2fa switch's initial unchecked state while asserting nothing, so any regression in that state stays green — the diff documents a false guard instead of fixing it.

[advisory] body.backupcodes is used unguarded (setbackupcodes(body.backupcodes) immediately followed by body.backupcodes.map(...)), but during a rolling deploy a user's page can be served by a new pod while their setup xhr is routed to an old pod whose setup.ts response predates the field. in the deploy window a 200 setup response lacking backupcodes throws typeerror at the blob construction (caught as a generic error), so 2fa setup fails spuriously for users mid-deploy even though the server already rotated their secret.

[bug] the backupcode value typed into the login form never reaches authorize(): this diff adds backupcode to loginvalues and registers the input, but no hunk in this pr adds backupcode to the zod formschema driving zodresolver (z.object strips unknown keys from the parsed values handed to handlesignin) nor to the unchanged signin() call inside handlesignin, so credentials.backupcode in next-auth-options.ts is always undefined. a user who lost their authenticator enters a valid backup code, the stripped submission makes authorize() fall into the totp branch and return second-factor-required, so the backup-code login path — the feature this pr exists to deliver — silently no-ops and the user is locked out; the diff's own todo (login.2fa.e2e.ts line 11) confirms no test exercises this path, so ci cannot catch it.

[bug] replacing onenable() with setstep(setupstep.displaybackupcodes) at line 135 silently changes the modal's output contract: the parent is now notified that 2fa was enabled only when the user clicks the new close button (line 269), not when the enable api succeeds. a user who enables 2fa and then dismisses the backup-codes screen via escape or the dialog's x (the onopenchange path, which never routes through the close button's onclick) triggers no onenable() call, leaving the settings page showing 2fa as disabled while the account now demands a second factor at next login — a state desync the original immediate-callback design made impossible.

[bug] the missingbackupcodes guard at line 137 tests !user.backupcodes, but the single-use consumption logic at line 148 writes back "[null,...]" after the tenth use, so an exhausted user passes the guard, hits the indexof check at line 144, and receives incorrectbackupcode instead of missingbackupcodes. a user who consumed all ten single-use codes and then lost the authenticator is told "backup code is incorrect" rather than that no codes remain, prompting endless re-entry of codes that can never validate instead of escalation to account recovery.

[bug] the disable endpoint's !user.backupcodes check at line 54 misses the exhausted state because consumed codes are persisted as a truthy "[null,...]" json array, so the user falls through to indexof at line 61 and gets incorrectbackupcode at line 63 instead of missingbackupcodes. a user relying on this endpoint as their last self-service recovery path with exhausted codes gets a misleading "incorrect code" error that hides the true state and the fact that only support intervention remains.

[bug] tabindex={-1} on the password-visibility toggle (line 49) removes the control from sequential keyboard focus for every passwordfield in the application, with no alternative keyboard activation path added. keyboard-only users across login, signup, and every settings password field can no longer tab to or activate the show/hide password button — an app-wide wcag 2.1.1 accessibility regression bundled into a 2fa pr with no connection to its stated objective and no explicit acceptance.

[bug] backup-code single-use enforcement in authorize() is a non-atomic read-modify-write: backupcodes.indexof(...) on the freshly decrypted list gates an unconditional prisma.user.update that rewrites the entire list, with no transaction, row lock, or compare-and-swap on the ciphertext. two concurrent sign-ins presenting the same backup code both read the pre-update list, both pass the indexof check, and both receive sessions — a double-submitted login form or an attacker racing a phished code gets a second session from a code the user believes is burned; worse, interleaved use of two different codes resurrects an already-consumed code (each request writes back a list derived from the pre-update state, so the later write restores the other request's code to valid), violating the 'each backup code can be used exactly once' guarantee the new locale string states.

[bug] showtoast(t('backupcodescopied'), 'success') runs synchronously on the line after the un-awaited navigator.clipboard.writetext(...) promise, so the success toast is displayed regardless of whether the clipboard write resolves or rejects. a user whose clipboard write rejects — firefox with the clipboard permission denied for the site, or an embedded webview without a clipboard grant — is told their one-time recovery codes were copied when they were not; they close the dialog relying on an empty clipboard and are permanently locked out when they later lose their authenticator, while the e2e test only asserts the toast appears and cannot catch the failure.

[bug] the enable-2fa e2e's switch-state assertion await expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch]').ischecked()).tobetruthy() (line 53) asserts an un-awaited promise object, which is always truthy, so it passes unconditionally — the fixme comment this same diff adds at lines 50-51 ("this passes even when switch is not checked") documents the tautology and the broken assertion is left in place. the step that reads as verifying 2fa was enabled verifies nothing: a regression that leaves the switch off (broken toggle handler, failed enable) is still green at this assertion, and real coverage of the checked state rests entirely on the later data-state="checked" selector at line 127 — every maintainer reading this test is handed false confidence that enablement is asserted mid-flow.

[bug] backup-code verification at login compares raw input case-sensitively and without trimming — backupcodes.indexof(credentials.backupcode.replaceall("-", "")) against lowercase hex codes from crypto.randombytes(5).tostring("hex") — so any uppercase letter or stray whitespace in an otherwise valid code fails the match. a user holding a valid code who types it on a mobile keyboard that autocapitalizes (the input has no autocapitalize/case normalization) or pastes it with surrounding whitespace is told 'backup code is incorrect' and is locked out of the last-resort recovery path; totp never had this failure because its codes are digits.

[bug] handleenable no longer calls onenable() on a successful enable — it defers the call to the displaybackupcodes 'close' button (line 269) — so dismissing the dialog via radix esc/outside-click/x (onopenchange) after enable succeeded never notifies the parent. the security settings page keeps rendering the 2fa switch as disabled while the database has twofactorenabled=true; the user proceeds believing 2fa is off, and reopening the modal resumes at the stale backup-codes step with the previous attempt's codes still in component state.

[bug] the disable endpoint's backup-code check uses the same case-sensitive, untrimmed comparison — backupcodes.indexof(req.body.backupcode.replaceall("-", "")) against lowercase hex codes — so correctly-typed codes with any capitalization or whitespace are rejected. a user disabling 2fa with a valid but non-lowercase backup code gets incorrectbackupcode and must fall back to totp; the backup path silently fails for the exact locked-out users it was built for.

[advisory] backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write: authorize decrypts the whole array, nulls one slot, and rewrites the full array with a plain prisma.user.update — no transaction, no optimistic concurrency — so concurrent sign-ins validate against the same pre-update snapshot. when two requests race (e.g., an attacker replaying a code observed on a printed sheet while the owner logs in), the second write overwrites the first's consumption and resurrects the already-used code, converting a single-use credential into a reusable one with no error logged anywhere.

[bug] req.body.backupcode is used as a string without validation: a json body sending a non-string (e.g. {"backupcode": 123}) passes the truthiness guard at line 48 and throws typeerror on .replaceall, which the handler does not catch. any non-browser client that sends a numeric or structured backupcode gets an unhandled 500 with a stack trace in the logs instead of the 400 incorrectbackupcode the endpoint's error contract defines, polluting error monitoring and breaking the documented api surface.

[bug] handleenable's success path replaces the onenable() call with setstep(setupstep.displaybackupcodes), leaving the modal's only success notification wired to the backup-codes close button, so dismissing the dialog at that step via escape, the header x, or a backdrop click (all routed to onopenchange/oncancel) completes the enable server-side without ever notifying the parent. the settings ui keeps showing 2fa as disabled while the account is actually protected; when the user next clicks the switch the setup endpoint re-runs and overwrites the stored backupcodes, silently invalidating the codes the user already saved, and the parent never runs its onenable side effects (state refresh/query invalidation).

[bug] the copy button fires navigator.clipboard.writetext without awaiting it and without any rejection handler, then unconditionally shows the 'backup codes copied!' success toast before the write can complete. when the clipboard write rejects (firefox without the clipboard-write permission, unfocused document) the user is told the codes were copied when they were not, and on non-https self-hosted deployments navigator.clipboard is undefined so the handler throws a typeerror and shows no feedback at all — in both cases the user closes the dialog believing the recovery codes are saved and is locked out when they later lose the authenticator.

[bug] the backup-code branch of the disable endpoint fails by unhandled throws — a raw error on a missing calendsoencryptionkey and an unguarded symmetricdecrypt/json.parse of user.backupcodes — instead of the res.status().json({error}) envelope every other branch of this handler returns. these failures surface as non-json next.js 500s; disabletwofactormodal unconditionally calls response.json() on non-200 responses, which throws into the generic catch, so the structured incorrectbackupcode/missingbackupcodes mapping is bypassed and the user only sees 'something went wrong' — and after a calendsoencryptionkey rotation on a self-hosted instance, every backup-code disable attempt returns an opaque html 500 instead of a parseable 4xx json error.

[bug] authorize() decrypts and json.parses user.backupcodes with no guard, so a failed decrypt (rotated calendsoencryptionkey since the codes were stored) or corrupted column throws a raw crypto/parse error instead of an errorcode. the raw error message propagates as res.error to login.tsx, matches no known error code, and renders as a generic 'something went wrong' — a user attempting backup-code login on a rotated-key instance gets an opaque, unactionable failure on every attempt with nothing distinguishing it in logs from a real auth failure.

[bug] backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read–decrypt–null–re-encrypt–write with no transaction or concurrency guard, so two concurrent sign-ins each read the full code array and last-write-wins resurrects a code the other request already consumed. a user signing in from two devices in quick succession (or a replaying holder of a shoulder-surfed code) double-spends a code the product's own instructions promise 'can be used exactly once', silently breaking the single-use invariant the feature states to users.

[bug] the missingbackupcodes message instructs 'please generate them in your settings', but no code path in this product can generate backup codes for an account with 2fa already enabled — codes are only written by the setup endpoint inside the enable flow — and a user receiving this error on the login page cannot reach settings without logging in first. the exact users this error targets — locked-out users without backup codes on the login screen, and disable-modal users sitting in settings — are directed to perform an action that is impossible from where they stand, leaving both audiences with dead-end recovery guidance that masks the absence of any recovery path.

[bug] when all ten codes have been consumed, the stored column is the json array [null×10] rather than null (consumption writes backupcodes[index] = null), so the !user.backupcodes guard never fires and further attempts throw incorrectbackupcode instead of missingbackupcodes. a user who exhausted their codes and lost their authenticator is told 'backup code is incorrect' on every attempt instead of learning that no codes remain, so they keep retrying dead codes instead of seeking account recovery.

stored xss: rss/atom feed content is imported and served completely unsanitized — pollfeed.rb feeds raw item html to topicembed.rb which sets cookmethod: rawhtml, post.rb's cook returns raw verbatim with no sanitize pipeline, and it is rendered via raw post.cooked in best.html.erb:23 and as cooked throughout the forum ui; anyone who publishes, compromises, or mitms the feed (fetched over plain open()) can execute arbitrary script on the discourse origin and steal viewer sessions.
the importremote readability path whitelists tags but not url schemes, so <a href='javascript:...'> survives sanitization as an additional live xss vector.

app/models/topicembed.rb:13 interpolates url unescaped into a single-quoted href after only a prefix check (url =~ /^https?\:\/\//); urls legally containing a single quote (e.g. slugs like /it's-alive.html) terminate the attribute early and corrupt the stored html, and a crafted feed link such as http://host/x' onmouseover='... performs attribute injection that lands as live markup since the post is rawhtml-cooked (second xss path).

topicembed.rb:31-34 update path assumes embed.post is non-nil when passing it to postrevisor.new; nothing removes topicembeds rows when a topic/post is destroyed, so an orphaned embed makes postrevisorinitialize nomethoderror mid-loop inside pollfeed's rss.items.each with retry: false — every feed item after the orphaned one is never imported every hour and the embed request for that url fails persistently, silently degrading the feed import.

lib/topicretriever.rb:26-29: $redis.setnx and $redis.expire are not atomic; if the process dies between them the retrieved:<url> key has no ttl and lives forever, permanently throttling that embed url so performretrieve never runs again and the page shows 'loading discussion...' indefinitely. use a single set ... ex 60 nx.

topicembed.rb:64-76 (absolutizeurls) mangles protocol-relative urls: //cdn.example.com/img.jpg passes startwith?('/') and then sub(/^\/+/, '') strips both leading slashes, producing http://<embed host>/cdn.example.com/img.jpg — a broken path on the wrong host, breaking images/links in imported posts.

app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17: the origin check is substring-based (discourseurl.indexof(e.origin) === -1) rather than exact equality, so any origin that is a substring-prefix of the forum url (e.g. http://fo matching http://forum.example.com) can post discourse-resize messages and drive the iframe height arbitrarily; the check should be e.origin === discourseurl.

embedcontroller.rb:9-16 / topicretriever.rb:15-18: embedurl is never validated as a string — params.require(:embedurl) happily returns an array/hash (?embedurl[]=x), and uri(@embedurl) in invalidhost? raises typeerror (not uri::invalidurierror) which escapes the rescue, so each such request enqueues a job that crashes on its first statement and burns through sidekiq retries — anonymous-triggerable job churn. validate it's a string before enqueueing.

embedcontroller.rb: the referer gate relies on the spoofable, fully client-controlled request.referer header, so it stops browsers but not scripted callers; any request with a faked referer and a novel embedurl enqueues retrievetopic, and with feedpollingenabled each such job synchronously re-polls and re-parses the entire feed (jobs::pollfeed.new.execute({})) plus a readability fetch — enabling anonymous queue-flooding / forced-feed-refresh amplification. a global rate limit on the controller is needed.

lib/tasks/disqus.thor:143: the importer rewrite from postcreator.new(..., createdat: date.parse(t[:createdat]), category: categoryid) to topicembed.importremote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title]) silently drops both timestamps and category support — imported disqus topics are dated 'now' (reordering listing pages and breaking embed dates), always land in uncategorized, and the -c cli option was removed; importremote should at least forward createdat.
there is no mutex between the scheduled and inline poll paths, and if the inline poll runs longer than the 60s throttle ttl, concurrent jobs re-enter and duplicate the work.

unbounded remote download into memory with no size/time policy: app/models/topicembed.rb:48 (open(url).read) and pollfeed.rb:29 buffer the full remote body into a string and parse it (readability + nokogiri, several times the document size in memory) with no max-size cap, bounded only by open-uri's default 60s timeouts; any large resource served on the embeddablehost will be fully downloaded and parsed in a sidekiq worker.

no enqueue-time dedupe and no negative caching on the retrieve path (app/controllers/embedcontroller.rb:15, app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:8-10, lib/topicretriever.rb:21-33): every embed impression enqueues a job, so a page whose topic can never be imported floods the sidekiq queue with near-duplicate jobs whose only work is a failed setnx; the 60s throttle only applies inside job execution and is set before retrieval regardless of outcome, so permanently failing urls (404, readability-empty, fetch error) are re-fetched up to once per minute indefinitely as long as they have viewers.
the redis setnx/expire throttle operations are non-atomic: a crash between them throttles that url forever.

force: true was added to the already-shipped migration db/migrate/20131223171005createtoptopics.rb:3 — inert day-to-day since normal deploys skip recorded migrations, but any db:migrate:redo or reset against an environment with data silently drops toptables... toptopics; reads like a local-dev convenience accidentally committed, and the same pattern in the brand-new createtopicembeds migration (20131217174004) sets a bad precedent.

external html from polled rss/atom feeds and readability extraction of arbitrary embeddable-host pages is stored and served completely unsanitized, causing stored xss in the discourse origin for every visitor of every embedding third-party page: the cookmethod == rawhtml early return in app/models/post.rb:133 bypasses the entire cooking/sanitization pipeline (sanitize), app/jobs/scheduled/pollfeed.rb:35-36 imports i.content raw with zero sanitization, and app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19 renders it via raw post.cooked

html attribute injection via unescaped url interpolation in app/models/topicembed.rb:13: url is interpolated into <a href='{url}'> without escaping, so a url like http://host/x' onmouseover='... (single quotes are legal uris and pass the http(s) url check) yields attribute injection

public cli signature break: the --category/-c option was removed from the disqus import task (lib/tasks/disqus.thor:117) and the category is no longer passed to postcreator (:144), so existing callers invoking disqus:import -c abort with an unknown-option error and imported topics all land in uncategorized; output also drifts to full readability-extracted html plus a topicembed row instead of a permalink stub, which can later collide with feed-polling imports keyed on the same url

ssrf via redirect: the host allowlist is checked only on the initial url (lib/topicretriever.rb:15), but the actual fetches via open-uri (app/models/topicembed.rb:36, app/jobs/scheduled/pollfeed.rb:29) follow cross-origin redirects, so an open redirect on the embeddable host can pivot the discourse server to fetch internal endpoints (169.254.169.254, localhost services) whose content is then readable via the public topic/embed; the referer gate is a forgeable header, so no on-host presence is even needed to trigger retrieval
no fetch timeout or size cap is set on the open() fetches, so retrieval/poll jobs can be hung or oom'd

pollfeed crashes on common rss 2.0 feeds: i.content.scrub at app/jobs/scheduled/pollfeed.rb:35 raises nomethoderror because simplerss exposes rss 2.0's content:encoded as contentencoded and plain rss items have no content; with sidekiqoptions retry: false (:12) the hourly import dies mid-feed and items after the crash point are never imported, silently breaking the documented rss/atom support for the most common feeds (wordpress et al.); stringscrub also requires ruby >= 2.1

absolutizeurls corrupts protocol-relative urls: the href.startwith?('/') check at app/models/topicembed.rb:61-72 treats //cdn.example.com/img.png as a root-relative path and, after stripping leading slashes, produces http://<embeddable-host>/cdn.example.com/img.png, breaking links and images in every feed containing // urls

<%- end if %> in app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 is not a block terminator — it either fails to compile (template syntaxerror making every successful /embed/best render a 500) or parses as a bizarre modifier-if whose condition is the next emitted erb output, making the header block depend on unrelated template code; it should be <%- end -%>, and since the controller specs stub topicview and never render views, the breakage would ship undetected

embed url matching is a byte-exact string contract across three independently produced values — the stored embedurl (app/models/topicembed.rb:78-80), the client snippet's discourseembedurl (app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:7), and the feed's i.link (app/jobs/scheduled/pollfeed.rb:32) — with no normalization layer anywhere, so any divergence (trailing slash, scheme, www, query params) means the embed never matches and the user sees the loading page reloading every 30s indefinitely while the server re-enqueues retrievals

the retrievetopic job is enqueued before any validation of user input (app/controllers/embedcontroller.rb:15) — the host allowlist runs only later inside the job (lib/topicretriever.rb:15) and the referer gate is a forgeable header, so an anonymous client with a forged referer: http://<embeddable-host>/ can enqueue unbounded jobs (varying embedurl to bypass the per-url throttle), and each first-time retrieval synchronously re-runs the entire feed import inline

the embeddablehost setting is silently config-sensitive: it must be a bare host string — an admin entering https://example.com or a host with a port never string-matches uri(...).host, and the feature fails silently with no validation or documentation of the expected format

already-shipped migration edited and given force: true: createtable :toptopics, force: true in db/migrate/20131223171005createtoptopics.rb:3 drops the table if it exists when the migration runs, violating released-migration immutability and risking silent data loss in environments where the table exists without the schemamigrations entry (partial states, restored dumps)

pollfeed's rss.items.each loop has no begin/rescue around topicembed.import, so a single bad feed item (nil field, bad url, postcreator failure, recordnotunique race) permanently poisons all feed importing — the job aborts, and with retry: false and hourly scheduling the next run dies on the same item, so later items are never imported; the unused feedkey also leaves no way to skip or flag a bad feed.

topicretrieverperformretrieve runs the entire feed poll inline in every retrieve job with no lock: jobs::pollfeed.new.execute({}) fetches and imports the whole feed synchronously once per unique embedurl per 60s, effectively ddos-ing the embeddable host, racing the check-then-insert in topicembed.import into activerecord::recordnotunique exceptions, and failing retrieve jobs on any pollfeed failure.

external feed content is stored and served as unsanitized raw html: the rss path has no sanitization at all before content becomes cooked, the readability path whitelists tags but permits javascript: urls in href/src attributes, and the feed-supplied url is interpolated unescaped into html — a malicious or hijacked feed yields stored script running on the discourse origin.

outbound http calls (open(sitesetting.feedpollingurl) and open(url).read) have no explicit opentimeout/readtimeout, no redirect policy, and no response-size cap, so a slow feed server ties up sidekiq workers and a huge response is slurped wholesale into memory before being persisted with no post-length bound.

/embed/best enqueues a retrievetopic background job on every request with no rate limiting — the referer host check in ensureembeddable is a client-controlled, trivially spoofed header, so varying the embedurl param generates unbounded queue growth; the 60s redis throttle limits fetch frequency, not enqueue volume.

no lifecycle cleanup for topicembeds: nothing deletes a topicembed when its topic or post is deleted, leaving a stale topicid that makes topicview.new 404, permanently blocking re-creation for that url because performretrieve short-circuits on the existing embed, and causing a nomethoderror when postrevisor.new(post) receives a nil post.

the embed loading page reloads forever with no failure state or retry cap, and failure is silent on both client and operator side: retrieval silently no-ops when embedbyusername is unset or the user was deleted, when the host doesn't match, or when retrieval fails, and no poll/retrieve path logs anything — with no circuit breaker, a permanently-bad embed url is re-fetched once a minute indefinitely.

feed item parsing assumes i.content exists, but simple-rss exposes namespaced content:encoded as contentencoded, so rss 2.0 description-only feeds raise nomethoderror on i.content.scrub, and combined with the missing error isolation one such item kills the entire poll.

the setnx/expire throttle in topicretriever is not atomic: if the worker dies between the two calls, the retrieved:<url> key persists with no ttl and that url is throttled permanently until manual redis intervention; should use set(key, "1", nx: true, ex: 60).

importremote fetches the url before validating its scheme: open(url) executes before the ^https?:// check in import, so a schemeless string like //eviltrout.com/x passes invalidhost? and hits kernelopen's local-file semantics instead of http.

<%- end if %> in app/views/embed/best.html.erb is a typo (presumably meant <%- end %>) that only renders correctly by accident of erb's chunk emission order, and is one template edit away from a semantics change or a syntaxerror that breaks every embed render with a topic present.

createtable ..., force: true in production migrations (createtopicembeds, createtoptopics) can silently drop any pre-existing table without warning if the migration is re-run, and modifying the already-shipped createtoptopics migration is a no-op on already-migrated databases that only adds risk.

the disqus import loop now performs network i/o with no rescue: topicembed.importremote(user, t[:link], ...) inside parser.threads.each means a single 404 or timeout on an old export permalink aborts the entire cli run partway through.

jobs::pollfeed's core feed-to-topic pipeline has zero behavioral coverage: the spec stubs pollfeed itself, so simplerss parsing, the link fallback, cgi.unescapehtml(i.content.scrub), the missing-user early return, and the handoff to topicembed.import are never executed, and no test anywhere verifies a feed item produces a topic/post. this untested path hides a latent crash: i.content.scrub (pollfeed.rb:35) raises nomethoderror on feeds/items lacking a content element (common in plain rss 2.0 feeds with only <description>), and since the job is sidekiqoptions retry: false, it dies silently every hour.

imported html is served completely unsanitized: postcook returns raw verbatim for cookmethod: rawhtml, bypassing the cooking/sanitization pipeline and the plugin::filter :afterpostcook hooks. pollfeed passes raw feed html straight into this path (only the readability path whitelists tags), and the embed view renders it with raw post.cooked (and it renders unsanitized on the regular topic page too) — a crafted feed/article containing <script> or onerror= executes in the discourse origin for every viewer, including logged-in users. the spec (topicembedspec.rb:29 asserting cooked == raw) codifies the vulnerability instead of guarding against it.

the embed controller's success-path tests verify mock interactions, not behavior: 'tells the topic retriever to work' asserts topicretriever.new/retrieve are called instead of asserting jobs.enqueue(:retrievetopic, ...) args, and topicretriever.expects(:new) matches any arguments; 'creates a topic view' mocks topicview.new returning nil. with view rendering off, nothing verifies the best template renders posts or that the loading template renders on the no-embed path — a broken template (e.g. @topicview.posts on a stale/deleted topic id) ships green. no renderviews/integration spec exists for either new template.

absolutizeurls edge cases are untested, including a real mangling of protocol-relative urls: //cdn.example.com/x starts with /, gets all leading slashes stripped by sub(/^\/+/, ''), and is rewritten to http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/x — a common real-world pattern that silently produces broken links. port-bearing urls (prefix << ":{uri.port}") are also uncovered.

[bug] for collective events where neither eventtype.destinationcalendar nor organizeruser.destinationcalendar exists, evt.destinationcalendar is set to null, so evt.destinationcalendar?.push(...teamdestinationcalendars) is skipped and the team members' destination calendars already collected in teamdestinationcalendars are silently discarded. the pr's core scenario — creating the event on every collective host's chosen calendar — no-ops whenever the organizer has no destination calendar: member events fall back to credential defaults instead of their selected calendars, with no error or log to indicate the drop.

[bug] in updateevent the fallback branch evaluates find((cal) => cal.externalid === externalcalendarid) with a falsy externalcalendarid, comparing every calendar's externalid against undefined/null so it always returns undefined, making the previous event.destinationcalendar?.externalid fallback dead code. for booking references without externalcalendarid (legacy references and the no-credentialid destination path), calendar.events.update is called with calendarid undefined and the remote event is never updated on reschedule, leaving stale event times on calendars.

[bug] deleteevent has the same dead fallback: with a falsy externalcalendarid, find((cal) => cal.externalid === externalcalendarid) can never match a destinationcalendar row (externalid is a required column), so calendarid resolves to undefined instead of the destination calendar's externalid. cancellations of bookings whose reference lacks externalcalendarid (e.g., old references created before externalcalendarid was persisted) now delete from 'primary' and 404 instead of deleting from the calendar the event lives on, leaving ghost calendar events behind.

[bug] createevent selects the target calendar solely via find((cal) => cal.credentialid === credentialid), which can never match when the destination has no credentialid (the eventmanager else-branch passes credentials whose ids differ from the null destination.credentialid), so selectedcalendar is undefined and the event is inserted into 'primary'. for destinationcalendar rows with null credentialid, events land on the user's primary calendar instead of the chosen destination calendar (pre-diff code inserted into destinationcalendar.externalid), while the stored reference still points at the destination's externalid, so later updates/deletes target a calendar that never held the event.

[bug] the newbookingid merge path still deletes only the first old calendar reference via booking.references.find(...), left unchanged while this pr makes collective bookings carry one calendar reference per host. rescheduling or merging a collective booking deletes the old calendar event of the first host only, leaving orphaned calendar events on the remaining hosts' calendars.

[advisory] per-destination targeting is implemented only in googlecalendarservice; basecalendarservice (apple/caldav and its subclasses), lark and office365 still resolve the target from destinationcalendar[0] and ignore the per-destination credentialid/externalid that the new createallcalendarevents loop passes. for collective multi-host bookings on non-google providers, iterations beyond the first host request destination[0]'s calendar with a different host's credentials — caldav's filter matches none of its calendars (silent no-op) and lark/o365 get an api error that calendarmanager swallows — so the other hosts' calendar events are silently never created.

[advisory] the reference builder changed non-calendar results from credentialid: result.credentialid to credentialid: undefined, so video booking references stop persisting the id of the credential that created the meeting. booking references for video apps lose the credential linkage they have carried until now; consumers that match booking references by credentialid (e.g., credential-removal cleanup flows) silently stop finding video bookings created after this change.

[advisory] the recurring-cancellation sweep, which deletes every remaining booking's event across all calendar credentials, now runs once per calendar reference inside the new for-loop instead of once per booking. cancelling all remaining bookings of a recurring collective booking with n calendar references fires the identical deletion sweep n times, doubling calendar api calls and logging errors for the duplicate (already-deleted) events.

[bug] the google meet fallback dereferences mainhostdestinationcalendar.integration without a guard, so evt.destinationcalendar being null or an empty array throws typeerror, where the replaced optional-chained check gracefully fell back to cal video. any booking scheduled with location integrations:google:meet and no destination calendar crashes with typeerror: the stripe/paypal success webhooks now build destinationcalendar: [] for organizers without a calendar (webhook.ts:229) and then call eventmanager.create, so the payment is captured but the booking is never scheduled and the webhook returns 500.

[bug] only evt.destinationcalendar[0] is connected to the booking (the booking.destinationcalendar relation stays one-to-one), so the collected team destination calendars exist only in the in-memory evt and are lost on persistence. flows that rebuild evt from the booking afterwards — booking confirmation (confirm.handler.ts:175) and payment success (webhook.ts:229, paypal-webhook.ts:152) — construct destinationcalendar with only the main host's calendar, so paid or confirmation-gated collective bookings get their calendar event created only in the main host's calendar and the other hosts' calendars never receive the event.

[bug] updateevent's fallback find((cal) => cal.externalid === externalcalendarid) executes only when externalcalendarid is already falsy and then compares externalid against that same falsy value, so it can never match and always yields undefined. for booking references without externalcalendarid (produced by the credentialid-less destination path, which now persists externalcalendarid: result.externalid = undefined), rescheduling passes calendarid undefined to calendar.events.update and the update fails, where the previous code fell back to the booking's destination calendar.

[bug] deleteevent has the same dead fallback: find((cal) => cal.externalid === externalcalendarid) runs only when externalcalendarid is falsy and compares against that falsy value, so it never matches and the intended destination-calendar fallback is unreachable. cancellation of a booking whose reference lacks externalcalendarid resolves calendarid to undefined (falling back to 'primary') instead of the calendar the event was created in, leaving the original calendar event orphaned and its slot busy.

topicscontroller.rb:98-116: the first unsubscribe click only moves tracking/watching users to regular, which does not stop direct reply/mention notifications, contradicting the email copy that says "to stop receiving notifications about this particular topic".

topicscontroller.rb:98-116: the state-changing mutation runs on a plain get with no nonce/token validation, so it is csrf-able — an on an external page silently flips notification levels for any logged-in user who views it, and corporate mail scanners/av that prefetch links trigger the mutation without a click.

config/locales/server.en.yml:1852-1856 + lib/email/messagebuilder.rb:~63-70: the shared unsubscribelink locale now hard-requires the %{unsubscribeurl} interpolation key — any mailer or plugin building an email with addunsubscribelink: true that doesn't pass unsubscribeurl raises i18n::missinginterpolationargument inside the email-delivery background job, which fails and retries while the message is never delivered. safer: default unsubscribeurl (e.g. fall back to the preferences url) when absent.

topicscontroller.rb:107-113: the notification-level write goes through tu.save! instead of topicuser.change, so no notificationlevelchange messagebus event is published on /topic/<id> — the user's other open sessions of the topic keep showing the stale notification level until refresh.

routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6 + templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs:2-4: when the unsubscribe url is reached via in-app client-side routing (e.g. link pasted in a post/chat and clicked in-app), the ember route loads the topic via topicsshow, which performs no mutation — yet the page copy asserts "you will stop receiving notifications for…", claiming an unsubscribe that never happened.

unsubscribing from a watching topic only drops the user to regular, where they still receive reply/mention notifications, contradicting the email's 'stop receiving notifications about this particular topic' promise — no spec enumerating the four starting levels forces this semantic decision to be explicit.

anonymous visitors trigger a 500 on the unsubscribe endpoint: unsubscribe is a public get with no login requirement, so currentuser is nil and currentuser.id (app/controllers/topicscontroller.rb:106-108) raises nomethoderror; unsubscribe urls embedded in emails mean bots and email-scanner prefetching will hit this constantly, and no test covers logged-out requests.

logged-in users with no topicuser record (e.g., manually visiting the unsubscribe url for a topic they never interacted with) trigger a 500 because tu.notificationlevel is called on nil; no test exercises the no-topicuser-record case.

the unsubscribelink locale now hard-requires %{unsubscribeurl} (i18n raises missinginterpolationargument if absent), so any other email path (digest mailer, plugins, future callers) setting addunsubscribelink: true without the new opt crashes at build time instead of sending; no test exercises htmlpart with addunsubscribelink: true without unsubscribeurl, or proves the remaining callers still build.

the topicunsubscribe route is registered after the topic resource, whose nested dynamic-segment routes (fromparamsnear at /:nearpost and its sibling post-number route) already match /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe — ember matches in definition order, so the unsubscribe page may be shadowed and never render (users land on the topic route with nearpost: 'unsubscribe'); no routing/acceptance test asserts /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe resolves to topicunsubscribe.

unguarded topicuser.findby in the new unsubscribe action (app/controllers/topicscontroller.rb:105-107): it returns nil when no topicuser row exists and the code immediately dereferences tu.notificationlevel, causing a nomethoderror/hard 500 on a link included in every notification email (reachable via shared-machine logins as a different account, or mention/reply recipients with no row).

second crash path in the same action: notificationlevel is nullable — topicuser.trackvisit! creates rows without a level and the tracking scope's coalesce confirms nulls are expected — so tu.notificationlevel > topicuser.notificationlevels[:regular] becomes nil > 1 and raises nomethoderror even when the row exists.

state-changing get request (config/routes.rb:439-441 + topicscontroller.rb:98): the unsubscribe toggle runs on get, which rails' csrf protection never checks, enabling cross-site csrf via , silent unsubscribes from email-scanner/webmail link prefetch, and non-idempotent reload that re-runs the toggle (regular → muted, suppressing even mentions) with no visible action; a post or tokenized confirm step is the standard shape for emailed unsubscribe actions.

domain logic duplicated in the controller (topicscontroller.rb:106-113): the if/else level-toggle semantics belong in the model via the existing topicuser.change, which creates the row when missing (preventing the nil crash) and publishes the messagebus /topic/{id} notificationlevelchange event — the inline version loses that event (other open tabs show a stale notification level) and leaves two divergent implementations to keep in sync.

topicuser.findby can return nil in the unsubscribe action when a different logged-in account clicks the per-topic link (shared machine, forwarded email) and has no topicuser row, causing nomethoderror on nil and a 500 error instead of a graceful message — no nil guard and no spec covers the unsubscribe action

unsubscribe url has no user binding (unsubscribeurl is identical for every recipient), so the notification-level change is applied to whoever is logged in — a user logged in as account b clicking a link from account a's email silently mutes/downgrades b's own topic state while a's subscription is untouched, and the success page falsely confirms the mutation hit the right target

state-changing get routes (t/:slug/:topicid/unsubscribe and t/:topicid/unsubscribe) mutate topicuser.notificationlevel with no csrf protection, token, confirmation, or origin check — a third-party page can embed to silently walk every logged-in visitor's topics down watching → regular → muted, inconsistent with discourse's convention of using put for other notification-state mutations (star, mute, unmute, togglenotifications)

unsubscribelink i18n string now hard-requires %{unsubscribeurl} and htmlpart cooks it unconditionally when addunsubscribelink is set, so any email setting addunsubscribelink: true without passing unsubscribeurl raises missinginterpolationargument during build and never gets delivered — only sendnotificationemail was updated, leaving other in-repo callers (e.g. digest emails) or plugin emails using email::messagebuilder to hard-fail

direct tu.save! in the unsubscribe action bypasses topicuser.change, skipping the messagebus publish that updates watcher/tracking ui in already-open topic tabs, and any future side-effects added to change (autos, callbacks, publishes) will silently not run on this path

confirmation text overpromises: the page unconditionally declares 'you will stop receiving notifications' but tracking/watching users land on regular and still receive direct-reply and @mention emails, with no indication of the actual resulting state or that clicking again would mute entirely (one-way ratchet: watching → regular → muted)
